Nec tamen tam horribile peccatum dissignauisse contenti sunt: sed ulterius progressi, sanguine innoxio manus polluunt, cum nec ea ignorare possent, quæ de iniustis homicidis in lege habentur. Num. 35. Adeo verum est, quod Solomon impios, cum in profundum delapsi sunt, nullam rerum rationem habere dicit. Proverb. 18. Horreamus ergo peccatorum blanda initia, ne dum hæc verbi diuini odium nobis instillant, tenaci illorum luto detenti, tandem immani impietatis barathro toti absorbeamur.
units.tr: It is worth particular notice that while they rage with the most unjust violence, they can still keep up the appearance of law. For since they accused him of blasphemy and false teaching, they exact from him that punishment which God had appointed for blasphemers and seducers (Lev. 24; Deut. 12 and 17). And the witnesses, just as the law described, cast the first stones; to do this more readily they lay aside their garments, which they entrust to Saul (who was later converted to Christ and received the name Paul) to guard. So with regard to the form of law you could desire nothing more. And Stephen may seem to have paid his penalty according to right and the laws. But what keeps the form of law is not always done lawfully, and unless we wish to give serious offence, the causes of such punishments must be examined more closely. Meanwhile observe how much God sometimes allows the impious, whose rage he wills to be exercised, and whom he wills to fill up the measure of their impiety. And from the example of the witnesses we are taught how far impiety may finally advance, unless we take care to resist its beginnings. They sinned by false witness, although they could not be ignorant of God's law or of the penalty appointed for false witnesses. Nor did it deter them that Solomon declares a false witness to be hateful and abominable to God (Prov. 6). Yet they were not content to commit so horrible a sin; they went further and polluted their hands with innocent blood, although they could not be ignorant of what the law says about unjust murderers (Num. 35). So true is it that, when the impious have fallen into the depths, Solomon says they take no account of anything (Prov. 18). Let us therefore shrink from the enticing beginnings of sin, lest, while this sins sow in us a hatred of God's Word, we become held fast in their sticky mire and at last be wholly swallowed up in the monstrous abyss of impiety.

units.la: QVÆ de Saulo dicuntur, qui in sanctissimi viri necem consensisse & haud vulgarem ex ea voluptatem hausse dicitur, sequentis historiæ parafceuem habent, & ad Dei gratiam illustrandam faci‐unt. Sed plura de his suo loco dicentur.
units.tr: WHAT is said of Saul, that he consented to the death of this most holy man and is said to have drawn no small pleasure from it, serves as a preface to the following history and helps to illustrate the grace of God. But more will be said about these matters in their proper place.

units.la: Restat, vt qualem Stephanus, cùm tam atroci supplicio multaretur, sese gesserit, consyderemus: ‹vbi tria de illo dicuntur.› Primò dominum inuocauit, quod illum indesinenter fecisse credimus. Et ex primitur orationis summa: Domine Iesu, suscipe spiritum meum. Habet hæc & veræ fidei confessio‐nem, & ingentis inuictæ spei argumentum. Nam mortis terroribus vndiq; oppugnatus, Christum adhuc saluatorem agnoscit & fatetur, latronis cum Christo crucifixi exemplum imitatus. Adhuc animas nè in morte quidem interire, sed in vitæ melioris conditionem transfire credit, imò nouit in ipsa morte vitam per fidem in Christum inueniri. Est hæc ingens fidei laus, quòd tunc quoq; inuicta mamet, & animorum solatium affert, quando omnia alia fallunt. Simul vero docet Stephani exemplum, cui animas iam moriturì commendemus. Non vtiq; diuis, vt superstitiosi solent. Sed Christo domino, qui vt illas sanguinis sui pretio redemit: ita resurrectione sua mortem vicit, & ascensione in cælos subuectus, ibi locum nobis præparauit, in quo ad ipsum colligamur. Ioh. 14. Secundò charitatis spe‐cimen edit Stephanus, quæ à fide separari nequit. Nam Christi præceptum & exemplū imitatus, pro hostibus suis orat, nè peccati huius dignas pœnas ab illis exigat Deus. Arguit hoc hostium iniquita‐tem, qui vt salutis publicæ hostem occiduntt, qui vltimo voto testatur, non alium publicæ omnium in‐columitatis studiosiorem fuisse. Sed est hæc piorum sors in hoc mundo, qui potissimam suæ infelicitatis causam habet, quòd nec benefactores agnoscere, nec publicæ salutis nocentissimos hostes cauere potest. Discamus autem, vel ingratis digna charitatis officia exhibere, & eorum salutem, qui summa in nos iniquitate peccant, pijs precibus Deo commendare. Matth. 5. Nec nos hominum impietate abster‐reri patiamur: quando nobis ignota sunt Dei iudicia, nec facilè cuiuis reuelat dominus, qui nã inter homines incurabiles sunt, vt olim Ieremiæ fecisse legitur. Ierem. 7. 14. 15. Excitemur etiam huius pre‐cationis euentu, quam vel vnius Sauli conuersio non infrugiferam fuisse, docere potest.
units.tr: It remains for us to consider what manner of man Stephen showed himself to be when he was punished with so cruel a torment. Three things are said of him there. First, he called upon the Lord, as we believe he did continually. And the substance of his prayer is set out: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit." This contains both a confession of true faith and a proof of a great and unconquered hope. For though assailed on every side by the terrors of death, he still acknowledges and confesses Christ as Saviour, imitating the example of the thief crucified with Christ. He still believes that souls do not perish even in death, but pass into a better condition of life; indeed he knows that in death itself life is found through faith in Christ. This is a great praise of faith, that it remains unconquered even then, and brings comfort to souls when all other things fail. At the same time, Stephen's example teaches us to whom we should commend our souls when we are about to die: not, of course, to the saints, as the superstitious are wont to do, but to the Lord Christ, who redeemed them by the price of his blood, conquered death by his resurrection, and, carried up into heaven by his ascension, prepared a place for us there, where we are gathered to himself (John 14). Second, Stephen gives a proof of charity, which cannot be separated from faith. For imitating Christ's precept and example, he prays for his enemies, that God may not exact from them the punishment deserved by such a sin. This shows the wickedness of the enemies, who kill him as an enemy of the public safety, when he bears witness in his last prayer that no one was more eager for the public well-being of all. But this is the lot of the godly in this world: their chief unhappiness is that they can neither recognise their benefactors nor guard against the most harmful enemies of public safety. Let us learn, then, both to show due acts of charity even to the ungrateful, and to commend to God by pious prayers the salvation of those who sin against us with the greatest injustice (Matt. 5). Nor let us allow ourselves to be deterred by the wickedness of men, since the judgements of God are unknown to us, and the Lord does not easily reveal them to anyone; for there are incurable men among them, as is read was once the case with Jeremiah (Jer. 7; 14; 15). Let us also be stirred up by the outcome of this prayer, which the conversion of Saul alone can show was not unfruitful.

units.la: Vltimò, Stephanus his dictis obdormiuisse dicitur, quem hostes iam cum sua doctrina extinctum esse sperabant. Frequenter autem dormiendi vocabulo scriptura vtitur, de piorum morte loquens. Ita enim mortis conditio exprimitur. Est hæc hominis, ex anima & corpore constantis, resolutio. In hac vero anima nec extinguitur, nec obdormit, sed transit in vitam æternam, sicuti Christus Ioh. 5. ad monet. Vnde non ineptè mors transitus in cælos dici consueuit. Corpus vero obdormire dicitur, quia terræ mandatum quasi ad somnum componitur, è quo nouissimo die per Christum excitabitur, vt ipsum quoq; cælestis vitæ gaudia percipiat. Extant passim de his scripturæ testimonia, & crebrò hac tractandi occasio incidit: quare nunc breuitati studemus. Stephanum vero nobis imitandum propo‐mus, vt è vita migraturi, animabus ad beatorum sedes transmissis, & tandem corporibus quoq; gloria se excitatis, regni cœlorum hæreditate fruamur per Christum Iesum dominum nostrum: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Lastly, Stephen is said to have fallen asleep with these words, he whom his enemies hoped was now extinguished along with his teaching. Now Scripture frequently uses the word "sleep" when it speaks of the death of the godly. For in this way the condition of death is expressed. It is the dissolution of a man, who consists of soul and body. In this dissolution the soul is neither extinguished nor falls asleep, but passes into eternal life, as Christ reminds us (John 5). Hence it is not inappropriately customary to call death a passage into heaven. But the body is said to fall asleep, because it is committed to the earth and laid down as if for sleep, from which it will be raised on the last day by Christ, so that it too may receive the joys of heavenly life. Testimonies of Scripture on these matters are found everywhere, and the occasion to treat them often arises; therefore now we aim at brevity. Let us propose Stephen to ourselves for imitation, so that when we depart from this life, our souls having been sent to the seats of the blessed, and our bodies at last also raised up to glory, we may enjoy the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven through Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: CAPUT VIII. HOMILIA LVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII. HOMILY LVI.

units.la: FActa est autem illo die persecutio magna aduersus ecclesiā, quæ erat Hierosolymis: & omnes dispersi sunt per regiones Iudææ & Samariæ, præterApostolos. Curauerunt autem vnà Stephanum viri religiosi, fecerunt‰ plactum magnum super eum. Saulus verò vastabat ecclesiā, singulas domus inuadens, trahensq; viros & mulieres, tradebat in custo‐diam. Illi autem dispersi peragrabant annunciantes verbum Dei.
units.tr: On that day a great persecution arose against the Church which was at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him. But Saul was ravaging the Church, entering every house and dragging off men and women, and he handed them over to prison. Those who had been scattered went about preaching the word of God.

units.la: Dui Stephani indignam necem magna diligentia per Lucam spiritus sanctus describi voluit, non quidem propter ipsum Stephanum modò, vt illius nomen iuxta Dauidis oracu‐lum æternæ memoriæ consecraretur, verumetiam propter nos, quorum institutioni & con‐solationi historia illa vehementer seruit. Docemur enim sanctissimi viri primiq; martyris exemplo, ut nos quoque extrema quaeque pro Christo & veritate obire, nec mortis quantumuis dirae periculum subterfugere debeamus, quando Christum vindicem habemus, qui amplissimam nobis mercedem in coelis reposuit. Rursum magnae consolationis plenum est, quod Christi regnum sanctorum caedibus & impiorum tyrannide non euerti, sed potius propagari videmus. Hoc enim ut saepe alias exemplis declaratum est, ita hoc etiam tempore, quo Stephanus martyrij coronam meruit, factum esse, sequens historia abunde docet: ad cuius expositionem praesenti loco commodè trafitu facit Lucas, & tria praemittit, quibus quod modo diximus comprobatur: quae singula ordine tractabimus.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit wished the unworthy death of Stephen to be described by Luke with great care. He did this not only for Stephen himself, so that his name might be consecrated to eternal memory according to the oracle of David, but also for our sake, since that history serves greatly for our instruction and comfort. For we are taught by the example of this most holy man and first martyr that we too ought to face the utmost dangers for Christ and the truth, and not shun the risk of death, however dreadful it may be, since we have Christ as our avenger, who has laid up for us a most ample reward in heaven. Again, it is full of great comfort that we see the kingdom of Christ not overthrown by the slaughter of the saints and the tyranny of the wicked, but rather spread abroad. For this, as has often been shown by other examples, so also at this time, when Stephen won the crown of martyrdom, has come to pass, as the following history abundantly teaches. For the explanation of this, Luke rightly makes a transition at this point, and sets out three things by which what we have just said is confirmed. We shall treat each of them in order.

units.la: Primo vniuersalis & saeua persecutio Hierosolymis aduersus ecclesiam excitata fuisse dicitur. Antea quidem multa à sacerdotibus tentata fuisse vidimus: sed apostoli potissimum petiti sunt, & vulgi metu repulsi hostes, minus feruidi fuere. Nunc verò vbi aduersus Stephanum rem sibi ex animi sententia succesisse, nec aliquem in populo motum oborium fuisse vident, belluarum instar, quasi gustato sanguine nouam rabiem concipiunt, truculentiores & audaciores facti, totum ecclesiae corpus aggredi & oppugnare instituunt. Qua in re tanto furore feruntur, ut breui ecclesia tota dissipetur, & in omnia tum Iudaeae tum Samariae loca dispergantur, qui hucusque Hierosolymis cohabitarant. Prodest verò hanc primitiuae ecclesiae faciem non oscitanter inspicere. In hac enim singula secundum Christi regulam rectissimè instituta fuisse vidimus. Et saepe illustrem retulerunt victoriam apostoli, quando vel capti vel in Concilijs causam dicere coacti sunt. Vnde quis summam rerum tranquillitatem pacemque stabilem facilè sperare potuisset. Sed ecce, horribiles turbae quasi momento temporis exurgunt, & vnius Stephani morte animati hostes, tam immani audacia aduersus totam ecclesiam bellum suscipiunt. Quid ergo nobis hodie sperandum est, quorum ignauia & multiplices defectus seueriorem castigationem meretur? Si enim haec in viridi fieri permisit Deus, quid fiet in arido? Simul verò illorum praepositera iudicia locus hic arguit, qui ex temporarijs rerum successibus de fide fideique doctrina pronuntiare solent. Si enim hos audire velis, sacerdotum causam iustissimam fuisse, ecclesiam verò primitiuam toto coelo errauisse fateberis. Sed altius scrutari conuenit iudiciorum Dei causas, & videbis e salute nostra esse, ut impiorum furoribus exerceamur, qui interim iniquitatis mensuram implent, & Christo ecclesiae vindici dignas suae tyrannidis poenas tandem exoluunt.
units.tr: First, it is said that a universal and savage persecution was stirred up at Jerusalem against the Church. Indeed, we have seen that many attempts had been made before by the priests, but they were aimed chiefly at the apostles, and the enemies, held back by fear of the crowd, were less fierce. But now, when they see that the business has gone to their liking against Stephen, and that no tumult has arisen among the people, they conceive a new rage, like beasts that have tasted blood. Becoming more savage and bolder, they set about attacking and assaulting the whole body of the Church. They are carried on in such fury that presently the whole Church is scattered, and those who had until then lived at Jerusalem are dispersed into all the regions of Judea and Samaria. It is worth looking closely at this aspect of the primitive Church. For we see that in it everything was most rightly arranged according to the rule of Christ. And often the apostles won a notable victory, whether when they were arrested or when they were compelled to plead their cause before councils. From this one might easily have hoped for complete calm and lasting peace. But look, dreadful crowds rise up in a moment of time, and the enemies, encouraged by the death of Stephan alone, take up war against the whole Church with such monstrous boldness. What then can we hope for today, whose sloth and manifold failings deserve a more severe chastisement? For if God allowed this to happen in the green wood, what will happen in the dry? At the same time, this passage exposes the perverse judgements of those who are wont to pronounce on faith and the doctrine of faith from the temporary outcomes of affairs. For if you were to listen to them, you would have to admit that the cause of the priests was most just and that the primitive Church had gone wrong entirely. But it is fitting to search more deeply into the causes of God's judgements, and you will see that it is for our salvation that we are exercised by the rages of the wicked, who in the meantime fill up the measure of their iniquity, and at last pay the penalties due to their tyranny, while Christ is the avenger of his Church.

units.la: Caeterum hoc loco cumprimis obseruandum est, quod reliquis fere omnibus fuga dilapsis, apostoli in vrbe mansisse dicuntur. Atqui illos antea praecipuè infestatos fuisse audiuimus. Quare illos in communi hac tempestate diuino auxilio miraculose seruatos fuisse oportet. Voluit enim Deus in cruenta Hierosolymorum vrbe euangelium diutissimè praedicari, ut euidentius eluceret ipsius tum misericordia tum iustitia. Misericordia quidem & bonitas, quod filij sui sanguine madentibus gratiae & salutis doctrinam tam diu praedicari passus est. Iustitia verò, quod incurabiles & poenitere nescios horribili excidio deleuit. Interim duo nobis obseruanda veniunt. Primum, impijs verbi & ecclesiae persecutoribus certos limites praescriptos esse, quos ipsis transgredi non licet. Qui enim mari terminum posuit, intra quem vasta illa aquarum moles se continet, & qui satanam legibus astringit, idem impios frenat, ne pro sua libidine quiduis possint, aut in quosus temere grassentur. In hoc autem eximia habetur animorum consolatio, quando impiorum furoribus diuinae prouidentiae leges nequaquam perrumpi posse cogitamus. Deinde apostoli exemplum fidelium verbi & ecclesiae antistitum nobis exhibent. Quamuis enim à Christo dictum esse scirent: Quando vos persequuntur in ciuitate aliqua, fugite in aliam: quia tamen certa vocatione astringebantur, & omnes ecclesiae reliquias corruituras videbant, si ipsi quoq; vrbe discederent, extremum potius vitae periculum subire malunt, quàm ecclesiam turpi fuga deserere. Et sanè diligenti cautione in hac causa ministris opus est. Vt enim non temere damnari debent quotquot fuga sibi consulunt: ita nequaquam putemus, id omnibus quouis loco aut tempore licere. Quod si ea sit rerum conditio, ut vel solus minister petatur ab hostium tyrannide, vel ipse deseratur ab ijs qui hactenus ecclesiae titulum sibi ipsi vendicarunt, aut certè nulla ex ipsius discessu sequatur ecclesiae ruina siue dissipatio: nihil obstat, quo minus melioribus temporibus sese referuet. At qui publicam ecclesiae causam deserunt, & ab ecclesijs fidei confessionem firmiter retinentibus discedunt, atque suo discessu lupis ecclesias dissipandi potestatem faciunt: hi reuera desertores sunt & mercenarij, quos Christus ad lupi conspectum fugere dicit. Iohan. 10. Vtinam verò haec diligentius expendissent, qui hodie ecclesias nimis festinanter deseruerunt: quos Ambrosij potius exemplum imitari oportebat, qui vel inuito Imperatore basilicas Arianus negare ausus est. Vide epistolam ad Marcellam sororem, quae trigesima tertia numeratur.
units.tr: Moreover, the thing to be noted especially here is that, when almost all the rest had fled away, the apostles are said to have remained in the city. Yet we have heard that they had been especially harassed before. Therefore they must have been miraculously preserved by divine help in this common storm. For God willed that the gospel be preached for a very long time in the bloodstained city of Jerusalem, so that both his mercy and his justice might shine more clearly. His mercy and goodness appear in that he allowed the doctrine of grace and salvation to be preached so long in a city soaked with the blood of his Son. His justice appears in that he destroyed with a dreadful overthrow those who were incurable and did not know how to repent. Meanwhile two things are to be observed by us. First, that limits have been fixed for the enemies of the word and of the Church, which they are not permitted to overstep. For he who set a boundary for the sea, within which that vast mass of waters is contained, and who binds Satan with laws, also restrains the wicked, so that they cannot do whatever they please, nor rage recklessly against whom they will. In this there is a remarkable comfort for minds, when we consider that the laws of divine providence can by no means be broken by the rages of the wicked. Second, the apostles set before us the example of the faithful ministers and leaders of the word and of the Church. For although they knew that Christ had said: "When they persecute you in one city, flee into another," nevertheless, since they were bound by a certain call, and saw that all the remnants of the Church would collapse if they too left the city, they preferred to undergo the extreme peril of life rather than abandon the Church by a shameful flight. And indeed in this matter ministers need careful caution. For just as those who look to their own safety by flight ought not to be condemned rashly, so we must by no means think that this is allowed to everyone in every place or time. But if the situation is such that either the minister alone is sought by the tyranny of the enemy, or he himself is deserted by those who until now have claimed for themselves the title of the Church, or certainly no ruin or dispersion of the Church follows from his departure, nothing stands in the way of his withdrawing until better times. But those who desert the public cause of the Church, and depart from churches that firmly hold the confession of faith, and by their departure give wolves the power of scattering the churches, these are truly deserters and hirelings, whom Christ says flee at the sight of the wolf. John 10. Would that those who have today too hastily abandoned the churches had weighed these things more carefully! They ought rather to have imitated the example of Ambrose, who dared to refuse the Arian basilicas even though the Emperor was unwilling. See the letter to Marcella his sister, which is numbered thirty-third. [Note: the passage in question is in the italicised text of the following unit.]

units.la: Pergens autem in instituta narratione Lucas, quid Stephano lapidibus obruto in tantis turbis & terroribus fideles, qui in urbe remanserunt, impenderint, docet. Primo autem hos illum curauisse, id est, sepulturae mandauisse dicit. Est hic vetustissimus mos, qui & primae Dei sententiae respondet, qua e terra sumptos in terram reditSuros pronunciauit: & resurrectionis mysterium continet, dum corpora telluri, ut semina sulcis mandantur, olim nimirum maiori cum honore resuscitanda. Caeterum alio etiam viros sanctos respexisse verisimile est. Nam dum eum honorifice sepeliunt, qui Concilij sententia damnatus erat, non obscure aduersariorum iniquitate arguunt, & constantem eduns fidei per Stephanum praedicatae confessionem. Adhaec se illum pie reuereri testantur, quem tam praeclarum Christi organum fuisse viderant. Nec eorum similes sunt, qui nostro seculo in verbi ministros impotentis & temerariae linguae habenas laxant, quorum liberiori doctrina aduersarios exacerbatos esse vident: adeo a fidis Christi ministris sanguinis iudicium expetunt, & eorum fortitudini insultant, quorum gloriae & honori studere debebant. Interim quid defunctorum corporibus debeatur hoc exemplo docemur. Sepultura nimirum, quam honorificam esse decet, quando corpora nostra spiritus sancti templa Paulus esse dicit. A sepulturis autem fastum simul & superstitionem abesse conuenit, quibus hodie variae peccatur. Sunt enim, qui stolide elati, mortalis suae conditionis ita oblivescuntur, ut post mortem quoque superbire velint, dum arma & vanae gloriae insignia sepulchris affigunt. Sunt rursum, qui vel exequijs & sacrificijs defunctorum peccata expiare satagunt, vel defunctos peculiari quadam Ceremonia canonizare, vel inter diuos referre solent: quorum alterum & inepetum est & exemplo caret, alterum vero Christi merito derogat, & doctrinae Christianae repugnat, quae credentes ex morte in vitam transfire, nec ullis nouis expiationibus indigere tradit. Ioan. 9. Deinde magnum planctum super Stephanum fecerunt. Nec id contra Pauli regulam fit, qui Christianos defunctos gentilitio planctu persequi vetat. 1. Thess. 4. Non enim ideo dolent, quod de Stephani conditione incerti sint aut dubij, sed quod impijs tantum licuisse, & ecclesia tanto ministro orbatam esse vident, cuius adhuc plurimus in propagando regno Christi vsus esse poterat. Nec statim peccas, quos humanitatis sensus & perdita cum amicis vitae recordatio ad lachrymas impellit: quando nos non truncos Deus fecit, & ἀσόφους pasim scriptura damnat. Ita Abrahamus Saram coniugem, loseph cum fratribus Iacobum patrem, Israelitae Aaronem, Mosen & Samuelem pio officio defluisse leguntur. Quid quod Christus Lazarum suum, cum sorores moerentes videret, lachrymis prosecutus est? Ioan. 11. Modus vero adhiberi debet, ne vel defunctis caelestem felicitatem inuidere, vel de huius hereditate dubij & in fide parum firmi esse censeri possimus.
units.tr: Luke, continuing his narrative, teaches what the faithful who remained in the city did for Stephen, stoned amid such great tumults and terrors. First, he says that these men "took care of him," that is, entrusted him to burial. This is a very ancient custom, which also answers to God's first sentence, by which he declared that men taken from the earth would return to the earth; and it contains the mystery of the resurrection, since bodies are committed to the earth as seeds are committed to furrows, to be raised again one day with greater honour. Moreover, it is likely that they also had regard to other holy men. For when they bury with honour the one who had been condemned by the sentence of the council, they clearly charge the adversaries with injustice, and they bear witness to the steadfast confession of the faith preached by Stephen. Besides, they testify that they piously revere the one whom they had seen to be so distinguished an instrument of Christ. Nor are they like those in our own age who loosen the reins of an unbridled and reckless tongue against the ministers of the word, whose freer teaching they see has exasperated the adversaries. So far do they seek the judgement of blood against the faithful ministers of Christ, and insult the courage of those whose glory and honour they ought to promote. Meanwhile, from this example we are taught what is owed to the bodies of the dead. Burial, namely, which ought to be honourable, since Paul says that our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit. But pride and superstition ought to be absent from burials, in which many errors are committed today. For there are some who, foolishly puffed up, forget their mortal condition so completely that they wish to be proud even after death, while they fix weapons and the emblems of vain glory to their tombs. There are again others who strive to expiate sins by funeral rites and sacrifices for the dead, or who are wont to canonise the dead with some peculiar ceremony, or to number them among the gods. Of these, the former is both foolish and lacking any example, while the latter detracts from the merit of Christ and is opposed to the Christian doctrine, which teaches that believers pass from death into life, and need no new expiations. John 9. Then they made great lamentation over Stephen. Nor is this done against the rule of Paul, who forbids Christians to pursue the dead with pagan lamentation. 1 Thess. 4. For they do not grieve because they are uncertain or doubtful about Stephen's condition, but because they see that the wicked have been allowed their way, and that the Church has been deprived of so great a minister, whose service could still have been of much use in spreading the kingdom of Christ. Nor do those sin at once who are moved to tears by the feeling of humanity and by the remembrance of a life lost with friends, since God has not made us stocks and stones, and Scripture everywhere condemns men without natural affection [ἄστοργοι]. Thus Abraham is read to have performed the pious duty of mourning for his wife Sarah; Joseph, with his brothers, for his father Jacob; the Israelites for Aaron, Moses and Samuel. What of the fact that Christ, when he saw his sisters grieving, wept with tears for his Lazarus? John 11. But a measure ought to be observed, lest we either begrudge the dead their heavenly happiness, or be thought doubtful about their inheritance and too weak in faith.

units.la: Vltimo singulare tyrannidis aduersus ecclesiam institutae, exemplum in Saulo Lucas proponit, in quo primum immanis tyranni crudelitas, deinde irritus tanti instituti euentus confyderari debent. Atqui de Saulo antea dictum est, quod & consenserit in necem Stephani, & lapidantium vestes custodierit: quibus significatur illum innoxij sanguinis reum factum fuisse. Nunc vero vniuersalis persecutionis tyrannide exaturari nequit, sed peculiare quid instituit, & totam quidem ecclesiam funditus extirpare conatur. Nec eos tantum oppugnat, qui ipsi fidem profitebantur publice, sed domos priuatas inuadit, & non viros modo, verumetiam mulieres (quas sexus infirmitas defendere poterat) protrahit & carceribus includit: vt non inepte Iacobi oraculum de lupo e Beniamin prociturum quidam in Saulum referri debere putarint. Genes. 49. Reuera enim lupus rapax fuit, qui tandem conuersus spolia salutifera euangelicae praedicationis per totum fere terrarum orbem distribuit. Et qua hic de illo Lucas commemorat, ipse non semel fatetur, imo saepius de ijsdem conqueritur. Vide Act. 26. 1. Corinth. 15. Galat. 1. Vsus vero omnium est, vt Dei bonitatem agnoscamus, qua tantum hostem in gratiam recipere dignatus est. Nam vt ipse interpretatur, in illo primo Iesus Christus omnem clementiam offendere voluit, ad exprimendum exemplar ijs, qui crediturii essent in ipso in vitam aeternam. 1. Tim. 1. Quid vero tantus Sauli conatus profecit? Num ecclesiam vastare potuit? Nihil minus. Imo author fuit, vt hinc inde dispersi credentes verbu salutis & Christi regnum latius propagarent. Ita Deus per ea filij sui gloriam illustrare nouit, quae huic cumprimis officere videbantur. Quo etiam referri potest, quod in euangelio daemones vel inuiti eos Christo adduxere, adduxêre, & coram illo prostrauêre, quos totos in suam potestatem redactos esse putabant. Ridicu- lus ergo illorum timor est, qui tyrannorum conatibus sese absterreri patiuntur. Interim officij admo- nemur, ne persecutionibus fracti, stationem deseramus illico. Quod hodie multi faciunt, qui vbi semel & iterum periclitati sunt, ipsi sibi ferias indicunt, quasi erga Christum omni officio plenissime defun- cti sint. Rectius autem hi faciunt, quorum hic Lucas meminit: qui Hierosolymis pulsi, exilio demum feruentiores facti, Christum passim prædicant: nimirum eius memores, quòd salui fore dicuntur, non qui bene cæperint, sed qui in finem usque perseuerarint. Matth. 24. Imitemur ergo horum zelum, ut vi- tæ huius curriculum constanti studio emensi, cœlestis brauij coronam assequamur in Christo Iesu: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Lastly, Luke sets before us in Saul a singular example of tyranny raised against the Church. In it we should consider first the savage cruelty of this cruel tyrant, and then the fruitless outcome of so great an undertaking. It was said earlier of Saul that he both consented to the killing of Stephen and kept the garments of those who stoned him, by which it is signified that he had become guilty of innocent blood. But now he could not be satisfied with the tyranny of a general persecution. He undertook something particular and tries to root out the whole Church from its foundations. Nor does he attack only those who openly professed the faith themselves. He invades private homes, and drags off not only men but also women (whom the weakness of their sex might have protected) and shuts them up in prisons. So some have not unsuitably thought that Jacob's prophecy about the wolf who would come from Benjamin should be referred to Saul. Genes. 49. For indeed he was a ravening wolf, who at last converted and distributed the saving spoils of evangelical preaching through almost the whole world. And what Luke recounts here of him, he himself confesses more than once; indeed he often complains of the same things. See Act. 26. 1. Corinth. 15. Galat. 1. It is, moreover, the custom of all of us to acknowledge God's goodness, by which he deigned to receive so great an enemy into favour. For, as he himself explains, in that first case Jesus Christ wished to display all his mercy, to set forth an example to those who were going to believe in him unto eternal life. 1. Tim. 1. But what did such a great effort of Saul achieve? Could he lay waste the Church? Nothing less. Indeed, he became the occasion for the believers, scattered here and there, to spread the word of salvation and the kingdom of Christ more widely. Thus God knew how to make the glory of his Son shine forth through those very things which seemed chiefly to hinder it. To this may also be referred what, in the Gospel, the demons, even against their will, brought people to Christ, and prostrated before him those whom they thought they had wholly reduced to their power. Therefore the fear of those is ridiculous who allow themselves to be frightened by the attempts of tyrants. Meanwhile we are reminded of our duty: not to abandon our post at once, broken by persecutions. Many do this today. Once or twice put in danger, they declare holidays for themselves, as if they had fully discharged every duty towards Christ. But those whom Luke mentions here act more rightly. Driven from Jerusalem, and made all the more fervent by exile, they preach Christ everywhere, mindful of that saying that those are saved not who have begun well, but who have persevered to the end. Matth. 24. Let us therefore imitate their zeal, so that, having finished the course of this life with constant earnestness, we may attain the crown of the heavenly prize in Christ Jesus, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LVII.
units.tr: Homily 57.

units.la: Philippus autem cum venisset in vrbem Samariæ, prædicauit illis Chri- stum. Attendebant autem turbæ vnanimiter his quæ dicebantur à Philip- po, cum audirent & viderent signa, quæ edebat. Nam cum multos im- mundi spiritus detinerent, clamantes voce magna exibant. Multi item paralytici & claudi sanati sunt. Et factum est gaudium magnum in illa ciuitate. Vir autem quidam, nomine Simon, priùs in vrbe fuerat, artem magicam exercens & dementans gentem Samariæ, dicens se esse aliquê magnum: cui adhærebant omnes à paruo vsque ad magnum, dicentes: Hic est magna illa virtus Dei. Adhærebant autem ei, eò quòd multo tem- pore magicis ipsius artibus dementati fuissent.
units.tr: When Philip came down to the city of Samaria, he preached Christ to them. The crowds paid close and united attention to what Philip said, when they heard him and saw the signs he performed. For many people were held by unclean spirits, and these came out crying with a loud voice. Many paralytics and lame men were also healed. And there was great joy in that city. But a certain man named Simon had previously been in the city, practising magic and bewitching the people of Samaria, saying that he himself was someone great. All of them, from the least to the greatest, clung to him, saying: This is that great power of God. They clung to him because for a long time they had been bewitched by his magic arts.

units.la: Quamuis Christi regnum & ecclesia perpetuis mundi impij conatibus oppugnari soleat, ex- pugnari tamen non potest, eò quòd æterna & inuicta sit oraculorum & promissionum Dei veritas, qui Christo filio suo regnum æternum destinauit. Id verò multis exemplis hucusq; illustra- tum fuisse vidimus. Sæpe enim in Senatu & Concilio acerrimè concertatū est cum apostolis: semper autem victrix discessit Veritas. Tandem lapidatus fuit Stephanus, eoq; successu ferociores factì ho- stes extremos conatus proferunt, inter quos Sauli rabies maximè elucet. Sed adeò non extinguitur inter furores hosce Christi regnum, vt potius in Iudæam omnem, adeoq; in Samariam usq; extenda- tur, quod hucusq; nimium angustiis Hierosolymorum mœnijs inclusum videri poterat. Hinc verò oc- casione sumpta, Lucas diligentius narrat, quo successu extra Iudæam euangelium prædicari cœperit. Et primùm de Samariæ conuersione, quam prophetarum oraculis prædictā fuisse legimus, agit: in cu- ius historia eò maiori studio nobis versandum est, quòd multum nostræ tum consolationi tum institu- tioni seruire possunt, quæ in hac diligentissimè perscripta proponuntur.
units.tr: Although the kingdom of Christ and the Church are usually attacked by the constant efforts of the impious world, they cannot be overcome, because the truth of God's oracles and promises is eternal and invincible, and God destined an eternal kingdom for his Son Christ. We have seen this shown by many examples up to now. For often there was the sharpest contest with the apostles in the Senate and the council, yet Truth always departed victorious. At last Stephen was stoned, and the enemies, made more fierce by this success, made their final attempts, among whom the rage of Saul shines most clearly. But the kingdom of Christ is not extinguished amid these furies; rather it is spread into all Judea, and even into Samaria, which until now could seem to have been shut in too narrowly within the walls of Jerusalem. Taking this occasion, Luke relates more carefully with what success the gospel began to be preached outside Judea. And first he deals with the conversion of Samaria, which we read was foretold by the oracles of the prophets. In this history we must dwell with all the greater care, because the things set forth here most diligently written down can serve greatly both for our consolation and for our instruction.

units.la: Primò, cuius ministerio Deus in conuertenda Samaria vsus sit, docet. Fuit is Philippus, nō qui- dem apostolus, sed qui supra inter Diaconos numeratus fuit, quemadmodum vnanimi consensu ve- teres ecclesiæ scriptores testantur, Epiphanius maximè de Simone & Simoniacis scribens. Licet enim diaconorum partes essent, communium ecclesiæ opum & pauperum curam gerere, simul tamen illis permissum erat euangelij prædicationem suscipere, si quando necessitas ita postularet, quod in Stephani exemplo bucusq; vidimus. Et fortassis non adeò magnus diaconorum vsus erat Hierosoly- mæ, cùm ecclesia persecutionis tempestate dispersa esset: & ideò ad verbi ministerium se totos contu- lerunt, qui priùs publica ecclesiæ bona dispensabant. Sed & Paulus postea monuit, vt diaconi bene ministrando gradum sibi ad maiorem functionem acquirant. 1. Timoth. 3. Duo autem Philippus Samariæ fecisse dicitur. Primò Christum illis prædicauit. Et quod hîc breuisculè proponit Lucas, idipsum infra clarius exponit, vbi illum mysteria regni Dei & nominis Iesu Christi prædicauisse di- cit. In præsenti autem solius Christi meminit, eò quòd huius nomine euangelium totum comprehen- ditur. Huius enim partes ipse Christus constituit, pœnitentiam & remissionem peccatorum. At v- trang, Christus Iesus confert, sicuti supra Petrus disserte monuit. Actio 5. Solus enim hic regeneratio- nis spiritum donat, & corruptæ naturæ succurrit. Idem etiam solus peccata remittit, & illa sanguin nis suo pretio expiauit. Quare qui Christum praedicat, idem poenitentiam veram & peccatorum remissionem necessario praedicabit. Et est haec infallibilis nota, qua veri euangelistae a falsis discerni possunt. Quicunq; enim Christum Iesum in carnem venisse docent, & ea peregisse, quae corrigenda simul & saluanda humanae naturae necessaria erant, pro veris Christi ministris agnosci debent. 1. Iohan. 4. Quisquis vero haec alibi, quam in Christo, monstrauerit, & noua finxerit salutis acquirendae media, falsus doctor dicetur, etiamsi angelus de caelo fuerit. Gal. 1. Ideo Paulus se solum Iesum Christum nouisse, & in illius duntaxat cruce gloriari, ingenue testatur. 1. Corinth. 2. Galat. 6. Praedicationi vero signa accesserunt, quae per Philippum iuxta Christi promissiones edita sunt. Nam & spiritus immundos ab hominibus expulit, & paralyticos, quorum iam desperata salus erat, curauit. Necsuperuacanea fuit haec spiritus Christi operatio. Licet enim per verbum omnia ea nobis offerantur, quae salutem seruiunt, animos tamen nostros ingenito quodam veterno aggrauatos externis signis excitari, & ad verbum excipiendum praeparari necesse est. Praeterea, cum multa extrinsecus accidant, quibus fides nostra tentatur, vehementer prodest, eam externis quoque signis fulciri. Interim eiusmodi fere signa per apostolos edita fuisse legimus, quae beneficiorum Christi nos admonere possunt. Is enim diaboli vires attribuit, regnum illius euertit, & nos ex eius tyrannide fortiter asseruit. Idem corruptae naturae vires instaurauit, vt qui ex nobis ipsis nulli rei bonae exequendae sufficimus, in illo possimus omnia. 2. Corinth. 3. Philip. 4. Et sine illo nos nihil posse, ipse in euangelio testatur. Ioban. 15. Caeterum obseruatione dignissimum est, quod immundi spiritus non fine clamore emigrauisse dicuntur. Idem alibi quoque illos fecisse constat. Nam apud Christum, se ante tempus eici queruntur, & miserè laniatos relinquunt eos, ex quibus inuiti discedunt. Haec vero satanae ingenium nobis obocu-los ponunt, perdendis hominibus per omnia addictum. Vt enim ab initio homicida fuit, ita nunquam non rugientis leonis instar obambulat, & quaerit quem deuoret. Ioban. 8. 1. Pet. 5. Qua causa est, quod inuitus eos deserit, quorum animos semel occupauit. Imo eiectus etiam, denuo se insinuare & amissam possessionem recuperare studet, vt Christus in Euangelio monuit. Matth. 12. Haec vero vt nos ad ardens pugnandi studium excitant, ne tam noxij hostis dolo circumuenti, salutis iacturam faciamus: ita Christi potentiam nobis declarant, qui diabolum quantumuis renitentem & inuitum, suo spiritu & verbo tam facile expellit.
units.tr: First, he teaches by whose ministry God was pleased to use in converting Samaria. This was Philip, not indeed an apostle, but one who was counted above among the deacons, as the ancient writers of the Church testify with one voice, Epiphanius especially, writing about Simon and the Simonians. For although it was the part of deacons to take care of the common goods of the Church and the care of the poor, nevertheless they were also permitted to undertake the preaching of the gospel, if ever necessity so required; as we have seen up to now in the example of Stephen. And perhaps the service of deacons was not so great in Jerusalem, since the Church was scattered by the storm of persecution; and therefore those who had previously dispensed the public goods of the Church devoted themselves wholly to the ministry of the Word. But Paul also later advised that deacons, by serving well, should acquire for themselves a step to a higher function (1 Tim. 3). Now Philip is said to have done two things in Samaria. First, he preached Christ to them. What Luke here sets forth briefly he explains more clearly below, where he says that Philip preached the mysteries of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ. Here, however, he mentions only Christ, because the whole gospel is comprehended in his name. For Christ himself appointed its parts: repentance and the remission of sins. Both are bestowed by Christ Jesus, as Peter plainly warned above (Acts 5). For he alone gives the Spirit of regeneration and comes to the aid of corrupted nature. He alone also forgives sins, and expiated them by the price of his blood. Therefore whoever preaches Christ will necessarily preach true repentance and the remission of sins. And this is the infallible mark by which true evangelists can be distinguished from false ones. For whoever teaches that Christ Jesus came in the flesh, and performed those things which were necessary both to correct and to save human nature, ought to be acknowledged as a true minister of Christ (1 John 4). But whoever shows these things anywhere other than in Christ, and invents new means of acquiring salvation, will be called a false teacher, even if he were an angel from heaven (Gal. 1). Therefore Paul frankly testifies that he knew only Jesus Christ, and gloried only in his cross (1 Cor. 2; Gal. 6). Signs also accompanied the preaching, which were performed through Philip according to Christ's promises. For he drove unclean spirits out of men, and healed paralytics whose salvation was already despaired of. Nor was this work of the Spirit of Christ superfluous. For although all those things which serve our salvation are offered to us through the Word, nevertheless our minds, weighed down by a certain innate lethargy, must be roused by external signs and prepared to receive the Word. Moreover, since many things happen from outside by which our faith is tested, it greatly helps for it to be supported also by external signs. Meanwhile we read that signs of this kind were for the most part performed by the apostles, which can remind us of the benefits of Christ. For he assigns power to the devil, overturns his kingdom, and strongly delivers us from his tyranny. He also restored the powers of corrupted nature, so that we, who of ourselves are not sufficient for carrying out any good thing, may be able to do all things in him (2 Cor. 3; Phil. 4). And he himself testifies in the gospel that without him we can do nothing (John 15). Moreover, it is most worthy of notice that the unclean spirits are said to have departed not without a shout. It is clear that they did the same elsewhere too. For they complain before Christ that they are cast out before the time, and they leave behind those from whom they reluctantly depart, grievously torn. These things set before our eyes the nature of Satan, who is devoted to destroying men in every way. For as he was a murderer from the beginning, so he never ceases to prowl like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour (John 8; 1 Pet. 5). For this reason he reluctantly abandons those whose minds he has once seized. Indeed, even when cast out, he strives to insinuate himself again and to recover the possession he has lost, as Christ warned in the gospel (Matt. 12). These things stir us to an ardent zeal for fighting, lest, circumvented by the trickery of so harmful an enemy, we suffer loss of salvation; and in the same way they declare to us the power of Christ, who with his Spirit and Word so easily drives out the devil, however much he resists and is unwilling.

units.la: II. Samaritani euangelium amplectuntur.
units.tr: II. The Samaritans embrace the gospel.

units.la: Videamus autem, vt Samaritani Iesum Christum, quem Philippus praedicabat, exceperint. Attendebant (inquit Lucas) turbae vnanimiter his quae dicebantur a Philippo, cum audirent, & videbant signa quae edebat. Et paulo post: Factum est gaudium magnum in illa ciuitate. His autem duo praecipue comprehendit euangelista. Primo illos Christum recepisse, & quo ordine ad huius cognitionem fidemq; peruenerint, docet. Deinde studij fideiq; huius fructum indicat. Ad prius pertinet, quod illos Philippi conciones audiuisse, miracula item vidisse, omnibus vero hisce animos applicuisse & attendisse dicit. Ex hoc itaq; studio fides enata est, quam (vt infra audiemus) baptismo obsignarunt. Nobis vero in his ordo salutis consyderandus venit. Nam licet vnicum huius authorem Deum esse agnoscamus, qui pro suo arbitrio in hominibus operatur, plerunq; tamen legitimo & certo ordine ac modo ad salutem nos perducere consueuit. In hoc primus locus verbi studio debetur. Quia enim per hoc salutem nobis Deus offert, adeoq; (vt Dauides inquit, Psal. 107.) missio verbo suo sanat nos, illud a nobis negligi non poterit, siquidem saluari volumus. At quia audiuisse non satis est (cum illud interdum impij & ipsi daemones faciant) animos permoueri & excitari oportet. Fit hoc partim externis rebus, vt hic per signa: partim interna spiritus sancti suggestione, quae nisi accedat, nihil vt externa verbi praedicatione vel lectione proficietur, sicuti diligenter & ingenue Paulus docuit. 1. Corinth. 3. Caeterum quando verbum suum nobis Deus reuelat, & mentes nostras tum externis rebus, tum spiritus sui suggestione extimulat, a nobis attentione & studium ardens requirit: ne vel patula mente infernales aues admittamus, quae semen deuorent, vel illud inter spinas suffocari, aut etiam a pra-uissimis affectibus conculcari patiamur. De qua re fideliter Christus admonuit. Luc. 8. & Matthaei 13. Quicunq; ergo hoc ordine in salutis negotio procedunt, quod hic Samaritanos fecisse legimus, magnum brevi profectum sentiunt. Haec vero si ad nostros mores transferas, quid illis respondere debeat, videbis, quibus mirum & insolens videtur, quod rarissimi ex verbi praedicatione, vt par erat, proficiant. Quotus enim quisque est, qui non in ipso limine (quod aiunt) impingat? Rari in templis verbi auditores considerantur, & egregiè se pietatis officio functos putant, qui dominicis diebus concionem sacram audiunt. Rariores tamen sunt, qui attentis animis & discendi cupidis audiant. Rarissimi verò, qui quod audiuerunt, sedulò meditentur. Interim dominantur passim improbissimi carnis affectus, qui nos in caeca mundi studia transfuerfos abripiunt. Quid ergo hic fiat aliud, quàm quod in agro sentibus & filicibus obsito, si nulla culturae diligentia accedat, fieri consueuit? Excutiamus noxiam hanc animorum ofcitantiam, & Samaritanos imitemur, nec deerit fructus, quem hos breui assecutos fuisse, Lucas docet.
units.tr: Let us now see how the Samaritans received Jesus Christ, whom Philip preached. Luke says: "The crowds gave heed unanimously to what was said by Philip when they heard him and saw the signs that he did." And a little later: "There was great joy in that city." The evangelist includes two things here. First, he teaches that they received Christ and by what order they came to know him and to believe. Second, he shows the fruit of this earnest attention and faith. To the first belongs the fact that they heard Philip's sermons, saw the miracles, and, as he says, applied their minds to all of these and paid attention. From this earnest attention faith sprang up, which (as we shall hear below) they sealed with baptism. For us, the order of salvation has to be considered in these things. For although we acknowledge God as the sole author of this, who works in people as he wills, yet he is accustomed to bring us to salvation by a lawful and fixed order and manner. In this order, the first place is owed to earnest attention to the Word. For since God offers salvation to us through the Word, and so (as David says, Ps. 107) "he sends his word and heals us," this cannot be neglected by us, if we wish to be saved. But because hearing is not enough (for the wicked and even the demons do this too), it is necessary that our minds be moved and stirred. This happens partly by external things, as here by signs; partly by the inward prompting of the Holy Spirit, which, unless it is added, nothing is gained by the external preaching or reading of the Word, as Paul taught carefully and candidly (1 Cor. 3). Moreover, when God reveals his Word to us, and stirs our minds both by external things and by the prompting of his Spirit, he requires from us attention and ardent zeal, lest we admit the infernal birds with an open mind, which devour the seed, or allow it to be choked among thorns, or even trampled down by the most wicked affections. Christ faithfully warned about this (Luke 8; Matt. 13). Therefore, those who proceed in this order in the business of salvation, as we read that the Samaritans did here, soon feel great progress. If you apply these things to our manners, you will see what should be answered to those for whom it seems strange and unusual that very few profit from the preaching of the Word as they ought. For how few are there who do not stumble at the very threshold (as they say)? Hearers of the Word are rare in the churches, and those who hear the sacred sermon on the Lord's days are thought to have discharged the duty of piety very well. Yet fewer still are those who hear with attentive minds and eager to learn. And very rare are those who diligently meditate on what they have heard. Meanwhile the most wicked desires of the flesh rule everywhere, and carry us off, turned aside into the blind pursuits of the world. What else, then, happens here than what usually happens in a field overgrown with brambles and ferns, if no careful cultivation is applied? Let us shake off this harmful dullness of mind, and let us imitate the Samaritans, and the fruit which Luke says they soon obtained will not be lacking.

units.la: Dicit enim: Factum est gaudium magnum in illa ciuitate. Est hic fidei fructus, qui ex sensu reconciliati nobis Dei enascisi consueuit. Vt enim irati Dei vultus animos scelerum conscientia perterritos, horribili metu & solicitudine diuexat: ita euangelij doctrina, quae credentibus Deum in filio suo Iesu Christo reconciliatum esse docet, noua & mira laetitia mentes perfundit. Ideo angeli, quando Christi natiuitatem pastoribus nuntiant, se illis gaudium ingens praedicare dicunt. Luc.2. Et Simeon senex, huius gaudij sensu abreptus, dimitti, & corporis huius carcere liberari cupit. Paulus item Christianos perpetuò gaudere iubet, eò quòd gaudium hoc nullis quantumuis aduersa fortunae casibus restingui possit, cum in afflictionibus quoq; pij gloriari soleant, vt supra in apostolis vidimus, qui eo nomine gaudent, quòd digni habiti sint, qui propter Christi nomen virgis caederentur. Impij ergo & ingratissimi hominum sunt, qui euangelium infortuniorum & publicarum calamitatum causam esse dicunt, cum has propter hominum peccata & inobedientiam immitti constet. Sed illorum similes sunt, qui Ieremiae hoc vnum obijciebant, quòd omnis generis aerumnas sensissent ab eo tempore quo ipse praedicare coeperat. Vide Ierem.44.
units.tr: For he says: "There was great joy in that city." This is the fruit of faith, which is usually born from the sense of God reconciled to us. For just as the face of an angry God torments minds terrified by the consciousness of sins with dreadful fear and anxiety, so the doctrine of the gospel, which teaches that God has been reconciled to believers in his Son Jesus Christ, fills minds with a new and wonderful gladness. Therefore the angels, when they announced Christ's birth to the shepherds, said that they were proclaiming to them a great joy (Luke 2). And old Simeon, carried away by the sense of this joy, desired to be dismissed and freed from the prison of this body. Paul likewise bids Christians always to rejoice, because this joy can be quenched by no adverse chances of fortune, since the godly are accustomed to glory even in afflictions, as we saw above in the apostles, who rejoiced on this account, that they were considered worthy to be beaten with rods for the name of Christ. Therefore those are impious and most ungrateful of men who say that the gospel is the cause of misfortunes and public calamities, since it is clear that these are sent on account of human sins and disobedience. But they are like those who objected to Jeremiah this one thing: that they had felt every kind of misery from the time when he had begun to preach (see Jer. 44).

units.la: Porrò, vt ad Lucam reuertamur, feliciter succedente apud Samaritanos Christi regno, ingens remora obijcitur: Simon Magus nimirum, qui longo tempore in ea ciuitate dominatus fuerat, & infelices magicis artibus dementarat. Voluit hunc cum Philippo & apostolis committi Deus, partim vt sciremus semper in ecclesia hypocritas fore, quorum leuitate & perfidia nemo offendi debeat: partim verò, vt euidenti & infallibili argumento omnibus notum fieret, per apostolos nō magicis artibus, sed diuina virtute, miracula edi, quando ab his celeberrimus Magus gloriosa victoria superatus, maiorem in ipsis virtutem agnouit, quam pecunia redimi posse putauit. Eadem ratione cum Mose etiam Aegyptiacos Magos congredi voluit Deus. Hic verò singulas personas diligentius inspicere prodest.
units.tr: Moreover, to return to Luke: while Christ's kingdom was succeeding happily among the Samaritans, a great obstacle is thrown in the way: namely Simon Magus, who had long ruled in that city and had driven people out of their minds by his magical arts. God willed that he should be pitted against Philip and the apostles, partly so that we might know that there will always be hypocrites in the Church, by whose fickleness and treachery no one ought to be offended; but partly so that it might be made known to all, by a clear and infallible argument, that miracles were performed through the apostles not by magical arts but by divine power, when this most famous magician, overcome by a glorious victory, acknowledged in them a greater power than he thought could be bought with money. For the same reason God also willed that Moses should contend with the Egyptian magicians. Here it is useful to examine the individual persons more carefully.

units.la: Et primò quidem Philippus haud vulgare fortitudinis fidei exemplum nobis exhibet. Erat enim ingens sanioris doctrinae remora Simon hic, quando error Samaritanorum tum vetustate, tum superstitione confirmatus erat. Nam non diuina modò virtute Simonem instructum, sed hunc ipsam Dei virtutem esse credebant. Ac nec magicorum incantamentorum praestigijs, nec stolidi populi pertinaci errore Philippus abster retur: quin potius Christi praeceptum respicit, qui in Samaria quoque euangelium praedicare iusserat. Hunc animum imitentur, quicunq; munus aliquod diuinitus sibi commissum esse vident, siue illi publicae siue priuatae personae fuerint. Nec enim leuibus terriculamentis eos impediri decet, qui Christo nomen dederunt, cuius potentiam inuictam esse tot tantisq; argumentis probatum est. Cogitemus fortiorem & maiorem esse eum, qui in nobis agit, quàm qui in mundo temere ferocire solet. 1.Ioan.4.
units.tr: And first, Philip sets before us an example of no ordinary courage in faith. For this Simon was a great obstacle to sounder teaching, since the error of the Samaritans had been confirmed both by antiquity and by superstition. For they believed that Simon was not only endowed with divine power, but that he himself was the power of God. And Philip was not deterred either by the trickery of magical incantations or by the stubborn error of a foolish people; rather, he kept before his eyes the command of Christ, who had also ordered the gospel to be preached in Samaria. Let those who see that some task has been committed to them by God imitate this spirit, whether they are public or private persons. For those who have given their name to Christ, whose power has been proved invincible by so many and such great arguments, ought not to be hindered by slight frights. Let us reflect that he who works in us is stronger and greater than he who rages rashly in the world (1 John 4).

units.la: Simon autem memorabile impostoris exemplum est, quem non inepte cum Baalamo pseudopropheta conferre possis. Dicitur is longo tempore infelicem Samariae populum dementauisse. Nam magia instructus, stupenda opera edebat, & diuinos sibi vendicabat honores, cum seipsum quidem non modò magnam Dei virtutem, verumetiam Deum patrem & filium (vt Epiphanius, diligentissimus veterum haeresteon indagator, memoria prodidit) scortillum verò Helenam, spiritum sanctum esse diceret. Huius autem exemplo admonemur, posse aliquid per suos ministros diabolum, non quidem propria & libera potestate, sed Dei permissione. Hac enim factum vidimus, quòd Aegyptiorum Magi quaedam Mosis miracula non omnino infeliciter imitati sunt. Et malefica, Saule tyranno postulante, Samuelis imaginem e sepulchro excitauisse visa est. 1.Sam.28. Quibus merito adnumerari debent oracula olim apud Delphos & Pythios edita, quamuis ea plerunq; ambigua & ancipitis significationis fuerint. Eiusdem generis sunt, quae de imaginibus traduntur, quarum alia quidem locuta sunt, aliae e sedibus suis migrauerunt, infinitae autem aliae variis miraculis olim celebres fuere: vt interim de ijs nihil dicam, quae sub Antichristi regno euenerunt, sicuti olim Christus & apostoli praedixerunt. Permittit autem haec iusto iudicio Deus: partim quidem propter impios, qui decipi merentur, cum veritatem amplecti nolunt, vt Pharaonis & Saulis exempla non obscure docent: partim vero propter electos, quorum fidem ita probari oportet, vt nudo Dei verbo adhaerere discant, nec aliquid contra illud admittant, vtcunq; authoritatem summam mereri videatur. Et huius quidem ipse dominus nos admonet, quando in lege pseudoprophetis credere vetat; etiamsi doctrinam suam miraculis confirmauerint. Nam tentat vos (inquit Moses) dominus Deus vester, num diligatis dominum Deum vestrum in toto corde vestro, &c. Deut. 13. Frustra ergo miracula nobis obiiciunt, qui diuersa a Dei verbo obtrudere conantur. Vide 2. Thess. 2. Matth. 24.
units.tr: Simon, however, is a notable example of an impostor, whom one could not inappropriately compare with Balaam the false prophet. He is said to have deluded the unhappy people of Samaria for a long time. For, furnished with magic, he performed astonishing works and claimed divine honours for himself, saying that he was not only the great power of God, but also God the Father and the Son (as Epiphanius, the most diligent investigator of the ancient heresies, has recorded), and that the harlot Helen was the Holy Spirit. From his example we are warned that the devil can accomplish something through his ministers, not indeed by his own and free power, but by the permission of God. For we have seen this happen, in that the magicians of Egypt imitated some of Moses' miracles, not altogether unsuccessfully. And at the request of Saul the tyrant, a sorcery seemed to raise the image of Samuel from the grave (1 Sam. 28). To these rightly should be added the oracles once given at Delphi and by the Pythia, although these were for the most part ambiguous and of doubtful meaning. Of the same kind are the things that are reported about images, some of which indeed spoke, while others moved from their places, and countless others were once famous for various miracles; not to mention for now those things that have happened under the reign of Antichrist, just as Christ and the apostles foretold. God permits these things by his just judgment: partly indeed on account of the impious, who deserve to be deceived because they are unwilling to embrace the truth, as the examples of Pharaoh and Saul clearly teach; but partly on account of the elect, whose faith must be tested in such a way that they learn to cling to the bare Word of God and admit nothing against it, however much authority such things may seem to deserve. The Lord himself warns us of this, when in the law he forbids us to believe false prophets, even though they confirm their teaching with miracles. "For the Lord your God tests you," says Moses, "whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart," etc. (Deut. 13). Therefore they object miracles to us in vain, who try to force on us things that differ from the Word of God (see 2 Thess. 2; Matt. 24).

units.la: Simul vero euidens impostorum nota, ex qua illi agnosci possint, in Simone proponitur. Diuinos enim sibi honores vendicat, quod in primis affectat satan, vt suo honore Deum spoliet. Quae in re a bonis angelis longe differt, qui honores ab hominibus sponte oblatos respuunt, & ad unum Deum relegant. Vide Apocal. 19. & 22. Et fideles Dei serui, cum ingenitae corruptionis probe memores sint, a sacrilega diuini honoris ambitione alienissimi, in unum Deum referre solent quicquid ab ipsis recte & laude dignum fit. Exemplum eius supra in Iohanne & Petro vidimus, simile infra in Paulo etiam visuri. Act. 14. Procul ergo facessant & vt impijssimi impostores explodantur, quicunq; vel minimam diuini honoris portionem sibi vendicare audent. Nec enim fidelis seruus esse potest, quisquis herilis gloriae splendorem in se transferre voluerit, &c.
units.tr: At the same time, a clear mark by which impostors can be recognised is set forth in Simon. For Satan, who above all aims at this, claims for himself divine honours, so that by his own honour he may deprive God of his. In this he differs far from the good angels, who refuse honours willingly offered them by men and refer them back to the one God alone. See Revelation 19 and 22. And the faithful servants of God, being well aware of their innate corruption and utterly remote from the sacrilegious ambition for divine honour, are wont to refer to the one God whatever is done by them rightly and is worthy of praise. We saw an example of this above in John and Peter, and we shall see a similar one below in Paul, Acts 14. Let them therefore depart far away, and let those most wicked impostors be driven out, whoever dares to claim for himself even the smallest portion of divine honour. For no one can be a faithful servant who wishes to transfer to himself the splendour of his master's glory, etc.

units.la: Postremo in Samaritanis leuitatis vulgi exemplum habemus, quando impostori impurissimo se decipiendos & seducendos praebent. Est hoc proprium mundo, quod deceptoribus gaudet, & novorum dolorum fabricatoribus mirifice delectatur. Quod si vero vel leuissima emolumenti spes accedat, mox furere senties, quos ab vnius Dei verbo dependere oportebat. Exempla huius insaniae nobis hodie praebent, qui ariolos & diuinos sequuntur, vt ab illis res amissas recipiant, vel quis illas ab stulerit, reficiant. Quibus deteriores sunt, qui incantationibus & conceptorum verborum murmure morbos depellere putant, & eos sumptuosa superstitione conducunt, qui id genus veneficij profitentur. Laudem vero merentur Samaritanorum obedientia, quam meliora edocti, Christo praestiterunt. Hanc nos imitari decet, nec curiosis artibus operam nauare, quas iam olim Dei sententia damnatas esse constat. Vide Exod. 22. Leuit. 20. Deut. 18. Mich. 5. Christum Iesum doctorem & saluatorem destinauit Deus pater. Hunc nos audire & illius iussa capessere conuenit. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Finally, in the Samaritans we have an example of the levity of the common people, when they allow themselves to be deceived and seduced by a most impure impostor. It is a characteristic of the world that it delights in deceivers and wonderfully enjoys the makers of new sorrows. But if even the slightest hope of gain is added, you will soon see them go mad, when they ought to have depended on the Word of the one God alone. Today there are examples of this madness among those who follow soothsayers and diviners, so that they may recover lost goods or, if someone has stolen them, get them back. Worse than these are those who think they can drive away diseases by incantations and the murmuring of set words, and who hire, through costly superstition, those who profess this kind of sorcery. The obedience of the Samaritans, however, deserves praise, since, once taught better things, they yielded to Christ. We ought to imitate this, and not spend our effort on curious arts, which, as is clear, were condemned long ago by the sentence of God. See Exodus 22, Leviticus 20, Deuteronomy 18, Micah 5. God the Father appointed Christ Jesus as teacher and Saviour. It is fitting that we hear him and carry out his commands. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY 58.

units.la: Porro cum credidissent Philippo euangelizanti de regno Dei, & de nomine Iesu Christi, baptizati sunt, viri simul & mulieres. Sed & ipse quoque Simon credidit, & baptizatus adhaerebat Philippo, videnscp virtutes & signa, quae fiebant, obstupebat. Cum autem audiuissent apostoli, qui erant Hierosolymis, quod Samaria recepisset verbum Dei, miserunt ad eos Petrum & Iohannem. Qui cum descendissent, orauerunt pro eis, vt reciperent spiritum sanctum. Nondum enim super quenquam illorum illapsus fuerat: sed baptizati tantum fuerant in nomine Christi Iesu. Tunc imposuerunt manus super illos, & receperunt spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: Then, when those who had believed Philip preaching the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ were baptized, both men and women. Simon himself also believed, and after being baptized he attached himself to Philip, and he was amazed as he saw the powers and signs that were done. When the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them. When these had come down, they prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit. For he had not yet fallen upon any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Quoniam Saluatoris nostri Iesu Christi regnum per totum terrarum orbem extendi debuit, euangelium quoque, cuius doctrina homines Christo adducuntur, in omnibus gentibus praedicari necesse fuit. Cuius rei mandatum ab ipso Christo, iam caelos conscensuro, apostolos accepisse vidimus. Occasionem autem huic negotio exequendo immanis persecutio praebuit, quam Hierosolymis excitatam fuisse, Lucas docuit. Cum enim ante hanc apostolorum conciones in sola Hierosolymorum vrbe sonarent, inde dispersi, alijs quoq; in locis praedicare coeperunt fideles Christi ministri, &c. & eo successu vsi sunt, vt breui temporis spacio Philippus Samariam ingressus, illius vrbis po-pulum, quem Magicis artibus antea Simon dementauerat, assidua euangelij praedicatione Christo lucrifaceret. Neglectis enim Magicis praestigijs, vni Christo aures praebere & credere coeperunt. Quam feliciter autem hoc ab illis coeptum sit, praesens locus perspicuè docet, qui pleniorem illius ecclesiae constitutionem, & amplissimos illorum hominum in fide & reliquis spiritualibus donis progressus diligentissimè exponit.
units.tr: Since the kingdom of our Saviour Jesus Christ had to be extended through the whole round of the earth, the gospel also, by whose teaching people are brought to Christ, had to be preached among all nations. We have seen that the apostles received the command for this from Christ himself, as he was about to ascend into heaven. The occasion for carrying out this task was given by the huge persecution which, Luke has taught, was stirred up at Jerusalem. For before this, the apostles' preaching had resounded only within the city of Jerusalem; from there, scattered, the faithful ministers of Christ began to preach in other places as well, etc. And they used such success that, in a short space of time, Philip, entering Samaria, won for Christ by constant preaching of the gospel the people of that city whom Simon had earlier bewitched with magic arts. For, setting aside the magic tricks, they began to lend their ears to Christ alone and to believe. How happily this was begun among them, the present passage makes plain, as it sets out in detail the fuller establishment of that church and the very large advances those people made in faith and in the other spiritual gifts.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Primò autem, vt in vnum ecclesiae corpus publicè coaluerint, ostenditur, cum dicit: Porrò cum credidissent Philippo euangelizanti de regno Dei, & de nomine Iesu Christi, baptizati sunt, viri simul & mulieres. Praecipuus ergo hic locus fidei tribuitur, quam Philippo euangelizanti adhibuerunt, & ita quidem, vt illius doctrinam nulla maiori authoritate confirmandam putarent, quam quae in miraculis, per ipsum editis, elucebat. Per fidem ergo ecclesias rite coalescere & interno vinculo firmissimè constringi discimus. Haec enim sola nos Christo Iesu inserit, & in illo eiusdem corporis membra facit, sicuti Paulus multis in locis testatur. Vnde rursum non obscurè colligimus, ecclesiam Dei esse non posse, vbi fide in Christum deficiuntur homines, quia tales diuersissimis studijs & maximè contrarijs sensibus distrahi oportet. Admonemur autem Samaritanorum exemplo, verbo Dei, quod per homines praedicatur, credendum esse, nec illud ad humanae rationis calculum revocari debere, vt noua illi aliunde accedat authoritas. Nam vt scripturas sacras diuinitus inspiratas esse Paulus testatur: ita verbi ministerium a Christo in ecclesia institutum esse, idem diserte monet. Ephes. 4. Quisquis ergo ministris, Christi vocem & verba afferentibus, crediderit, vt non hominibus, sed Christo credidisse dicetur. Ad omnes enim hos vox illa Christi pertinet: Qui vos audit, me audit. Et qui recipit quem ego misero, me recipit. Luc. 10. Iohan. 13. Quare Paulus Thessalonicenses hoc nomine laudandos putat, quod ipsius doctrinam, non vt hominis sermonem, sed vt vocem angeli receperint. 1. Thess. 2. Et eandem laudem Samaritani merentur, & quotquot alij horum exemplo euangelio credere confreuerunt.
units.tr: First, that they were firmly joined together into one body of the church publicly, is shown where he says: Then, when those who had believed Philip preaching the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ were baptized, both men and women. The chief place is therefore given here to the faith which they gave to Philip preaching, and indeed so that they thought his teaching was to be confirmed by no greater authority than that which shone forth in the miracles he performed. We learn, then, that churches are rightly joined together through faith and are bound most firmly by an inner bond. For faith alone engrafts us into Christ Jesus and makes us members of the same body in him, as Paul testifies in many places. Hence again we gather, not obscurely, that the church of God cannot exist where people fail in faith in Christ, because such people must be pulled apart by the most diverse pursuits and by the most contrary opinions. We are warned, moreover, by the example of the Samaritans, that the word of God, which is preached by men, must be believed, and that it must not be called back to the reckoning of human reason, so that new authority might come to it from elsewhere. For just as Paul testifies that the holy Scriptures are inspired by God, so he clearly teaches the same thing, that the ministry of the Word was instituted in the church by Christ. Eph. 4. Whoever therefore has believed ministers who bring the voice and words of Christ is said to have believed not men but Christ. For that saying of Christ applies to all of these: He who hears you hears me, and he who receives whomever I send receives me. Luke 10. John 13. Wherefore Paul thinks the Thessalonians are to be praised on this account, that they received his teaching not as the word of a man but as the voice of an angel. 1 Thess. 2. And the Samaritans deserve the same praise, as do all others who have become accustomed to believe the gospel after their example.

units.la: Porrò internae coniunctioni, quae fide constat, externum quoque communionis vinculum accedit. Omnes enim simul, tam viros quàm mulieres, in nomine Iesu Christi baptizatos fuisse dicitur. Vt enim suos è mundo selegit Christus, Iohan. 15. ita eosdem à mundo separatos & sibi soli consecratos esse vult. In quem finem ingenuam ab ipsis fidei confessionem requirit, & sacramentis instruit, quibus à reliquis discernantur. Licet enim sacramenta beneficiorum Christi & diuinae gratiae non vulgaria symbola & sigilla sint, hic tamen non exiguus illorum quoque vsus est, quòd Dei populum à mundo secernunt, & externo communionis Christianae vinculo constringunt. Quae causa est, quòd Petrus supra, vbi baptizari voluit credentes, mox etiam admonet, vt à generatione prava Iudaeorum sese conferuent. Et Paulus simili argumento indignum esse docet, vt idolorum sacris communicent, qui dominicae mensae consortes facti sunt. Arguitur hic obiter illorum error, qui fidei confessionem inter indifferentia numerant, nec aliqua exteriori nota fideles à mundo discernendos esse arbitrantur.
units.tr: Moreover, to the inner joining, which consists in faith, there is added also an outward bond of fellowship. For it is said that all of them together, men as well as women, were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. For just as Christ chose his own out of the world, John 15, so he wishes them to be separated from the world and consecrated to himself alone. To this end he requires an open confession of faith from them and furnishes them with sacraments by which they may be distinguished from the rest. For although the sacraments are not common signs and seals of the benefits of Christ and of divine grace, nevertheless their use here is not small, in that they set the people of God apart from the world and bind them with the outward bond of Christian fellowship. This is why Peter above, when he wished those who believed to be baptized, soon also urges them to keep themselves from the perverse generation of the Jews. And Paul by a similar argument teaches that it is unworthy for those who have been made partakers of the Lord's table to share in the rites of idols. Here, in passing, their error is refuted, who count the confession of faith among matters of indifference and think that the faithful need not be distinguished from the world by any outward mark.

units.la: Simul etiam Anabaptistarum delirium hic excutiendum est, qui hoc loco & similibus, vbi fidem baptismo priorem fuisse vident, paruulorum baptismum damnari contendunt. Atqui hic de adultis sermo est, qui hactenus à Dei populo prorsus alieni fuerunt: quos absq; fidei confessione in ecclesiae & sacramentorum communionem recipere nefas fuisset, ne canibus & porcis margaritas proiecisse viderentur. Longè alia verò infantium ratio est, qui cum ex Christianis parentibus progeniti sint, ad Dei regnum non ambiguo iure pertinent. In foedere enim Deus, se seminis quoq; nostri Deum fore pollicetur. Gen. 17. Et Christus regnum coelorum ad pueros pertinere, & eosdem fidem habere, palam testatur. Matth. 18. & 19. Quid, quòd Paulus eos liberos, qui ex alterutro tantùm parente Christiano enati sunt, sanctos esse dicit? 1. Cor. 7.
units.tr: At the same time, the madness of the Anabaptists must also be shaken off here, who, from this place and similar ones where they see faith to have come before baptism, contend that the baptism of infants is to be condemned. Yet here the discussion concerns adults, who until now have been wholly foreign to the people of God; to receive them into the communion of the church and of the sacraments without a confession of faith would have been wrong, lest they seem to have thrown pearls to dogs and pigs. But the situation of infants is quite different: since they are born of Christian parents, they belong to the kingdom of God by an unambiguous right. For in the covenant God promises that he will be the God of our seed also. Gen. 17. And Christ openly testifies that the kingdom of heaven belongs to children, and that they have faith. Matt. 18 and 19. What of the fact that Paul calls children sanctified, those who are born of only one Christian parent? 1 Cor. 7.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Porrò ad Simonem redit Lucas, vt quid ille fecerit intelligamus, vbi populum abs se deficere, & Christo certatim nomina dare vidit. Et primò quidem illum credidisse dicit. Id non de mera simulatione mihi exponendum esse videtur. Nam animum eius aliquo fidei sensu tactum & perculsum fuisse, inde patet, quòd indiuulsus Philippo comes factus, visis miraculis & eximijs spiritus sancti operibus, obstupuit.
