units.tr: Let us now pass to the other part of this passage, by which we are taught how we may become partakers of, or capable of receiving, the salvation which is had in Christ. Peter sets this forth with great weight of words, saying: "To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives remission of sins through his name." Here the individual points must be distinguished, so that this doctrine, which is especially necessary, may have greater clarity. For first, indicating the fruit of those things which have been explained so far, he teaches that the remission of sins comes to us in the name of Christ. But while he mentions this, he testifies not obscurely that we are sinners, for whom it is needed. And when he teaches that it is conferred in Christ, he makes it gratuitous, something that comes apart from our merit by the mere grace of God; so that here you may plainly hear that saying of Paul: "All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, but they are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus," etc. Rom. 3. And to this must be referred what we said above about the expiation of sins made on the altar of the cross. For there the Son of God was made sin for us, so that we might be made the righteousness of God through him. 2 Cor. 5. By this statement the religions of all other sects are overthrown. For since Peter shows that remission of sins is in the name of Christ alone, he teaches that all those who seek it outside him labour in vain; and thus by a new argument he confirms that weighty sentence by which he testified before the Jerusalem senate that there is no other name under heaven given to men in which they can be saved. Christ himself affirms the same when he says: "I am the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me." John 14.

units.la: Fide peccatorum remissio percipitur.
units.tr: Remission of sins is received by faith.

units.la: Secundo medium, quo peccatorum remissio per Christum oblata, apprehenditur, Petrus hac sententia indicat. Hac enim potiri ait omnem, qui in illum crediderit. Fide ergo peccatorum remissionem consequimur. Cuius dogmatis ea ratio est, quod sola fides nos Christo inserit, ipso dicente: Qui edit meam carnem & sanguinem meum bibit (id est, quisquis in me credit) in me manet, & ego in illo. Et quia ex gratuita Dei promissione peccatorum remissio dependet, ea non aliter quam fide percipi potest. Ea enim Christum, qualis in euangelio proponitur, arripit, & promissioni diuinae toto animo innititur. Quae causa est, quod ipse Christus pastim fidei nostrae salutem tribuit, & nusquam non vniuersalem illam sententiam inculcat: Qui credit in me, habet vitam aeternam. Item: Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Marc.16. Et mulieri: Magna est fides tua, fiat tibi sicut vis. Matth.15. Et rursum: Fides tua saluam te fecit. Matth.9. Atqui hinc suum illud dogma sumpsea sumpserunt apostoli, quo sola fide in Iesum Christum homines iustificari, id est, peccatis liberari & absolui docent. Quo dogmate operum iustificatio plane excluditur. Nam cum hoc (ut modo demonstratum est) in uno Christo habeatur, qui non aliter quam fide a nobis percipi potest, sola hac nos iustificari necesse est. Nec ideo bonorum operum studium damnamus, sed insolentem meriti & iustificationis titulum, cuius gloria uni Christo debetur, illis detrahimus, ut Christo sua gloria salva maneat. Alioqui non ignoramus, summo iure ab illis iustitiae & innocentiae studium requiri, quos Iesus Christus sanguinis sui merito ablutos in libertatem filiorum Dei asseruit.
units.tr: Second, Peter indicates by this statement the means by which the remission of sins offered through Christ is grasped. For he says that everyone who believes in him obtains it. Therefore we obtain the remission of sins by faith. The reason for this doctrine is that faith alone joins us to Christ, Christ himself saying: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood (that is, whoever believes in me) abides in me, and I in him. And because the remission of sins depends on God's free promise, it can be received in no other way than by faith. For faith lays hold of Christ as he is set forth in the gospel, and rests wholly upon the divine promise. This is why Christ himself ascribes the salvation of our faith to faith alone, and everywhere presses that universal saying: Whoever believes in me has eternal life. Likewise: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved. Mark 16. And to the woman: Great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish. Matt. 15. And again: Your faith has saved you. Matt. 9. Yet from this the apostles drew their own doctrine, that men are justified by faith alone in Jesus Christ, that is, are freed and absolved from sins. By this doctrine the justification of works is plainly excluded. For since (as has just been shown) this is had in Christ alone, who can be received by us in no other way than by faith, we must be justified by this faith alone. Nor on this account do we condemn the pursuit of good works, but we strip from them the arrogant title of merit and justification, whose glory is due to Christ alone, so that Christ's glory may remain safe. Otherwise we are not unaware that the pursuit of righteousness and innocence is rightly required of those whom Jesus Christ, washed by the merit of his blood, has asserted into the freedom of the sons of God.

units.la: Caeterum, quia paulo ante apostolorum testimonijs doctrinam suam confirmarat Petrus, ne quis inter hos collusionem esse diceret, graviori authoritate causam hanc tueatur, dum omnes prophetas hoc ipsum de Christo testari docet. Nec dubium est, quin in recitandis illorum testimonijs aliquandiu versatus sit, quae tamen Lucas (cui satis fuit summa brevitatis studio omisit. At perquam facile est ex prophetarum scriptis probare, quod hoc loco Petrus dicit. Nam ut a Mose exordiamur, nec tamen primas promissiones producamus, ille Abrahamum Deo credidisse, & fidem illi ad iustitiam imputatam fuisse scribit. Genes. 15. At non aliam Abrahami fidem fuisse constat, quam qua semen illud expectavit, in quo omnes gentes benedici oportebat. Genes. 22. Et Christus Iesus hunc in suum diem respexisse, & in eo exultavisse, dicit. Iohan. 8. Idem Moses legales typos proponit, quos omnes Christi umbras fuisse, nemo negabit, qui vel una ad Hebraeos epistolam non osciter perlegerit. Et Paulus non obscure fidei iustificationem ex Psalm. 32. probat. Rom. 4. De Isaia quid dicere attinet, cum illius testimonium paulo ante audiverimus, & idem hoc quoque addat, Cognitione sui multos iustificabit iustus servus meus, quorum iniquitates ipse baiulabit? Isa. 53. Et Ieremias de Christo salvatore loquens, ait: Hoc erit nomen eius, quo vocabunt eum: DOMINVS IVSTITIA NOSTRA. Ierem. 23. Omitto infinita alia, quae adduci poterant, ne prolixior fit oratio, & praestat studiosis haec inquirendi occasionem relinquere. Interim observemus, Petrum non alijs quam prophetarum & apostolorum testimonijs niti. Unde discimus qui nam consensus & quorum hominum authoritas in fide & religionis causa valere debeat. Eorum videlicet, quos ex spiritu sancto locutos fuisse constat. Sunt hi, quorum ministerio veteris & novi Testamenti libros Deus conscribi voluit. Si quid ergo borum doctrinae contrarium producitur, id ex hominibus profectum sciamus, quorum traditiones iam olim Dei sententia ingulatae sunt. Isa. 29. Matth. 15.
units.tr: Moreover, because Peter had shortly before confirmed his teaching by the testimonies of the apostles, lest anyone say that there is collusion among them, he defends this cause with greater authority, while he teaches that all the prophets bear witness to this very thing about Christ. There is no doubt that he dwelt for some time on reciting their testimonies, which Luke, to whom it was enough to be brief, nevertheless omitted. Yet it is exceedingly easy to prove from the prophetic writings what Peter says in this place. For, to begin with Moses, without bringing forward the first promises, he writes that Abraham believed God, and that his faith was imputed to him for righteousness. Gen. 15. And it is clear that Abraham's faith was none other than that by which he looked for that seed in whom all nations ought to be blessed. Gen. 22. And Christ Jesus says that Abraham looked forward to his day and rejoiced in it. John 8. Moses also sets forth the legal types, all of which were shadows of Christ, as no one will deny who has read through even the one Epistle to the Hebrews with care. And Paul, not obscurely, proves justification by faith from Psalm 32. Rom. 4. What need is there to speak of Isaiah, since we have heard his testimony a little earlier, and he also adds this: By the knowledge of himself my righteous servant will justify many, bearing their iniquities? Isa. 53. And Jeremiah, speaking of Christ the Saviour, says: This will be his name by which they will call him: THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS. Jer. 23. I pass over countless other passages that could be adduced, so that the discourse may not grow too long, and it is better to leave the diligent an occasion of inquiring into them. Meanwhile let us observe that Peter relies on nothing but the testimonies of the prophets and apostles. From this we learn what consensus and whose authority ought to carry weight in matters of faith and religion: namely, of those who are known to have spoken by the Holy Spirit. These are the men through whose ministry God willed the books of the Old and New Testaments to be written. If, therefore, anything contrary to their teaching is brought forward, let us know that it has come from men, whose traditions God's sentence has long since condemned. Isa. 29. Matt. 15.

units.la: Habemus ergo celebrem & salutarem Petri concionem, qua primi ex gentibus ad Christi fidem conversi sunt. Continet haec, si probe examinetur, omnes fidei nostrae articulos de Deo patre, filio Iesu Christo, & spiritu sancto. Complectitur eadem absolutam humanae salutis rationem, quae ut in Christo proponitur, ita sola fide in hunc percipi potest. Quae cum Dei donum sit, hunc nos precibus assiduis fatigare decet, ut Christo Iesu vere insiti, eiusque merito iustificati, salvemur. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: We have, then, Peter's famous and saving sermon, by which the first of the Gentiles were converted to the faith of Christ. This contains, if it is carefully examined, all the articles of our faith concerning God the Father, the Son Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit. The same sermon embraces the complete plan of human salvation, which, as it is set forth in Christ, so it can be received in him by faith alone. Since this is a gift of God, it becomes us to beseech him with constant prayers that, truly grafted into Christ Jesus and justified by his merit, we may be saved. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXVII.

units.la: Adhuc loquente Petro verba haec, cecidit spiritus sanctus super omnes, qui audiebant sermonem. Et obstupuerunt qui ex circumcisione erant fideles, quotquot venerant cum Petro, quod etiam super gentes donum spiritus sancti effusum esset. Audiebant enim eos loquentes linguis, & magnifice laudantes Deum. Tunc respondit Petrus: Nunquid aquam prohibere quis potest, quo minus baptizentur hi, qui spiritum sanctum acceperunt sicuti & nos? Et iussit eos baptizari in nomine Domini. Tunc rogarunt ipsum, ut maneret dies aliquot.
units.tr: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were listening to the sermon. The believers of the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out upon the Gentiles. For they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered: "Can anyone forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?" And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they asked him to stay for some days.

units.la: Vt Deus pater omnem humanae salutis rationem in filio suo, Iesu Christo, concluffit: ita eundem non unius modo populi, sed communem omnium gentium salvatorem & redemptorem esse voluit. Cuius rei non obscura argumenta tum ex primis promissionibus & prophetarum oraculis, tum ex ultimo Christi mandato colligi possunt, quo apostolos ad praedicandum euangelium in totum terrarum orbem emisit.Quia tamen Iudæi,legis & legalium ceremoniarum prærogatiua elati,reliquas gentes fastidire solebant,nec in ecclesiam recipere dignabantur, nisi & circuncisionem & alias eius generis purificationes suscepissent:peculiari demonstratione opus fuit,quæ legis maceriam in Christo dirutam esse, & Dei gratiam gentibus quoque absque legis iustitia offerri doceret. Eam itaque in præsenti historia luculentissimam spiritus sanctus proponit.Vt enim Cornelio,homini gentili & incircunciso, angelum submittere,& Petrum cœlesti visione ad hunc instituendum Deus excitare dignatus est: ita eidem Petrus apostolus,dictante spiritu sancto,omnem salutis rationem mira & compendiosa simplicitate prædicat, & nulla legalium ceremoniarum mentione facta, Iesum Christum nobis à Deo destinatum esse docet,in quo peccatorum remissio omnibus credentibus obtingat. Ceterum ne quis Petrum hac liberius & incosulte nimis effutiuisse putaret,hoc ipsum rei exitus testatur, quem vel hoc nomine Lucas diligentissime describit,vt nos quoque ad diligentiorem tanta rei consyderationem excitet.
units.tr: Just as God the Father has enclosed the whole plan of human salvation in his Son, Jesus Christ, so he willed that the same Christ should be the common Saviour and Redeemer, not of one people only, but of all nations. The clear proofs of this can be gathered both from the first promises and the oracles of the prophets, and from Christ's last command, by which he sent the apostles out to preach the gospel to the whole world. Yet because the Jews, puffed up by the privilege of the law and its legal ceremonies, were accustomed to despise the other nations and did not deign to receive them into the Church unless they had also taken on circumcision and other purifications of that kind, there was need of a special demonstration, one that would teach that the wall of the law had been broken down in Christ, and that God's grace is offered to the Gentiles too, without the righteousness of the law. The Holy Spirit therefore sets forth this most clearly in the present history. Just as God deigned to send an angel to Cornelius, a Gentile and uncircumcised man, and to stir up Peter by a heavenly vision to instruct him, so the apostle Peter, under the dictation of the Holy Spirit, preaches the whole plan of salvation with wonderful and concise simplicity, and, without any mention of legal ceremonies, teaches that Jesus Christ, appointed by God for us, is the one in whom forgiveness of sins is granted to all believers. Lest anyone think that Peter spoke too freely and rashly in these matters, the outcome of the event itself bears witness to it, and Luke describes this outcome very carefully for this very reason, so that it may also stir us to a more careful consideration of so great a matter.

units.la: I. Petri doctrina spiritus sancti missione obsignatur.
units.tr: I. Peter's teaching is confirmed by the mission of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Principio autem adhuc loquente Petro,spiritus sanctus delapsus esse dicitur super omnes,qui salutis doctrinam audiebant.Et paulo post,diuersis linguis locuti esse,& Dei gratiam magnifice prædicauisse dicuntur. Idem ergo hic factum est,quod in die pentecostes apostolis euenerat: voluit, Deus visibili spiritus sancti missione Petri doctrinam, quam Cornelius & sui cum fide amplexi fuerant, confirmare,ac reipsa testari,salutis gratiam æque communem esse omnibus credentibus ( siue illiex Iudæis , siue ex gentibus fuerint) nec posthac legalium ceremoniarum obseruationem exigi debere. Patet vero,solenne hoc apostolorum tempore fuisse, vt euangelij prædicationi visibilis spiritus sancti missio coniungeretur , qua eos Deus dignabatur, qui illi credidissent. Quo argumento Paulus fidei iustificationem contra eos asserit,qui operum legalium obseruatione homines iustificari contendebant.Ait enim: Hoc solum cupio discere à vobis : vtrum ex operibus legis spiritum accepistis,an ex prædicatione fidei? Adeò stulti estis,cum spiritu cœperitis,nunc carne consummamini? Qui igitur subministrat vobis spiritum,& operatur virtutes in vobis, vtrum ex operibus legis,an ex prædicatione fidei id facit? Galat. 3. Nobis vero euangelicæ prædicationis dignitas & efficacia,hoc loco consideranda venit. Hanc enim organum Dei esse videmus, quo spiritum suum Deus largiri, & in hominum animis efficaciter operari consueuit: vt non temere Paulus, euangelium dicat potentiam Dei esse ad salutem omni credenti. Rom. 1. Idemq; hac de causa euangelij præcones , spiritus ministros vocauit.2. Cor. 3. Licet enim non omnibus,qui bodie euangelium audiunt,linguarum donum conferatur,& reliqua quoque dona,quæ in ecclesia ad Irenæi tempora vsque & deinceps floruisse constat,maxima ex parte cessarint:constat tamen adoptionis & regenerationis spiritu omnes eos donari, quicunque euangelium rite audiunt & fide amplexantur, in quo clamant, Abba pater,& quem salutis nostræ arrhabonem Paulus vocat. 2. Cor. 1. & 5.&c. Nec obscuri sunt eius effectus, dum in credentibus carnem cum membris suis terrestribus mortificat,homines regenerat,mentem illuminat,& facit vt in Christo omnia possint,qui nullis naturæ viribus ad bonum instructi sunt vel idonei.Vnde rursum colligimus, pro Christi membris minimè agnoscendos esse,in quibus nulli spiritus sancti effectus elucent.Nec enim otiosus est & iners spiritus ille.Et Paulus Christi eos esse negat,quicunque spiritu ipsius destituti fuerint. Rom. 8.
units.tr: At the beginning, while Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit is said to have come down upon all who were hearing the teaching of salvation. And shortly afterwards they are said to have spoken in various tongues and to have proclaimed the grace of God magnificently. So what happened here is the same as what had happened to the apostles on the day of Pentecost. God willed, by a visible mission of the Holy Spirit, to confirm the teaching of Peter, which Cornelius and his people had embraced in faith, and to attest in fact that the grace of salvation is equally common to all believers (whether they are from the Jews or from the Gentiles), and that from then on the observance of legal ceremonies ought not to be required. It is clear that it was the custom in the time of the apostles for the visible mission of the Holy Spirit to be joined to the preaching of the gospel, by which God deigned to honour those who had believed it. By this argument Paul asserts justification by faith against those who contended that men are justified by keeping the works of the law. For he says: "This only I want to learn from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the preaching of faith? Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being made perfect in the flesh? Therefore, does he who supplies you with the Spirit and works miracles among you do so by the works of the law, or by the preaching of faith?" Gal. 3. But for us, the dignity and efficacy of evangelical preaching come into consideration here. For we see that this is the instrument by which God is accustomed to bestow his Spirit and to work effectively in the minds of men. So it is not without reason that Paul calls the gospel "the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes." Rom. 1. For this same reason he also called the heralds of the gospel "ministers of the Spirit." 2 Cor. 3. For although the gift of tongues is not given to all who hear the gospel today, and although the other gifts too, which are known to have flourished in the Church up to the time of Irenaeus and afterwards, have for the most part ceased, it is nevertheless certain that all who hear the gospel rightly and embrace it in faith are endowed with the Spirit of adoption and regeneration, by which they cry, "Abba, Father," and which Paul calls the pledge of our salvation. 2 Cor. 1 and 5, etc. Nor are its effects obscure, when in believers it mortifies the flesh with its earthly members, regenerates men, enlightens the mind, and makes them able to do all things in Christ, who by no powers of nature are equipped or fit for any good. Hence we gather again that those in whom no effects of the Holy Spirit shine forth are by no means to be acknowledged as members of Christ. For that Spirit is not idle and inactive. And Paul denies that they are Christ's who have been deprived of his Spirit. Rom. 8.

units.la: Præterea,quæ nam post acceptum spiritum sanctum exercitia sint vere credentium,locus hic admonet. Linguis nouis & peregrinis illi loquuntur: quod licet (vt modo diximus) non omnibus contingat, omnium tamen credentium linguas spiritus sanctus formare solet, vt ea loquantur,quæ gloriæ Dei illustranda,& aliorum ædificationi seruiunt: de quo supra cap. 2. abunde dictum est.De inde Deum magnificè prædicauisse dicuntur.Faciunt hoc,quicunque gratiam Dei, quam is nobis in Christo offert,vere agnoscunt: cum è contra seipsos prædicent,quicunque suis operibus sese iustificari & saluari credunt. Estq; hæc gratiarum actio,sacrificium Deo gratissimum,quod & ipse frequenter exigit,& sanctis passim vouent. Nam huc pertinet, quòd iuuencos labiorum suorum apud propheram pollicentur.Hos.14.De hoc Dauid loquens,ait: Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus,quæ in me contulit?Sumpto calice gratiarum actionis,pro accepta salute nomen Domini vocabo. Meas vota exoluam Domino nunc coram vniuersa populo ipsius. Psal. 116. Et idem hoc Deo gratius fore testatur,quàm si quis illi bouem,cornibus & vngulis insignem offerret.Psal.69.Docent hæc,quid de inide ingratis & improbis verbi Dei conuiciatoribus iudicemus, quibus volupe est illud virulenta lin gua rabie lacessere, & publicarum calamitatum causam dicere, in quo salutarem Dei gratiam agno scere & celebrare debebant.
units.tr: Moreover, this passage points out what the exercises of truly believing people are after they have received the Holy Spirit. They speak in new and foreign tongues. Although (as we have just said) this does not happen to everyone, the Holy Spirit does customarily form in all believers a tongue to speak those things which serve to make the glory of God shine forth and to build up others. This was dealt with at length above in chapter 2. Next, they are said to have proclaimed God magnificently. Those do this who truly acknowledge the grace of God which he offers us in Christ, whereas on the contrary those proclaim themselves who believe that they are justified and saved by their own works. This thanksgiving is also a sacrifice most pleasing to God, which he himself frequently requires and which the saints everywhere vow. For to this belongs what the prophet says, that they will offer the calves of their lips. Hos. 14. Speaking of this, David says: "What shall I render to the Lord for all the benefits he has bestowed on me? I will take up the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord for the salvation I have received. I will pay my vows to the Lord now in the presence of all his people." Ps. 116. And he testifies that this is more pleasing to God than if someone were to offer him an ox marked with horns and hooves. Ps. 69. These things teach us what we should think of the ungrateful and wicked revilers of the word of God, who delight to assail it with venomous tongue and rage, and to blame the cause of public calamities, when they ought rather to acknowledge and celebrate God's saving grace concerning ungrateful and wicked revilers of God's word, who delight to assail it with venomous tongue and rage, and to blame the cause of public calamities, when they ought rather to acknowledge and celebrate in it God's saving grace.

units.la: Porrò videamus, vt miraculo hoc affecti fuerint spectatores. Inter quos fuere aliquot ex Iu daeis oriundi, qui Petrum ex Ioppe descendentem comitati fuerant. Illos obstupuisse Lucas ait, eò quòd spiritus sancti donum super gentes quoq; effusum viderent. Licet enim ignorare non possent, quae Petro acciderant, adhuc tamen illos communis ille Iudaeorum error dementat, qui omnes gentes prophanas & à Deo alienas esse censebant, nisi circuncisione & reliquis caeremoniis initiatae ad Iudaismum transirent. Est autem cumprimis memorabile, quòd qui fideles dicuntur, tam crasso errore laborant. Hinc enim patet, in sanctis etiam errorum labes interdum haerere, & proinde non quiduis temere in exemplum trahi debere, quod illos fecisse legimus. Quod Paulum obseruauisse con stat, qui Corinthios sui exempli imitatores esse iubet, quatenus illum Christi imitatorem esse videat. 1. Cor. 11. Nihil enim tam humanum est, quàm errare & falli. Nec aliud perinde laboriosum & difficile est, quàm inueteratos errores hominum animis eximere: cuius rei exemplum cap. 1. in apostolis ad carnalis & terreni regni expectationem subinde impingentibus, vidimus. Vehementer ergo errant, quicunq; assiduam doctrinam & admonitiones superuacaneas & inutiles esse clamant: cum ea sit humani ingenij caecitas simul & pertinacia, vt vndiquaq; offendiculi occasionem arripiat, difficil lime autem in viam reuocetur. Quare prudentius multò Paulus sensit, quando Timotheum opportune simul & importune instare iubet. 2. Tim. 4.
units.tr: Furthermore, let us see how the spectators were affected by this miracle. Among them were some of Jewish origin, who had accompanied Peter when he came down from Joppa. Luke says that they were astonished because they saw that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out upon the Gentiles too. For although they could not be ignorant of what had happened to Peter, that common error of the Jews still deluded them, the error which held that all the nations were profane and alien from God, unless they passed over to Judaism by being circumcised and initiated in the other ceremonies. It is especially worth noting that those who are called believers were labouring under such a gross error. For from this it is clear that even in the saints some stain of error sometimes sticks, and therefore that we ought not rashly to take as an example whatever we read that they did. Paul is known to have observed this, when he bids the Corinthians to be his imitators, in so far as he is seen to be an imitator of Christ. 1 Cor. 11. For nothing is so human as to err and be deceived. And nothing else is equally laborious and difficult as to remove deep-rooted errors from men's minds. We saw an example of this in chapter 1, where the apostles kept stumbling again and again into the expectation of a carnal and earthly kingdom. Therefore those are gravely mistaken who cry out that constant teaching and admonitions are superfluous and useless, since the blindness and obstinacy of the human mind is such that it seizes on any occasion of offence from every side, and is most difficult to bring back to the right way. So Paul showed much greater prudence when he bade Timothy to press on both in season and out of season. 2 Tim. 4.

units.la: Caeterum vt ad historiae expositionem redeamus, longè rectius Petrus sentit, qui ex anteactis miraculi finem agnoscit. Quia enim coelesti visione ad Cornelium descendere, & illi euangelium praedicare iussus erat, nunc verò spiritus donum audientibus & credentibus collatum esse videt: facilè agnoscit, gentibus quoq; communem esse euangelij gratiam, & in ecclesiae communionem incircuncisos quoq; (si in Christum credant) recipi debere, quando illos spiritus sui dono Deus dignetur. Nam ab ipsa re ad signum argumentum ducens ait: Nunquid aquam prohibere quis potest, quò minus baptizentur hi, qui spiritum sanctum acceperunt sicuti & nos? Quod perinde est, ac si dixisset: Quotquot Christi membra sunt, eos per baptismum in ecclesiae Christi communionem suscipi conuenit. At hos Christi membra esse, nemo dubitare potest, cum spiritū Christi perinde vt nos acceperint. Aequum ergo, vt baptismum accipiant. Nec mora, eos in nomine Domini baptizari, id est, Christo Domino consecrari, & ecclesiae huius accenseri iubet. Non enim de forma baptismi, sed eius potius fine & vsu Petri mandatum intelligi debet.
units.tr: But to return to the explanation of the history: Peter judges far more rightly, since from the events that preceded he recognises the outcome of the miracle. For since he had been commanded by a heavenly vision to go down to Cornelius and preach the gospel to him, and now sees that the gift of the Spirit has been bestowed on those who listen and believe, he readily recognises that the grace of the gospel is common to the Gentiles too, and that the uncircumcised too, if they believe in Christ, ought to be received into the fellowship of the Church, since God deigns to honour them with the gift of his Spirit. For drawing the sign-argument from the thing itself, he says: "Can anyone forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?" This is as much as to say: "All who are members of Christ ought to be received through baptism into the fellowship of Christ's Church. But no one can doubt that these are members of Christ, since they have received the Spirit of Christ just as we have. Therefore it is right that they receive baptism." And without delay he commands that they be baptized in the name of the Lord, that is, consecrated to Christ the Lord and counted among this Church. For the command must be understood not as concerning the form of baptism, but rather its purpose and use.

units.la: Ex his verò vniuersam baptismi rationem colligere facillimum fuerit. Petrus certè hunc initiale populi Dei & ecclesiae sacramentum esse agnoscit, quo extrinsecus obsignantur regenerationis & adoptionis beneficia, & quaecunq; alia eius generis nobis in Christo obtigerunt, simulq; officij admonentur, quicunq; istorum conscrites facti sunt. Vnde colligimus, hunc omnibus deberi, quosqunque ex populi Dei conciuibus esse constat. Confutantur hic multiplices errores, quos circa baptismum iam saeculi aliquot irrepsisse, & hodie passim regnare videmus. Et primò quidem prophanos sacramentorum contemptores locus iste arguit, qui haec credentibus & per fidem regeneratis superuacanea esse censent. Quod hominum genus, dum fidem & gratiam Dei magnificè praedicat, Dei sapientiam & constitutiones improbè contemnit. Atqui Cornelius cum suis vere credere, & eosdem spiritu sancto donatos, & proinde in filiorum Dei numerum adoptatos esse Petrus videbat. Idem tamen illos baptizare iubet, ne Christi mandatum contempsisse videretur. Cur enim Christi sacramenta contemneret, qui in veteri Testamento capitis poenam sacramentorum contemptoribus constituta fuisse nouerat? Deinde Anabaptistarum audaciam locus hic confutat, qui Christianorum infantes à baptismo arcere consueuerunt. Atqui Petrus non alio argumento bos baptizandos esse probat, quàm quòd spiritu Christi donatos, & proinde ecclesiae eius membra esse videret. Cur ergo non eodem iure infantes baptizarentur, quos ecclesiae membra nasci scimus, & quos ad Dei regnum pertinere, Christus ipse testatur? Marc. 10. Praeterea Papistarum errori huius loci exemplum repugnat, qui gratiam Dei sacramentis alligare, eamq; exorcismis quibusdam elicere & in illa transfundere solent: cum illa gratia Dei, quae in Christo confertur, tesseras & signacula esse constet. Et si hunc locum examines, idem in Cornelio, quod olim in Abrahamo contigisse patebit, ut eandem omnino in utroque Testamento sacramentorum rationem videas. Nam Abrahamum fide iustificatum fuisse, & postea demum circuncisionem, quae iustitiae fidei sigillum erat, accepisse, Paulus testatur Rom. 4. Ita Cornelium credidisse, & spiritu Christi donatu fuisse audiuimus, quod infallibile erat regenerationis simul & iustificationis argumentum: at nunc demum baptismus, quo haec tanta Dei beneficia obsignetur, accedit. Minime ergo baptismi sacramento Dei gratiam alligari, nec illam per hoc ceu canalem in nos transfundi constat: quando illa si abfq; fide vsurpentur, prorsus superuacanea, imo suis contemptoribus noxia esse scimus, quod in Iudae proditoris & Simonis Magi exemplis euidentissime cernitur.
units.tr: From these things it will be very easy to gather the whole account of baptism. Peter certainly acknowledges it to be the initiatory sacrament of the people of God and of the Church, by which the benefits of regeneration and adoption, and whatever other such blessings have fallen to us in Christ, are outwardly sealed, and by which those who have become fellow citizens of these people are reminded of their duty. Hence we gather that it is owed to all who are known to be fellow citizens of the people of God. Several errors are refuted here, which we see have crept in concerning baptism for some centuries and are now everywhere prevalent. First of all, this passage rebukes the profane despisers of the sacraments, who judge them superfluous for believers who have been regenerated through faith. This kind of men, while they loudly proclaim faith and the grace of God, wickedly despise the wisdom and ordinances of God. Yet Peter saw that Cornelius and his people truly believed, had been endowed with the Holy Spirit, and therefore had been adopted into the number of the sons of God. Nevertheless he orders them to be baptized, lest he seem to have despised Christ's command. For why would he despise Christ's sacraments, who knew that in the Old Testament the penalty of death had been laid down for the despisers of the sacraments? Next, this passage refutes the audacity of the Anabaptists, who are accustomed to keep the infants of Christians from baptism. Yet Peter proves that these men are to be baptized by no other argument than that he saw them endowed with the Spirit of Christ and therefore members of his Church. Why then should infants not be baptized by the same right, since we know they are born members of the Church, and Christ himself testifies that they belong to the kingdom of God? Mark 10. Moreover, the example in this passage is contrary to the error of the Papists, who are accustomed to tie the grace of God to the sacraments and to draw it out by certain exorcisms and pour it into them, although that grace of God which is conferred in Christ is known to be a token and seal. And if you examine this passage, it will be clear that what once happened in Abraham also happened in Cornelius, so that you may see the same plan of the sacraments in both Testaments. For Paul testifies in Romans 4 that Abraham was justified by faith and only afterwards received circumcision, which was the seal of the righteousness of faith. So we have heard that Cornelius believed and was endowed with the Spirit of Christ, which was an infallible proof of regeneration and at the same time of justification; but only now does baptism, by which these great benefits of God are sealed, follow. It is therefore plain that the grace of God is in no way tied to the sacrament of baptism, nor is it poured into us through it as through a channel, since we know that if these things are received without faith they are utterly superfluous and even harmful to their despisers, as is most clearly seen in the examples of Judas the traitor and Simon Magus.

units.la: Priusquam vero hinc discedamus, iustificationis & salutis ordinem in Cornelij exemplo obseruare praestat. Hunc Dei gratia excitatum simul & aduitum fuisse vidimus, ut faceret quae Deo grata & accepta erant, cum gentilis hucusq; & a populo Dei alienus fuisset. At in gratiam recepto doctor destinatur Petrus apostolus, qui salutis doctrinam praedicet. Verbo praedicato credit Cornelius. Fidem spiritus sanctus comitatur, qui & animum totum regenerat, & mirificas praeterea virtutes exerit. Hoc illuminatus in Dei laudes totus effunditur, & tandem baptismo accepto inter Christi ecclesiae cives numeratur. Hunc ordinem passim obseruatum videmus. A Dei gratia enim nostrae salutis initium est, qui elegit nos priusquam mundi fundamenta iacerentur. Ephes. 1. Is electos per verbum externum erudit, fide donat, spiritu suo regeneratos illuminat, & ad omne opus bonum idoneos reddit. Et quod verbo pollicetur & fideli menti per spiritum suum offert, idipsum externis quoque sacramentis obsignat. Vide Rom. 9. & 10. cap.
units.tr: Before we depart from here, however, it is worth observing the order of justification and salvation in the example of Cornelius. We have seen that he was stirred up and made ready by the grace of God so that he might do what was pleasing and acceptable to God, although until then he had been a Gentile and alien from the people of God. But once he was received into grace, the apostle Peter is appointed as teacher to proclaim the doctrine of salvation. Cornelius believes the preached word. The Holy Spirit accompanies the faith, who both regenerates the whole mind and moreover displays wonderful powers. Enlightened by this, he is wholly poured out in praise of God, and at last, having received baptism, he is numbered among the citizens of Christ's Church. We see this order observed everywhere. For the beginning of our salvation is from the grace of God, who chose us before the foundations of the world were laid. Ephesians 1. He instructs the elect through the external word, grants them faith, enlightens them regenerated by his own Spirit, and makes them fit for every good work. And what he promises in the word and offers to the faithful mind through his Spirit, he also seals by the external sacraments. See Romans chapters 9 and 10.

units.la: Postremo, qualem se post omnia ista Cornelius gesserit, indicatur. Rogarunt Petrum (inquit Lucas) ut maneret dies aliquot. At non alia huius desiderij causa esse potuit, quam quod euangelij amore incensi, quotidie docentem audire cupiuerunt, quo solidior in ipsis efficeretur verae salutis cognitio. Adhaec non tam cito satiari poterant hominis amicissimi praesentia, quem sibi tantae gratiae ministrum & dispensatorem fuisse senserant. Hic vero ingenium vere credentium exprimitur. Non fastidiunt illi verbi doctrinam, nec tantum sibi tribuunt, ut illam sibi posthac superuacaneam esse putet. Imo se homines esse norunt, & quia Dei filij haberi volunt, patris voce exatiari non possunt, sed hic indesinenter sibi loquente audire cupiunt. Ioban. 8. Praeterea gratos & amicos erga Dei ministros sese praebent, quorum opera in fide & salutis causa instituuntur. Nec enim magni momenti rem putant, si carnalia illis beneficia rependant, qui ipsis spiritualium bonorum authores sunt. Abhis enim maxima ex parte salutem suam pendere intelligunt. Quae causa est, ut increpari etiam & obiurgari sese patiantur, quod in Dauide & Ezechia esse videre. At longe alia impiorum mens est, qui mini stros verbi, impiorum suorum studiorum interturbatores, tanquam publicos hostes odisse consueuerunt: cuius rei exemplum in Pharaone, Achabo, Pharisaeis & infinitis aliis scriptura proponit. Quorum impietas meretur, ut ultricem iusti Dei manum sentiant, qui fideles admonitiones ferre noluerunt. Agnoscamus ergo nos Dei gratiam, & verbum eius gratis animis amplexi, in illud transformari studeamus, ut olim promissae salutis consortes & heredes reddamur per Iesum Christum saluatorem nostrum: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Lastly, it is shown what manner of man Cornelius became after all these things. They asked Peter (says Luke) to stay for some days. Yet there could be no other cause of this desire than that, inflamed with love of the gospel, they longed to hear him teaching every day, so that the knowledge of true salvation might become more solid in them. Besides, they could not so quickly be satisfied with the presence of a most dear man, whom they had perceived to be the minister and steward of so great a grace. Here indeed the character of truly believing people is expressed. They do not scorn the teaching of the word, nor do they think so highly of themselves that they consider it superfluous from now on. Rather, they know that they are men, and because they wish to be regarded as sons of God, they cannot be satiated with the voice of the Father, but desire to hear him speaking to them without ceasing. John 8. Moreover, they show themselves grateful and friendly toward the ministers of God, through whose work they are instructed in faith and in the cause of salvation. Nor do they think it a matter of great importance if they repay carnal benefits to those who are the authors of spiritual goods for them. For they understand that their salvation depends for the most part on these men. This is why they also allow themselves to be rebuked and reproved, as we see in David and Hezekiah. But the mind of the wicked is far different: they are accustomed to hate the ministers of the word, the disturbers of their impious pursuits, as public enemies. Scripture sets before us an example of this in Pharaoh, Ahab, the Pharisees and countless others. Their impiety deserves that they feel the avenging hand of the righteous God, since they were unwilling to bear faithful admonitions. Let us therefore acknowledge the grace of God, and embrace his word with thankful minds, and strive to be transformed into it, so that we may be made partakers and heirs of the salvation promised of old, through Jesus Christ our Saviour, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: CAPUT XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXVIII.

units.la: Audiuerunt autem apostoli & fratres, qui in Iudaea erant, quod gentes quoque recepissent verbum Dei: & cum Petrus ascendisset Hierosolymam, disceptabant aduersus eum, qui erant ex circuncisione, dicentes: Ad viros praeputium habentes ingressus es, & comedisti cum illis. Exorsus autem Petrus, expositi illis ordine, dicens: Ego eram in urbe Ioppe, orans, & vidi in raptu mentis visionem: nempe, descendens vas quoddam ceu linteum magnum, quatuor initijs demissum e coelo, & venit usque ad me. In quod cum intendissem oculos, animaduerti & vidi quadrupedia terræ, & feras, & reptilia, & volatilia cœli. Audiui autem vocem dicentem mihi: Surge Petre, macta & vescere. Dicebam autem: Nequaquam domine, quia nihil vnquam commune vel immundum introiuit in os meum. Respondit autem mihi vox secundo, è cœlo: Quæ Deus mundauit, tu ne communia dixeris. Hoc autem accidit tertio, & rursum omnia subducta sunt in cœlum. Et ecce subito tres viri astiterunt ad domum, in qua agebam, è Cæsarea ad me missi. Dixit autem mihi spiritus, vt cum illis proficisceret, nihil hæsitans. Me vero comitati sunt & hi sex fratres. Et ingressi sumus domum viri, qui retulit nobis, quomodo vidisset angelum domi suæ, stantem & dicentem sibi: Mitte viros Ioppen, & accerse Simonem, cognomento Petrum, qui tibi loquetur verba, per quæ seruaberis tu & tota domus tua. Cum autem exordus esse loqui, de lapsus est spiritus sanctus in eos, sicut & in nos principio. Recordatus autem sum verbi domini, quomodo dixisset: Iohannes quidem baptizauit aqua, vos autem baptizabimini spiritu sancto. Si ergo par donum dedit illis deus, sicut & nobis, qui credidimus in dominum Iesum Christum: ego porro quis eram, qui possem prohibere Deum?
units.tr: The apostles and brethren who were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God. When Peter went up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision contended with him, saying, "You went in to men uncircumcised and ate with them." But Peter began and explained the matter to them in order, saying: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance of mind I saw a vision: a certain vessel, like a great sheet, let down by four corners from heaven, and it came down to me. When I fixed my eyes on it, I considered and saw four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and birds of the air. And I heard a voice saying to me, 'Rise, Peter; kill and eat.' But I said, 'Not so, Lord, for nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.' A voice answered me a second time from heaven: 'What God has cleansed, do not call common.' This happened a third time, and again all things were drawn up into heaven. And behold, at once three men stood before the house where I was, sent to me from Caesarea. The Spirit told me to go with them without hesitation. These six brethren also went with me. We entered the man's house, and he told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, who said to him: 'Send men to Joppa and call for Simon, who is called Peter; he will speak to you words by which you and all your household will be saved.' As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as on us at the beginning. Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said, 'John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.' If therefore God gave them the same gift as he gave us, who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?"

units.la: Vanquam Diuus Lucas Cornelij ad fidem conuersi historiam in præcedenti cap. copiose & diligenter descripserit, eandem tamen hoc capite, mutata narratione figura repetit. Cuius instituti causa est, vt omnibus pateat, gentes diuino plane consilio per euangelij prædicationem vocatas, & baptismi sacramento in ecclesiæ communionem assumptas esse. Necessariam vero fuisse demonstrationem hanc propter Iudæos, sæpe iam dictum est. Sed & nobis eadem non mediocriter feruit, dum hac & diuinæ bonitatis gratia mirifice illustratur, & omnium nostrum (qui ex gentibus oriundi sumus) salutis certitudo constantissime asseritur. Nemo igitur diuinum scriptorem vel tautologiæ vel ineptæ loquacitatis accusare debet: sed potius illius diligentia ad attentam tantæ rei consyderationem excitari. Porro eandem historiam repetendi occasionem ex iniquis quorundam iudicijs Lucas sumit, qui præcipiti iudicio decepti, Petrum accusarunt, quæ causa fuit, vt illi facti sui rationem reddere coactus fuit.
units.tr: Although St. Luke described in detail and diligently the history of Cornelius's conversion to the faith in the preceding chapter, he nevertheless repeats the same account in this chapter, with the narrative changed in form. The reason for this design is that it may be plain to all that the Gentiles were called by the clear counsel of God through the preaching of the gospel, and were received into the fellowship of the Church by the sacrament of baptism. That this demonstration was necessary on account of the Jews has often been said already. But it is also of no small concern to us, since by it the grace of divine goodness is wonderfully illustrated, and the certainty of salvation for all of us who are descended from the Gentiles is most firmly asserted. Therefore no one ought to accuse the divine writer of tautology or of foolish wordiness, but rather be stirred up by his diligence to a careful consideration of so great a matter. Moreover, Luke takes the occasion for repeating the same history from the unjust judgments of certain men, who, deceived by hasty judgment, accused Peter; this was the reason why he was compelled to give an account of his action.

units.la: Videamus igitur primo loco, vt de gentium vocatione ecclesia, quæ per Iudæam hinc inde differ a erat, iudicarit. Nec enim diu latere potuit factum hoc, tum propter personarum illustrem dignitatem, tum quod per se nouum erat & insolens. Mox ergo eius famam in Iudæa diuulgatam fuisse tradit. Hic autem duo sese produnt hominum genera. Primum apostolorum & fratrum est, quo nomine verbi ministros & Symmystas potissimum hic designari puto. De his hoc vnum euangelista, quod audierint gentes quoq; recepisse verbum dei, nec quicquam præterea addit. Vnde conijci potest, ipsos etsi facti huius mysterium nondum plane intelligerent, Christianæ tamen modestiæ memores, noluisse Petrum apostolum, cuius fides & diligentia multis argumentis perspecta erat, præcipiti iudicio carpere aut accusare. Quorum modestiā nobis imitanda proponit spiritus sanctus: ne dum in alio factis dijudicandis inconsulto zelo abripimur, charitatis fraternæ leges violemus. Simul vero locutio obseruanda est, quaे gentes verbum dei recepisse dicuntur, cum illas Christianismi suscepisse, aut in Christi & ecclesiæ partes transfuisse dicere possent. Ita enim plus quiddam dicere, & verum Christianismum a fucata quorundam simulatione distinguere voluit. Verbum Dei enim recipere dicuntur, qui illud Dei verbum esse agnoscunt, & proinde in illud transformari & ipsius Dei imitatores fieri studeant. Sic Paulus Thessalonicenses verbum recepisse scribit, quando scribit: Cum accepistis sermonem a nobis, quo deum discebatis, accepistis non sermonem hominum, sed sicut erat vere, sermonem Dei. 1. Thess. 2. Item. Et vos imitatores nostri facti fuistis & domini, recipientes sermonem cum afflictione multa, &c. 1. Thess. 1. Qui hoc pacto Dei verbum recipiunt, mirificos ex eo fructus proferunt. Nam seipsos abnegantes & carnis affectus mortificantes, priština impietatis studia deserunt, & tanquam lucis filij pietati & innocentiæ studeant. Sciunt enim Deum lucem esse, & in luce ambulandum esse, qui cum illo communionem habere cupiunt. 1. Iohan. 2. Et in hac consyderatione
units.tr: Let us see, then, first of all, how the Church, which was scattered here and there through Judaea, judged the calling of the Gentiles. For this matter could not long remain hidden, both because of the distinguished dignity of the persons involved and because the thing was in itself new and unusual. Accordingly, Luke relates that its report was soon spread abroad in Judaea. Two kinds of men reveal themselves here. The first is that of the apostles and brethren, by which name I think the ministers of the Word and fellow-workers are chiefly designated here. Of these the evangelist says only this one thing, that they heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God, and adds nothing more. From this it may be conjectured that, although they did not yet fully understand the mystery of this event, yet, mindful of Christian modesty, they were unwilling to attack or accuse Peter the apostle, whose faith and diligence had been proven by many arguments, with hasty judgment. The Holy Spirit sets their moderation before us to imitate, so that while we are carried away by misguided zeal to judge the deeds of another, we do not violate the laws of brotherly love. At the same time, the manner of speaking must be noted: that the Gentiles are said to have received the word of God, when one could say they had taken up Christianity, or had passed over to the side of Christ and the Church. For the Spirit wished to say something more, and to distinguish true Christianity from the counterfeit pretence of certain people. For those are said to receive the word of God who acknowledge it to be the word of God, and therefore strive to be transformed into it and to become imitators of God himself. So Paul writes that the Thessalonians received the word, when he writes: "When you received from us the word of God's message, you accepted it not as the word of men, but, as it truly is, the word of God" (1 Thess. 2). Likewise: "And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction, etc." (1 Thess. 1). Those who receive the word of God in this way bring forth wonderful fruits from it. For, denying themselves and mortifying the desires of the flesh, they abandon their former pursuits of impiety, and as sons of light they pursue godliness and innocence. For those who desire to have fellowship with God know that God is light, and that one must walk in the light (1 John 2). And in this consideration

units.la: C
units.tr: C

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Vt de Petri facto iudicarit ecclesia.
units.tr: How the Church judged Peter's deed.

units.la: Recipere verbum Dei quid. frequenter eos versari conuenit, qui euangelij nomine gloriantur, ne dum Dei verbum sese recepisse plenis buccis vociferantur, mendacij seipsos arguant, quando nullos verbi dei fructus proferunt.
units.tr: It is worth considering often those who boast of the name of the gospel. While they shout with full mouths that they have received the word of God, they convict themselves of lying when they produce no fruit of that word.

units.la: Sed ad alterum hominum genus transseamus, qui minus aequi tam praeclari facti, quod Petrus ediderat, iudices fuerunt. Hos ex circuncisione fuisse Lucas ait. At cum priores quoque circuncisi & Iudaei fuerint, non simpliciter hic Iudaeorum gentem, sed eos potius denotari puto, qui cum Christiani haberi vellent, circuncisioni tamen & legalibus ceremoniis, tanquam necessarijs ad salutem, pertinacius inhaerebant. Hos Petri factum audacius reprehendisse, adeoque cum illo palam disceptauisse, Lucas scribit. Et hoc illi ceu capitale quoddam crimen obijciunt, quod ad viros praeputium habentes, id est, ad gentiles sive ethnicos ingressus fit, & cum illis comederit. Ita enim violata maiorum traditionis & consuetudinis illorum accusant, cuius originem ex lege Dei, arbitrus nonnihil strictA, manauisse alibi diximus. Admonemur autem horum exemplo, quam noxium sit erroribus semel imbui, & in illis consenescere. Fere enim contumax quidam errorem defendendi ardor accedit, dum pro humani ingenij natura, nemo videri vult errauisse. Quo malo hi quoque excaecati fuisse videntur, dum gentibus ne nunc quidem in ecclesia locum permittere volunt, quas tamen luculento dei testimonio receptas esse constabat. Tanta tamen pertinax est humani ingenij corruptio, tamque inuita in eorum ribus semel suscepti defendendis contumacia. Atqui vtinam non hodie infinita passim eius generis exempla extarent in ijs hominibus qui cum primas in ecclesia teneant, pro leuiculo ducunt ea tuerì, quae diserti diuini verbi oraculis contraria esse noverunt.
units.tr: But let us pass to the other kind of men, who were less fair judges of the very notable deed Peter had performed. Luke says these were from the circumcision. But since the former were also circumcised and Jews, I think that here not simply the Jewish nation is meant, but rather those who, although they wished to be regarded as Christians, clung more stubbornly to circumcision and the legal ceremonies as necessary to salvation. Luke writes that these men rebuked Peter's deed rather boldly and disputed openly with him. They charge him with this as if it were a capital crime: that he went in to men having foreskins, that is, to Gentiles or heathen, and ate with them. For they accuse him of violating the traditions and customs of their ancestors, whose origin I have said elsewhere flowed, not without some strictness, from the law of God. We are warned by their example how harmful it is to be steeped in errors and to grow old in them. For a certain stubborn ardour for defending error usually accompanies this, since by the nature of the human mind no one wishes to seem to have erred. These men too seem to have been blinded by this evil, since they still wish to allow no place in the Church for Gentiles, whom it was nevertheless plain had been received by a clear testimony of God. Such is the stubborn corruption of the human mind, and such unwilling obstinacy in defending what has once been taken up. Yet would that today there were not countless examples of this kind everywhere among those who hold the first places in the Church, who think it a trifling matter to uphold things they know to be contrary to the plain oracles of the divine word.

units.la: Praeterea docet locus hic, neminem tam feliciter tamque pie res administrare posse, ut omnibus satisfaciat. Ea potius mundi huius conditio est, ut accusationem & vituperium reportent, qui laudem merebantur. Hoc olim Mosi accidisse tum inter Aegyptios tum inter Israelitas, scriptura docet. Idem prophetas expertos fuisse legimus, qui dum pro publica salute inuigilant, regni turbatores, patriae hostes & publicorum malorum authores dicti sunt. Nec aliud de Christo Iesu mundi iudicium fuisse constat. Modo enim propter neglectam manuum ablutionem, modo propter conuersationem cum peccatoribus accusatur: mox rursus sabbati violatorem, & paulo post Samaritanum & daemoniacum esse clamant. Eandem ergo nunc cum praeceptore suo sortem Petrus sustinet, & cum exi mia laude dignus esset ob regnum Christi ad gentes usque tam feliciter propagatum, calumniatorum potius venenatos morsus experitur. Nec manifestos modo Christiani nominis hostes, verum etiam eos factij suiinequissimos censores habet, qui & Christiani & fratres dici volebant. Quid? quod discipuli in praeceptorem censoriam virgulam arripiunt? Debet horum consyderatio nos patientes reddere, si quid simile nobis quoque accidat. Simul vero admoneat, ut studia nostra deo potius quam mun do approbare curemus, qui & benefactoribus suis plerunque ingratus est, & iudicio suo vt plurimum fallitur. Rursus discamus ingens hoc peccatum esse, si quae bene a fratribus gesta sunt improbe calumniemur. Nam qui id faciunt, satanae ingenium referunt, quem Graeci diabolum dixere, quod omnia nostra calumniari & obliquis iudicijs perstringere soleat. Et charitatis leges violant, cuius est nunquam non benesperare de fratribus, & peccatorum multitudinem tegere potius quam traducere. 1. Cor. 13. Prouerb. 10. 1. Pet. 4.
units.tr: Moreover, this passage teaches that no one can administer affairs so happily and so piously as to satisfy everyone. Rather, this is the condition of this world: those who deserve praise bring back accusation and reproach. Scripture teaches that this happened to Moses, both among the Egyptians and among the Israelites. We read that the prophets too experienced it; while they watched over the public safety, they were called disturbers of the kingdom, enemies of the fatherland and authors of public evils. Nor is it clear that the world's judgment about Christ Jesus was any different. At one time he is accused on account of neglected washing of hands, at another on account of his association with sinners; soon they cry that he is a violator of the sabbath, and shortly after that he is a Samaritan and demon-possessed. Therefore Peter now undergoes the same lot as his teacher. Although he deserved exceptional praise for the kingdom of Christ propagated so happily even to the Gentiles, he experiences instead the poisonous bites of slanderers. He has not only open enemies of the Christian name, but also censors of his deed most wicked, who wished to be called both Christians and brothers. What then? Do the disciples seize the censor's rod against their teacher? The consideration of these things ought to make us patient if anything similar happens to us. At the same time it admonishes us to take care to commend our endeavours to God rather than to the world, which is both often ungrateful to its benefactors and most often mistaken in its judgment. Again, let us learn that it is a great sin if we wickedly slander what brothers have done well. Those who do this bear the character of Satan, whom the Greeks called diabolos, because he is wont to slander all our doings and to pierce them with crooked judgments. They also violate the laws of charity, whose part is never to despair of brothers, and to cover the multitude of sins rather than to expose them. 1 Cor. 13. Prov. 10. 1 Pet. 4.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Caeterum iniquae morosissimorum hominum criminationi Petri apologia, omnis amarulentia expers subijcitur: cuius haec summa & hic vnicus scopus est, nihil hic priuato consilio, sed dei iussu omnia facta esse, qui gentes in Christi & ecclesiae sua communionem susciperi voluerit. Quia vero exacerbatos nimium videbat aduersariorum animos, diligentem rerum gestarum, ab ipso principio repetitam narrationem contexit, eamque argumentis solidissimis confirmat. Quam priusquam attingamus, apostoli modestia inspicienda erit, qui tam humili & solicita excusatione apud eos vti voluit, quae causae bonitate fretus, vel contemnere & responso dedignari, vel saltem asperius repellere & increpare poterat. Sed agnoscit ad se quoque eam legem pertinere, qua ipse Christianos ad reddendam mutationem quibusque semper paratos esse iubet. 1. Pet. 3. Et hoc loco in optima causa iniquam morosorum hominum censuram patienter fert: ita cum a Paulo ob simulationem & constantiam coram omnibus reprehenderetur, nihil illum insolentius respondisse legimus. Gal. 2. Atqui semper tam in ecclesia veteri consuetudinem fuisse cernimus, ut episcopi ab episcopis sese iudicari et corrigi paterentur. Ita Victorem Romam, episcopum ob praecipitem aduersus Asiae episcopos excommunicationis sententiam. tentiam ab Irenæo & alijs quibusdam minus celebrium ecclesiarum episcopus, reprehensum & ossi-cij admonitum fuisse, constat. Arguunt hæc Romanorum Pontificum, qui postea secuti sunt, infolen-tiam. Quos non pudet, sese totius orbis iudices constituere, & vicissim omnium hominum iudicia detrectare. Horret animus, quoties blasphemi illius Canonis recordor, quo ne tunc quidem Papa iudicari vult, fi suæ simul & aliorum fa'utis negligens, hominum animas caterua tim ad inferos deducat. At non alio argumento euidentius sese Antichristum esse probare poterat, quàm quòd ecclesiæ & episcoporum omnium censuram reijcit, cùm in ecclesia & inter episcopos primum locum sibi vendicet. SED omisso hoc, Petrum causam suam perorantem audiamus.
units.tr: Moreover, Peter's defence is set against the unjust accusation of these very captious men, and it is entirely free of bitterness. Its sum and sole aim is that nothing here was done by private counsel, but everything by God's command, who wished the Gentiles to be received into communion with Christ and his Church. But since he saw that the minds of his adversaries were too much inflamed, he set out a careful account of events, repeated from the very beginning, and confirms it with most solid arguments. Before we touch on it, the apostle's moderation must be noticed. He chose to use such a humble and careful excuse towards them, when, relying on the goodness of his cause, he could have despised them and disdained to answer, or at least repelled and rebuked them more sharply. But he acknowledges that the law applies to himself too, by which he bids Christians always be ready to give an account to everyone. 1 Pet. 3. And here, in a very good cause, he patiently bears the unjust censure of captious men. Thus when Paul rebuked him in public before everyone for hypocrisy and inconstancy, we read that he answered nothing more insolently. Gal. 2. Yet we see that in the ancient Church it was always the custom for bishops to allow themselves to be judged and corrected by bishops. Thus it is established that Victor, bishop of Rome, was rebuked and admonished of his duty by Irenaeus and some other bishops of less famous churches, because he had rashly pronounced a sentence of excommunication against the bishops of Asia. These things expose the arrogance of the Roman pontiffs who came later. They are not ashamed to make themselves judges of the whole world, and in turn to refuse the judgments of all men. My mind shudders whenever I recall that blasphemous canon by which the Pope does not wish to be judged even then, even if, neglecting both his own salvation and that of others, he drives men's souls headlong to hell. But he could not have proved himself Antichrist more clearly than by rejecting the censure of the Church and of all bishops, while claiming the first place for himself in the Church and among the bishops. BUT, leaving this aside, let us hear Peter pleading his cause.

units.la: Habet vero ipsius defensio diligentem (vt modò diximus) narrationem, quam ita instituit, vt non obiter modò quid factum fit commemoret, sed illud ipsum recte & legitime factum esse doceat: funtq; narrationis huius partes quinq;, de quibus singulis paucula, quæ ad præfentem causam pertinent, dicemus, omissis ijs, quæ in præcedenti Capite tractata sunt.
units.tr: Peter's defence contains, as we have just said, a careful narrative, which he arranged so that it does not merely mention in passing what was done, but teaches that it was done rightly and lawfully. The parts of this narrative are five. I shall say a few things about each that pertain to the present cause, leaving aside those treated in the preceding chapter.

units.la: Prima parte visionem vasis fiue lintei magni, cœlitus ad fe demissi, comprehendit: quà illum à domino edoctum fuisse diximus, nemine posthac propter legis ceremonias neglectas euangelio & populi Dei communione indignum censeri debere, cùm in Christo Iesu legis maceria diruta fit, vtq; ex vtroq; populus vnum fecerit. Ephef. 2. Voluit autem hinc narrandi initium facere Petrus, vt omnibus pateret, nihil abs fe priuato consilio factum, sed omne hoc diuinæ administrationis opus fuisse.
units.tr: In the first part he records the vision of the vessel or great sheet let down to him from heaven. As we said, by it he was taught by the Lord that no one should henceforth be deemed unworthy of the gospel and of communion with God's people on account of neglected legal ceremonies, since in Christ Jesus the dividing wall of the law has been broken down, and so he has made both peoples one. Eph. 2. Peter wished to begin his narrative here, so that it would be clear to all that nothing was done by his private counsel, but that this whole work was a divine administration.

units.la: Secunda parte certum dei mandatum allegat, ne somnio aliquo aut inani spectro deceptus fuisse videretur. Nam eo ipso temporis momento, non fine diuina prouidentia duƈtu, foribus hospitij fui missos à Cornelio legatos astitisse ait, & addit: Dixit mihi spiritus, vt cum illis proficiscerer, nihil hæ-fitans. Atqui hic totius apologiæ nerus est, quem directe aduersariorum criminationi opponi vide-mus. Illi enim dixerunt: Ad viros præputium habentes ingressus es, & comedisti cum eis. Respon-det ergo hic Petrus: Spiritus domini me hoc facere iussit. Et hac verborum simplicitate contentus, oratorios colores facile intermittit, quibus argumentum hoc ornare & confirmare potuisset. Quo ex-emplo docemur, minimè accusandos esse, vel si accusentur facile defendi posse apud Christianos homi-nes, quicunq; à receptis consuetudinibus & hominum traditionibus ex dei præscripto discedunt. Æter-na enim & inuiolabilis esse debet apostolica huius sententiæ authoritas. Oportet deo potius obedire quàm hominibus. Hac ergo ratione nos hodie etiam contra Papistas tueamur, qui simili morositate ob violatas à nobis hominum traditiones nos accusant, & offendiculi ansam, nobis quoque non præ-bentibus, vndiquaque arripiunt. Offendit illos, quòd Christum in altaris sacramento pro viuorum & mortuorum peccatis offerri negamus. At nos Christi verbum opponimus, qui in cruce expiratus, peccatorum expiationem omnemq; nostræ redemptionis rationem iam consummatam esse testatus est. Adhæc Paulum audimus, qui Christum semel oblatum, amplius immolari posse negat. Of-fenduntur, quòd Christi & sanctorum imagines templis nostris eiectas vident. At nos dei authorita-tem illis obtendimus, qui imagines fieri prohibet, & factas delere ac euertere iubet. Offenduntur pro-pter sublata à nobis ciborum discrimina. Sed nos apostolus tuetur, qui dæmoniorum dogma esse dicit, il-la obtrudere. Eadem est omnium aliorum, quæ inter nos controuertuntur, ratio. Hæc enim tantum-modo exempli gratia produximus. Quòd si vero nostri illi aduersarij dei verbo cedere noluerint, sed illius authoritati hominum consensus & traditiones opponere perrexerint: facile patebit, illos non Christi, sed hominum seruos esse, &c.
units.tr: In the second part he cites a certain command of God, lest he should seem to have been deceived by some dream or empty apparition. For at that very moment, he says, not without the guidance of divine providence, the men sent by Cornelius stood at the doors of the house, and he adds: The Spirit told me to go with them, doubting nothing. Indeed, this is the sinew of the whole defence, and we see it is directly set against the accusation of his adversaries. For they said: You went in to men having foreskins, and ate with them. Peter answers: The Spirit of the Lord bade me do this. Content with this simplicity of words, he readily leaves aside the rhetorical colours with which he could have adorned and confirmed the argument. By this example we are taught that those who depart from received customs and human traditions in accordance with God's prescription are by no means to be accused, or, if they are accused, can easily be defended among Christian people. For the apostolic authority of this sentence ought to be eternal and inviolable: we must obey God rather than men. Therefore let us today defend ourselves in this way even against the Papists, who with like captiousness accuse us of violating human traditions, and on every side seize on any occasion of offence, though we give them none. They are offended that we deny that Christ is offered in the sacrament of the altar for the sins of the living and the dead. But we set against them the word of Christ, who, expiring on the cross, testified that the expiation of sins and the whole reason of our redemption is now complete. Besides, we hear Paul, who denies that Christ, once offered, can be sacrificed again. They are offended that they see the images of Christ and the saints cast out of our temples. But we oppose to them the authority of God, who forbids images to be made and orders those made to be destroyed and overthrown. They are offended by the distinctions of foods which we have abolished. But the apostle defends us, who says that it is a doctrine of demons to impose such things. The reasoning is the same for all the other matters disputed between us, for we have brought forward these only by way of example. But if those adversaries of ours refuse to yield to the word of God, and persist in opposing the consent and traditions of men to its authority, it will readily be clear that they are servants not of Christ but of men, etc.

units.la: Tertia narrationis pars angeli apparitionem continet, quæ Cornelio diuinitus submissum fuisse audiuimus. Huius autem meminisse voluit Petrus, vt doceret, ne ipsum quidem Cornelium quic-quam temere fecisse, sed à Deo excitatum fuisse, vt se doctorem accesseret. Hic vero obseruatione di-gnum est, vt de euangelij ministerio siue prædicatione angelus loquatur. Petrus (inquit) loquetur tibi verba, per quæ seruetur tu & tota domus tua. Salutem ergo per euangelium hominibus obtin-gere testatur. Vidit hoc ipsum diuinus Psaltes, quando ait: Misit Deus verbum suum, & sanauit eos. Psal. 107. Et Paulus euangelium potentiam Dei esse ait, ad salutem omni credenti. Dicuntur autem hæc, non quòd verborum sonus salutem afferat, quod de exorcismis suis superstitiosi sentiunt: sed quòd euangelij prædicatione Christus nobis offertur, & qui illud prædicant, Christi nomine lega-tionem obeunt, vt illorum ministerio homines Deo patri per Christum reconcilientur. 2. Cor. 5. Nulla ergo vel rebusspub. vel familijs salus aut solida felicitas continget, nisi euangelium Iesu Christi receperint. Execrabilis itaq; est illorum ingratitudo, qui salutis verbum tam priuatorum quàm publicorum malorum causam esse dicunt, quod olim Ieremiæ etiam obiectum fuisse legimus. Ierem. 44. Agitantur isti homines Caiaphæ spiritu, qui & ipse Christum excidij authorem fore dicebat, nisi nefaria sacerdotum coniuratione opprimeretur.
units.tr: The third part of the narrative contains the appearance of the angel, which we have heard was sent by God to Cornelius. Peter wished to mention this, to show that not even Cornelius himself had done anything rashly, but that he had been roused by God to seek out a teacher. Here it is worth noting that the angel speaks of the ministry of the gospel, or of preaching: "Peter," he says, "will speak to you words by which you and all your household will be saved." He therefore testifies that salvation comes to men through the gospel. The divine Psalmist saw this very thing when he says: "He sent his word and healed them" (Ps. 107). And Paul says that the gospel is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes. These things are said not because the sound of the words brings salvation, as the superstitious think of their exorcisms, but because Christ is offered to us in the preaching of the gospel, and those who preach it discharge an embassy in Christ's name, so that through their ministry men may be reconciled to God the Father through Christ (2 Cor. 5). Therefore no welfare of commonwealths or households, and no lasting happiness, will come unless they receive the gospel of Jesus Christ. Detestable, then, is the ingratitude of those who say that the word of salvation is the cause of evils, both private and public, as we read was once objected to Jeremiah (Jer. 44). Those men are driven by the spirit of Caiaphas, who also himself said that Christ would be the author of the destruction of the nation unless he were crushed by the wicked conspiracy of the priests.

units.la: Quarto loco miraculosam spiritus sancti missionem refert. Eius vero interpretem allegat, Iesum Christum. Recordatus sum (ait) verbi domini, quomodo dixisset: Iohannes quidem baptizauit aqua, vos autem baptizabimini spiritu sancto. Ita vero argumentari videtur Petrus: Christus dominus electiis suis spiritum pollicitus est, quem mundus hic capere non potest, & huius quidem largitorem se solum fore dixit. Hunc ergo cum in gentes ipse effuderit, easq; spiritu suo baptizare dignatus sit, ego tanti ducis exemplum non potui non sequi, nec aquæ baptismo indignos iudicare debui, quos spiritu suo dignos esse Deus iudicauerat. Pulchrè autem inter ministrum & Christum Petrus distinguit, ne externo ministerio perperam tribuatur, quod solius Christi est. Quia tamen de hoc alibi diximus, id obiter in præsenti annotauisse sufficiat.
units.tr: In the fourth place he recounts the miraculous sending of the Holy Spirit. He cites as its interpreter Jesus Christ himself: "I remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said: John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit." Peter seems to reason in this way: Christ the Lord promised his elect the Spirit, whom the world here cannot receive, and he said that he alone would be the giver of it. Since he himself has therefore poured out this Spirit upon the Gentiles, and has deigned to baptize them with his Spirit, I could not but follow the example of so great a leader, nor ought I to judge unworthy of the baptism of water those whom God had judged worthy of his Spirit. Peter distinguishes well between the minister and Christ, so that what belongs to Christ alone is not wrongly attributed to external ministry. Yet since we have spoken of this elsewhere, it is enough to have noted it in passing here.

units.la: Quinta pars conclusionem habet verborum simul & argumentorum ponderegrauem. Ait enim: Si ergo par donum dedit illis Deus, sicut & nobis, qui credidimus in dominum Iesum Christum, ego porrò quis eram, qui possem prohibere Deum? Impium per se foret, impares dicere, quos Deus pares facere dignatus est. At quantò maior impietas foret, eos ab ecclesiæ communione arcere, quos ad illa pertinere Deus tam euidenti argumento docuit? imò quos ipse palam adoptauit? Fateturitaq; Petrus, se Dei aduersariu fieri oportuisse, si quid tale conari voluisset. Quòd si verò dei aduersarij sunt, qui quos Deus ecclesiæ suæ membra esse vult, hoc nomine ab illius communione arcent, quòd tanta gratia indignos censent: quid de illis dicemus, qui falsa doctrina Christi oues seducunt, aut in easdem ob Christi confessionem aperta ui & tyrannide grassantur? Sentient illi aliquando eius potentem & ultricem manum, cuius hostes potius quàm amici & sectatores esse malunt. Nostrum est, dei gratiam ita agnoscere & exosculari, vt simul quosuis alios in salutis commercium pertrahamus, quod electis suis proposuit deus pater in filio suo dilecto, Iesu Christo: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: The fifth part contains a conclusion of weighty words and arguments. For he says: "If then God gave them the same gift as he gave us, who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?" It would be impious in itself to call those unequal whom God has deigned to make equal. But how much greater impiety would it be to shut out from the communion of the Church those whom God has taught by so clear an argument to belong to it, indeed whom he himself has openly adopted? Peter therefore confesses that he would have had to become an opponent of God if he had attempted anything of the kind. But if those are opponents of God who, because they count them unworthy of so great a grace, keep from their communion those whom God wills to be members of his Church, what shall we say of those who lead Christ's sheep astray with false doctrine, or who rage against them with open violence and tyranny on account of their confession of Christ? They will one day feel the powerful and avenging hand of him whose enemies they prefer to be rather than his friends and followers. It is our duty so to acknowledge and embrace the grace of God that we at the same time draw any others whatever into the fellowship of salvation, which God the Father proposed to his elect in his beloved Son, Jesus Christ, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXIX.
units.tr: Homily 79.

units.la: Hæc verò cum audiuissent, quieuerunt & glorificauerunt Deum dicentes: Ergo & gentibus Deus pœnitentiam dedit ad vitam. Porrò, qui dispersi fuerant à tribulatione, quæ contigerat propter Stephanum, transierunt vsq; in Phœniciam, & Cyprum, & Antiochiam, nemini loquentes sermonem, nisi Iudæis solis. Erant autem ex ipsis quidã viri Cyprij & Cyrenei, qui ingressi Antiochiam, loquuti sunt Græcis: prædicantes dominum Iesum. Et erat manus domini cum illis, multusq; numerus cum credidisset conuersus est ad dominum.
units.tr: When they heard this, they fell silent and glorified God, saying: "So God has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles also." Meanwhile, those who had been scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen travelled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews. Some of them, however, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, came to Antioch and spoke to the Greeks, preaching the Lord Jesus. The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number who believed turned to the Lord.

units.la: Quemadmodum diuus Petrus in Cornelio conuertendo pij simul & fidelis apostoli officium est, dum diserto Dei mandato absq; omni tergiuersatione obtemperandum esse putauit: ita cum illius factum à quibusdam iniquius carperetur, præclarum Christianæ & apostolicæ modestiæ exemplum prebuit. Nam ijs facti sui rationem amicissimè & diligentissimè reddit, à quibus ipse maiori iure rationem exigere poterat. Omissis autem multis alijs argumentis, hoc vnum vrget, quòd nihil priuato consilio, sed ex Dei præscriptione & mandato omnia ista gesserit. Quo exemplo didicimus, quibus argumentis nos quoque aduersus eos pugnare debeamus, qui simili morositate nos ob violatas hominum traditiones & consuetudines hodie accusare consueuerunt. Sufficiat nobis diuini verbi authoritas, quam quicunque aspernari audent, indigni sunt, quorum aliqua habeatur ecclesia Christi ratio.
units.tr: Just as holy Peter acted with the devotion and fidelity of an apostle in converting Cornelius, when he judged that he must obey the clear command of God without any evasion, so when some criticised his action too harshly, he gave a notable example of Christian and apostolic modesty.
