Such schools existed among the ancient people in the cities of the Levites, and that the most excellent prophets of God had the chief care of them is clear from the histories of Samuel and Elisha. Indeed, the prophet Amos sharply accuses those who corrupted with wine the young men dedicated to sacred study, the Nazarites. The most powerful kings and emperors in the ancient Church saw this, and at their own expense they set up colleges, lest at any time a lack of teachers should bring loss to the Christian religion. But today these colleges are either occupied by idle drones or are subject to the lust of arrogant men, who are accustomed to hunt for ambitious titles rather than to care for the comfort of the churches.

units.la: Porrò ne eximij ecclesiæ Christi ministri digna laude fraudarentur, illorum nomina perpetuæ memoriæ spiritus sanctus consecrari voluit, vt certò constaret, nequaquam à Deo eos negligi, qui ecclesiæ fideli cura & studio inseruiunt. At inter hos Manaen cumprimis eminere videtur, quem cum Herode Tetrarcha à pueris enutritum & educatum fuisse, Lucas docet. Nobilis ergo & aulicus fuit. Quis enim obscuro genere natum regio puero adhibitum, aut eum postea ab Herode neglectum fuisse putaret, quo cum ab ineunte ætate consueuerat? Est hoc præclarum diuinæ bonitatis exemplum, quæ in quouis hominum genere electos suos habere, & vbi illi visum fuerit, vocare consueuit. Nam vbicunq; voluerit, spirat almus ille & cælestis vitæ author spiritus. Iohan.3. Sic in Syri regis aula Naaman fuisse legimus. Et in Babylone Daniel cum suis veri Dei cognitionem retinet. Quid? quòd Paulus eorum, qui in Neronis domo crediderunt, mentionem facit? Phil.4. Et inter scribas, acerrimos Christi hostes, Nicodemus numeratur. Simul verò fidei & syncerae pietatis exemplum in Manae nobis proponitur, qui Mosen secutus, potius cum populo Dei affligi, quàm temporarijs peccati commodis frui maluit, maiores nimirum arbitratus diuitias probrum Christi, quàm Herodis thesauros. Hebr.11. Et sane si ecclesiæ conditione, qualis illo tempore fuit, cum aulica vita conferas, mirificam in Manae hoc spiritus sancti operationem, & non obscura cum regenerationis vera, tum suipsius abnegationis & mortificationis argumenta deprehendes. At quod illum fecisse audimus, nos quoq; imitari conuenit. Nec enim fieri potest, vt Christum vere apprehendant, qui mundum hunc eiusq; honores, opes & voluptates nondum contemnere & conculcare didicerunt.
units.tr: Furthermore, lest the outstanding ministers of Christ's Church be defrauded of their due praise, the Holy Spirit wished their names to be consecrated to perpetual memory, so that it might be clearly established that God by no means neglects those who serve the Church with faithful care and zeal. Among these Manaen seems especially to stand out, whom Luke tells us was brought up and educated with Herod the tetrarch from boyhood. He was therefore noble and a courtier. For who would think that a man of obscure birth, admitted as a royal boy, and one who had from early age been accustomed to Herod, was afterwards neglected by him? This is a notable example of divine goodness, which is accustomed to have its chosen ones in every kind of men, and to call them when it pleases. For the life-giving Spirit, the author of heavenly life, breathes wherever he wills (John 3.). So we read that Naaman was in the court of the Syrian king; and in Babylon Daniel with his companions retained the knowledge of the true God. And what of the fact that Paul mentions those who believed in the household of Nero (Phil. 4.)? And among the scribes, the bitterest enemies of Christ, Nicodemus is numbered. At the same time, in Manaen a pattern of faith and sincere piety is set before us, for he, following Moses, preferred to suffer with the people of God rather than to enjoy the temporary pleasures of sin, judging, of course, the riches of Christ greater than the treasures of Herod (Heb. 11.). And indeed, if you compare the state of the Church at that time with the life of the court, you will detect in Manaen a remarkable working of the Holy Spirit, and clear proofs both of true regeneration and of self-denial and mortification. But what we hear he did, we too ought to imitate. For those cannot truly lay hold of Christ who have not yet learned to despise and trample underfoot this world, its honours, riches and pleasures.

units.la: Sed ad alteram huius loci partem transeamus, qua Pauli & Barnabæ missio ad gentes describitur. Hic autem duo potissimum excutienda sunt, nimirum totius negotij author & moderator spiritus: deinde modus, quem ab illis obseruatum fuisse Lucas tradit. Et authorem quidem totius negotij spiritum fuisse diserte docetur. Nam illis ministrantibus domino & ieiunantibus, dixit spiritus, Segregate mihi Barnabam & Saulum in opus, ad quod vocaui eos. Nec dubium est, de sancto spiritu ista dici, quando & ministerij sacri & ieiunij mentio fit. Ineptiunt hoc loco, Erasmum interpretem secuti Papistæ, & quia is sacrificandi verbo non minus inepte Græcam vocem reddidit, de Missæ sacrificio locum exponunt. At λειτουργὼν Græcis dicuntur, qui publicum aliquod munus obeunt, quod vel inde patet, quòd & magistratus & angeli à Paulo λειτουργοὶ dicuntur, non quòd sacrificent illi, sed quòd publici Dei ministri sint. Rom.13. Heb.1. Et quia in Christi morte Leuitica sacra abrogata esse constat, & Christianorum cultus non in externis ceremonijs, sed in spiritu & veritate consistit, non aliud ministerium hic intelligi potest, quàm quod Christus in ecclesia sua exercere voluit. Comprehendit hoc verbi prædicationem, publicas preces & Sacramenta, quæ non sacrificia, sed actiones sacræ sunt, in sacrificij per Christum in ara crucis semel oblati memoriam instituta. Et his quidem studijs occupati fuerunt feriò, quando de Pauli & Barnabæ missione illos spiritus admonuit. Seriò enim in his illos versatos fuisse, ieiunij mentio abunde docet. Insunt autem his multa, quæ gentium vocationem diuinum opus fuisse probant. Nam cum Domino publicè ministrarent, de hac spiritus ecclesiam admonuit. Deinde: Segregate (inquit) mihi Paulum & Barnabam. In Dei igitur ministerio fuerunt, quando gentibus prædicarunt. Accedit quod ait: In opus, ad quod ego vocaui eos. Faciunt hæc ad afferendam nostræ salutis certitudinem aduersus Iudæorum insolentem gloriationem, qui se solos Dei populum esse contendunt, & hinc in tentationibus argumenta petere possunt, quibus Christum ad nos quoque pertinere conscientijs ad desperationem vergentibus, persuaderi possit.
units.tr: But let us pass to the other part of this passage, in which the sending of Paul and Barnabas to the Gentiles is described. Here two things above all must be examined: first, that the Spirit was the author and governor of the whole business; and second, the manner which Luke relates they observed. And that the Spirit was the author of the whole matter is taught plainly. For while they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Spirit said: "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." Nor is there doubt that these words concern the Holy Spirit, since both the mention of sacred ministry and of fasting occurs. The Papists, following Erasmus the translator, talk nonsense here, and because he rendered the Greek word by the word "sacrificing" no less absurdly, they expound the passage about the sacrifice of the Mass. But those are called by the Greeks [λειτουργῶν] who perform some public office; this is clear enough from the fact that both magistrates and angels are called [λειτουργοί] by Paul, not because they offer sacrifice, but because they are public ministers of God (Rom. 13.; Heb. 1.). And since it is certain that the Levitical rites were abrogated by the death of Christ, and since Christian worship consists not in external ceremonies but in spirit and truth, no other ministry can be understood here than that which Christ wished to be exercised in his Church. This comprises the preaching of the Word, public prayers and the sacraments, which are not sacrifices but sacred actions, instituted in remembrance of the sacrifice once offered by Christ on the altar of the cross. And they were indeed busily occupied with these duties when the Spirit admonished them about the sending of Paul and Barnabas. For that they were seriously engaged in them, the mention of fasting abundantly shows. There are also many things in this which prove that the calling of the Gentiles was a divine work. For while they were publicly ministering to the Lord, the Spirit addressed the Church about this. Then he says: "Set apart for me Paul and Barnabas." They were therefore in God's service when they preached to the Gentiles. Add to this what he says: "For the work to which I have called them." These things serve to establish the certainty of our salvation against the arrogant boasting of the Jews, who contend that they alone are God's people; and in temptations, when consciences are sliding towards despair, from these things they can draw arguments by which Christ may be persuaded to pertain to us also.

units.la: Est autem hic nobis consideranda ministerij ratio, de qua nos iudicare locus iste docet. Author huius spiritus sanctus est, quemadmodum infra quoque cap. 10. patebit. Ut vero ex eo ministrorum dignitas elucet, ita liquido constat, pro legitimis ministris minime agnoscendos esse, nisi qui per spiritum vocati fuerint. Quomodo enim praedicabunt nisi missi fuerint? Rom. 10. Qua causa est, quod tam prophetae quam apostoli vocationem suam toties inculcant & constantissime afferunt. Nemo tamen vocem caelitus delatam semper expectet, qua ad ministerium vocentur homines. Diuinitus enim vocatos esse censebimus, quoscunque Dei spiritus donis necessarijs instruxerit, & legitimis ecclesiae suffragijs elegerit. Aliquas enim in hac causa partes ecclesiae mandatas esse, hic locus perspicue tradit. Quamvis enim spiritus sanctus diserte fateatur, se iam vocauisse duos hosce, & Paulus se ab utero matris ad hoc ministerium segregatum esse testetur, ecclesiae tamen calculum spiritus requirit. Atqui id hoc potissimum nomine factum esse non dubito, ut praesenti causae plus authoritatis accederet, quam multorum calumnijs expositam fore spiritus noverat. Interim tamen admonemur, ordine in ecclesia opus esse, tum in omnibus aliis rebus, cum maxime in ministrorum electione, ne quis sibi ipsi (ut apostolus ait) honorem usurpet. Hebr. 5. Quam enim id Deo displiceat, Coræ exemplo discimus, & multorum seculorum historijs, quibus probari potest, vix aliunde maiores in ecclesia turbas obortas esse, quam ex inordinata & illegitima ministrorum electione. Porro, ut ad ecclesiam ministrorum electio aliqua ex parte spectat: ita hanc in re maximi momenti summa cum religione versari conuenit. Quapropter hi denuo ieiunauisse & orauisse dicuntur. Atqui in personis falli non poterant, cum spiritus sanctus eos nominauisset, qui praesenti negotio destinari debebant. Orant tamen, ut spiritus incremento donentur, quos ad prouinciam laboris simul & periculi plenam vocari audiebant. Haec vtinam expenderent, qui inter pocula ministros eligere, & in re omnium grauissima affectibus, pessimis consultoribus, ita consuevuerunt. Quorum impietati maxima ex parte debemus, quicquid malorum hodie in ecclesia cernitur. Caeterum Antiocheni ipsi precibus solennem ceremoniam, manuum videlicet impositionem, subiungunt, quam externum consecrationis symbolum fuisse, supra diximus, vbi de Diaconorum institutione dictum est.
units.tr: Here we must consider the manner of the ministry, about which this passage teaches us to judge. The Holy Spirit is its author, as will also become clear below in chapter 10. Just as the dignity of the ministers shines forth from this, so it is clearly established that no one should be acknowledged as a lawful minister unless he has been called through the Spirit. For how shall they preach unless they are sent? Rom. 10. For this reason both the prophets and the apostles so often insist on their calling and assert it most steadfastly. Yet no one should always wait for a voice sent down from heaven by which men are called to the ministry. For we shall judge that those are called of God whom the Spirit of God has equipped with the necessary gifts and whom the lawful votes of the church have chosen. This passage plainly teaches that some part in this matter has been entrusted to the church. Although the Holy Spirit clearly declares that he had already called these two, and Paul testifies that he was set apart for this ministry from his mother's womb, the Spirit nevertheless requires the church's vote. I do not doubt that this was done chiefly so that the present matter would carry more authority, since the Spirit knew it would be exposed to the slanders of many. Meanwhile we are admonished that order is needed in the church, in all other matters but especially in the choice of ministers, so that no one takes honour to himself (as the apostle says). Heb. 5. How much God is displeased by this we learn from the example of Korah, and from the histories of many ages, by which it can be proved that greater disturbances have arisen in the church scarcely from any source than from disorderly and unlawful choice of ministers. Furthermore, since the election of ministers concerns the church in some measure, it is fitting that this matter of the greatest importance be handled with the utmost reverence. Hence these men are said to have fasted and prayed again. Yet they could not be mistaken about the persons, since the Holy Spirit had named those who were to be designated for the present task. They pray nonetheless that those whom they heard were being called to a province full of labour and danger may be granted an increase of the Spirit. Would that those who are accustomed to choose ministers over their cups, in the most weighty matter of all, and are guided by their passions, the worst advisers, would weigh this! To their impiety we owe for the most part whatever evils are seen today in the church. Moreover, the Antiochenes themselves add to their prayers the solemn ceremony of the laying on of hands, which, as we said above where we spoke of the institution of deacons, was an external sign of consecration.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Restat vltima huius loci pars, ut officio diuinitus simul & ab ecclesia sibi commisso Paulus & Barnabas fungi coeperint: quam ita superioribus connectit Lucas, ut illos abs omni mora iter ingressos fuisse pateat. Est hoc eximium sanctae industriae & diuini zeli argumentum. Quam multa enim praetexere potuerint, facile intelligunt, qui illius temporis historias vel obiter legerunt. Dominabantur tunc in toto pene orbe terrarum Romani, quos auitae superstitionis & veteris cultus abrogationem nunquam admissuros esse, non ignorabant. Sciebant item sibi cum gentium philosophis, astutissimis hominibus & in dicendo exercitatissimis, rem fore. Adhaec vulgi mores nouerant, quod veteres superstitiones plerunque ea pertinacia tuetur, ut vitam potius quam has amittere velit. Sed non obstant haec omnia, quo minus sese illico accingant, quaevis pericula & labores ferre parati. Horum vero industriam omnes eos imitari conuenit, qui in publicum aliquod munus a Deo constituti sunt, ut & sine mora Dei vocationi obtemperent, & in eadem constanter pergant. Nec enim ferre potest cunctatores & cergiuersatores dominus, qui summo iure omnia nostra sibi vendicat. Ideo Moses olim, officium detrectanti iratus fuisse dicitur. Exod. 3. & 4. Et Christus discipulo, qui patrem prius sepelire volebat, respondet: Sequere me, & sine, ut mortui sepeliant mortuos suos. Matth. 8. cap. Caeterum tria hic Lucas commemorat, de quibus singulis quaedam dicenda sunt.
units.tr: It remains the last part of this passage: that Paul and Barnabas began to discharge the office committed to them by God and by the church. Luke connects this with what goes before in such a way that it is clear they set out on their journey without any delay. This is a notable proof of holy diligence and divine zeal. Those who have read even briefly the histories of that time easily understand how many excuses they could have made. The Romans then ruled over almost the whole world, and they knew that the Romans would never allow the abolition of ancestral superstition and old worship. They knew too that they would have to deal with the philosophers of the Gentiles, most crafty men and very practised in speaking. Besides, they knew the customs of the common people, who usually defend old superstitions with such stubbornness that they would rather lose their lives than these. Yet none of these things prevented them from setting to work at once, ready to bear any dangers and labours. All those whom God has appointed to some public office ought to imitate their diligence, both by obeying God's calling without delay and by persevering constantly in it. For the Lord, who by the highest right claims all that is ours for himself, cannot tolerate laggards and shirkers. Therefore Moses of old is said to have been angered at one who refused the office. Exod. 3. and 4. And Christ answers the disciple who wished first to bury his father: Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead. Matt. 8. But Luke mentions three things here, and something must be said about each of them.

units.la: Primo, quo peruenerint docet. Seleuciam, quae non procul ab Antiochia distabat, profecti sunt, & inde ad Salaminem Cypri oppidum traiecerunt. Cypro autem inter omnes Mediterranei maris insulas primam fere felicitatis & opulentiae laudem veteres Geographi tribuunt. Inde vero ita apud Cyprios luxus & libido inualuit (sicuti nuper diximus) ut insula tota Veneri sacra esset, quae illorum suum habuisse ferebatur. Atqui vnum hoc satis docet, quanta in ea gente morum & totius vitae corruptio fuerit, quae sese totam cum sua terra Veneri consecrauerat. Quare non temere factum putabimus, quod ad hanc primum peruenerunt, qui vt euangelium gentibus praedicarent, a spiritu sancto emissi fuerant. Est enim hoc memorabile omnino diuinae bonitatis exemplum, quae peccatores non auersari, sed eorum salutem quaerere consueuit, vt iuxta Pauli dictum, vbi abundauit peccatum, ibi quoq; abundet gratia. Rom.5. Quo cumprimis pertinet, quod Christus se, vt peccatores saluos faceret, in mundum venisse testatur. Matth.9. & 18. Luc.9. & c. Nec desunt insignium peccatorum exempla, quos mirifica bonitate & gratia complexus est, inter quae praesens hoc non postremum locum meretur. Haec vero vt consolationi seruiunt, ita docent peccatores non temere abiiciendos, sed fouendos potius esse & instituendos, si quo modo emendari & saluari possint.
units.tr: First, he teaches where they came. They set out for Seleucia, which was not far from Antioch, and from there they crossed to Salamis, a town of Cyprus. Among all the islands of the Mediterranean, the ancient geographers award Cyprus almost the first praise for fortune and wealth. But from there, as we lately said, luxury and lust so prevailed among the Cypriots that the whole island was sacred to Venus, who was said to have been their own goddess. Indeed this one fact sufficiently shows how great was the corruption of morals and of the whole of life among that people, who had consecrated themselves and their whole land to Venus. Therefore we shall not think it by chance that they came first to this island, they who had been sent out by the Holy Spirit to preach the gospel to the Gentiles. For this is a memorable example of divine goodness, which is accustomed not to turn away from sinners but to seek their salvation, so that, according to Paul's saying, where sin abounded, grace may abound too. Rom. 5. To this especially pertains Christ's testimony that he came into the world to save sinners. Matt. 9. and 18. Luke 9. etc. Nor are there lacking examples of notorious sinners whom he embraced with wonderful goodness and grace, and this case deserves no small place among them. These things serve for consolation, and they teach that sinners are not to be cast off rashly, but rather cherished and instructed, if in any way they can be amended and saved.

units.la: Deinde doctrinae & praedicationis argumentum notatur, quando verbum Dei praedicauisse dicuntur. At verbo Dei omnem salutis rationem contineri, certum est. Quare non opus fuit, vt singulos doctrinae ipsorum articulos commemoraret, quos ex aliis tum concionibus tum epistolis apostolorum facile est colligere. Illud potius obseruemus, nullius in ecclesia tantam authoritatem esse, vt illi quidum praedicare permitti debeat, quando Paulum & Barnabam nihil ex suo cerebro, sed solum Dei verbum praedicauisse audiuimus. Quia enim Dei domus est ecclesia, in eadem solius Dei vox sonare debet, & sacrilega audacia est, in ea sub diuini nominis praetextu aliquid docere, quod Dei verbo non sit consentaneum. Quae causa est, quod omnes tam prophetas quam apostolos ad hoc mandatum astrictos fuisse legimus, vt nihil ecclesiae obtruderent, quam quod illi ex Dei ore accepissent. Vide Ezech.3. Ierem.1. Matth.28.
units.tr: Next, the argument of their teaching and preaching is noted, when they are said to have preached the word of God. Now it is certain that all the way of salvation is contained in the word of God. Therefore there was no need for Luke to recount the particular articles of their teaching, which can easily be gathered from the other sermons and letters of the apostles. Rather let us observe this: no one in the church has such authority that he should be permitted to preach anything of his own, since we hear that Paul and Barnabas preached nothing from their own brain, but only the word of God. For since the church is the house of God, only the voice of God ought to sound in it, and it is sacrilegious audacity to teach in it, under the pretext of the divine name, anything that does not agree with the word of God. For this reason we read that all the prophets as well as the apostles were bound by this command, to offer the church nothing but what they had received from the mouth of God. See Ezek. 3. Jer. 1. Matt. 28.

units.la: Tertio, vbi docuerint, offenditur: nimirum in Synagogis Iudaeorum. Quanquam enim ad gentes emissi essent, seruandus tamen fuit ordo, vt Iudaeis primum salus praedicaretur. Ita enim ipsis propria culpa a salute excidentibus, regnum Dei ad gentes transferri oportebat, vt illorum lapsus gentium saluti seruiret. Rom.11. Imo si rem probe expendamus, diuinae prouidentiae consilio factum fuisse patebit, vt eo tempore, Iudaei per omnes fere gentes dispersi habitarent. Inde enim commodissima praedicandi euangelij occasio apostolis oblata est. Ex lege etenim & prophetarum oraculis demonstrabatur Iesum esse promissum mundi saluatorem. Quod cum gentes audirent, & Iesu Christi historiam cum propheticis scriptis per omnia conuenire viderent, de scripturis sacris pie sentire coeperunt, qui primus ad salutem gradus fuit: sicq; factum est, vt praedictum in illis saluatorem vera fide ampletterentur. Recte ergo & prudenter in Iudaeorum synagogis praedicandi initium apostoli fecerunt. Agnoscamus nos Dei bonitatem, cuius beneficio hodie quoq; quantumuis indignis, salus vera per euangelium offertur in Iesu Christo Domino nostro: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Third, where they taught, they met with offence: namely in the synagogues of the Jews. For although they had been sent to the Gentiles, the order was nevertheless to be observed, so that salvation was preached to the Jews first. For since they had, through their own fault, fallen away from salvation, the kingdom of God had to be transferred to the Gentiles, so that their fall would serve the salvation of the Gentiles. Rom. 11. Indeed, if we weigh the matter carefully, it will be clear that by the counsel of divine providence it came about that at that time the Jews lived dispersed through almost all the nations. For from this the most convenient opportunity of preaching the gospel was offered to the apostles. For it was shown from the law and the oracles of the prophets that Jesus was the promised Saviour of the world. When the Gentiles heard this, and saw that the history of Jesus Christ agreed in every respect with the prophetic writings, they began to think devoutly of the sacred Scriptures, which was the first step to salvation; and so it came about that they embraced with true faith the Saviour foretold in them. Therefore the apostles rightly and wisely made it their beginning to preach in the synagogues of the Jews. Let us acknowledge the goodness of God, by whose benefit true salvation is offered today also through the gospel, in Jesus Christ our Lord, to us however unworthy: to whom be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXVII.
units.tr: Homily 87.

units.la: Cum autem peragrauissent insulam usque ad Paphum, inuenerunt quendam Magum pseudoprophetam Iudaeum, cui nomen erat Bariesu, qui erat cum Sergio Paulo proconsule, viro prudente. Hic accersitis Barnaba & Saulo, quaerebat audire sermonem Dei. Resistebat autem illis Elymas Magus (sic enim alio vocabulo enuntiabatur nomen eius) quaerens auertere proconsulem a fide. Saulus autem, qui idem Paulus, plenus spiritu sancto, & intentis in eum oculis, dixit: O plene omni dolo & omni malitia, fili diaboli, inimice omnis iustitiae, non cessas peruertere vias Domini rectas. Et nunc ecce manus Domini super te, & eris caecus, non videns Solem usque ad tempus. Continuo autem cecidit super eum caligo & tenebrae, & circumiens quaerebat, qui eum manuducerent. Tunc videns proconsul quod acciderat, credidit, admirans super doctrina Domini.
units.tr: When they had gone through the island as far as Paphos, they found a certain Magus, a Jewish false prophet named Bariesus, who was with Sergius Paulus the proconsul, a prudent man. He summoned Barnabas and Saul, because he wished to hear the word of God. But Elymas the Magus (for that was how his name was rendered in another word) opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith. Then Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his eyes on him and said: "O you who are full of all deceit and all malice, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you never stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord? And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a time." Immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went about seeking people to lead him by the hand. Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

units.la: Perquàm memorabilis est Dauidis regis & prophetae sententia, qua Iesum Christum in medio inimicorum suorum esse vaticinatur. Psalm.110. Ea enim regnum quidem Christo promittitur, sed simul de diaboli insidijs & tyrannide admonemur, qua regnum illud indefinenti bello oppugnat. Et huius quidem rei multa & praeclara exempla hic liber nobis exhibet. Nam hucusq; eos propofuit, qui aperta vi cum Christo congredi ausi sunt, quales primò quidem Hierosolymitanos proceres, deinde vero Herodem Agrippam vidimus. Vicit tamen illorum conatus Christus Rex, & illi quidem se frustra pugnare sentiunt, Herodes autem quia plus ceteris ausus fuerat, horribiles poenas pro tanto scelere exoluit. Non tamen idcirco pedem refert satan, sed novum regni sui propugnatorem in arenam producit, Elymam magum, si quo modo magicis impostturis Christi milites superare posset, quos ad carcerem & praesentis mortis pericula invictos esse videbat. Cum enim Paulus & Barnabas totam fere Cyprum euangelij doctrina illustrassent, iamq; Papho celeberrimae urbi imminerent, Magum hunc illis obijcit, ut huius opera felicem apud Cyprios euangelij cursum remoretur. Vincunt tamen apostoli Christo duce, cuius gloria eò clarior redditur, quò magis illam satan obscurare studet. Est autem diligenti consyderatione digna huius certaminis descriptio, quo cum famosissimo Mago & impostore suos apostolos Dominus commisit. Nam praeter id, quod nobis pugnas semper expectandas esse docet, pseudoprophetarum quoq; mores & studia egregie pingit, & ut cum illis pugnandum sit, admonet. Nos vero, quo plus inde ad nos fructus redeat, primò quidem certaminis huius occasionem, deinde vero congressum ipsum, & tandem illius exitum consyderabimus.
units.tr: The saying of David the king and prophet is most worthy of note, in which he foretells that Jesus Christ is in the midst of his enemies. Psalm 110. For by it a kingdom is indeed promised to Christ, but at the same time we are warned about the snares and tyranny of the devil, by which he assails that kingdom in a war without end. This book sets before us many notable examples of this. For so far it has presented those who dared to contend with Christ by open force: first the leaders of Jerusalem, and then Herod Agrippa, as we have seen. Yet Christ the King overcame their attempts, and they perceive that they fight in vain; Herod, because he had dared more than the rest, paid horrible penalties for so great a crime. Still, Satan does not on that account withdraw his foot, but brings forth a new champion of his kingdom into the arena: Elymas the Magus, in case by magical deceptions he might be able to overcome the soldiers of Christ, whom he saw to be unconquerable in prison and in the dangers of present death. For when Paul and Barnabas had illumined almost all of Cyprus with the teaching of the gospel, and were now bearing down on Paphos, a most famous city, he set this Magus against them, so that by his work the happy course of the gospel among the Cypriots might be held back. Yet the apostles conquer, with Christ as their leader, whose glory is made all the brighter the more Satan strives to obscure it. The account of this conflict, in which the Lord pitted his apostles against this most notorious Magus and impostor, is worthy of careful consideration. For besides teaching us that battles are always to be expected, it also vividly portrays the character and pursuits of false prophets, and admonishes us how we must contend with them. We, however, so that more fruit may come back to us from it, will consider first the occasion of this contest, then the encounter itself, and finally its outcome.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Occasionem tantae rei felix in Cypro insula euangelij cursus praebuisse videtur. Cum enim initio à Salamine facto, quae in Orientali littore posita est, totam insulam Paphum usq; in Occidentis angulo sitam, apostoli perlustrassent, fama novae doctrinae ab ipsis vulgatae, ad Sergij Pauli Proconsulis aures peruenit: qui ad se vocatis apostolis, verbum Dei ab illis audire cupit. Unde apparet illum, licet Romanus esset, veritatis tamen studiosum fuisse & gentilitiam religionem iam tum suspectam habuisse. Quae forsitan causa fuit, quod Iudaeo Mago aures praebuit, à quo se veritatem edoceri posse sperabat. Et eodem studio excitatus Paulum quoq; & Barnabam accersit ut illos docentes audiat. Illud vero Elymae Magi, qui Proconsulis familiaritate bucusq; usus fuerat, intolerabile visum est, qui propterea omnem adversus apostolos pugnandi occasionem diligentissime observavit, ut paulo post audiemus. Nunc enim priusquam hinc progrediamur, duo observanda veniunt. Primum, quod Deus in omni hominum genere suos habet, sicuti in praecedenti Sermone diximus. Hic vero illud addendum, quod suos vocat & feruat Deus, cum in praecipitio perditionis stare videtur. Nam Sergius Paulus, de quo hic agitur, à puero quidem in gentilismo educatus, idololatriae adsueuerat. Postea vero, licet errorem agnoscat, novo tamen & nocentiori inuoluitur, dum in Iudaeum Magum & pseudoprophetam incidit. Quis autem hunc Deo curae esse diceret, quem tot tamq; diversis erroribus seduci patitur? Sed quaerit amissam ouem per montes & valles, imò per maria quoq; fidelis ille pastor Christus, nec illam é manu sua eripi patitur. Vide Luc. 15. Iohan. 10. Docet ergo locus hic, ne de quoquam temere desperemus, nisi quis palam se ex reproborum numero esse probauerit. Deinde boni & pij magistratus exemplum in Sergio hoc Lucas proponit. Nam & veritatis discendae studio flagrat, & inauditae bactenus doctrinae ministros non praecipiti iudicio damnat, sed ad se accersitus doctrinam suam libere proponendi copiam facit. Debebant hunc imitari nostri saeculi principes, quorum plerique veritatis doctrinam, priusquam illam cognouerint, damnant, & crudelibus supplicijs in eos grassantur, quorum fidem & religionem prorsus ignorant. Sed meminerint ignorantia eos excusari non posse, qui nihil ex ignorantia facere, sed causas omnes diligenter inquirere debent.
units.tr: The course of the gospel in the island of Cyprus seems to have provided the occasion for so great a matter. For when the apostles, beginning from Salamis, which lies on the eastern shore, had traversed the whole island as far as Paphos, which lies at the corner of the west, the report of the new teaching which they had spread reached the ears of Sergius Paulus the proconsul; he summoned the apostles to himself and desired to hear the word of God from them. From this it appears that he, although he was a Roman, was nevertheless eager for the truth, and already held gentile religion under suspicion. This was perhaps the reason he lent his ear to the Jewish Magus, from whom he hoped to be taught the truth. Moved by the same eagerness, he also summoned Paul and Barnabas to hear them teaching. But it seemed intolerable to Elymas the Magus, who had enjoyed the proconsul's familiarity until then; therefore he watched most diligently for every occasion to fight against the apostles, as we shall hear a little later. For now, before we proceed from here, two things must be noted. First, that God has his own in every kind of people, as we said in the preceding sermon. But here this must be added: God calls and preserves his own even when they seem to stand on the brink of perdition. For Sergius Paulus, of whom we are speaking here, had been brought up from boyhood in paganism and was accustomed to idolatry. Afterwards, although he recognised his error, he was caught up in a new and more harmful one, when he fell in with a Jewish Magus and false prophet. Yet who would say that this man was of concern to God, when God allows him to be led astray by so many and such diverse errors? But that faithful shepherd, Christ, seeks the lost sheep over mountains and valleys, indeed even across the seas, and does not allow it to be snatched from his hand. See Luke 15, John 10. This place teaches us, therefore, not to despair rashly of anyone, unless he has plainly shown himself to belong to the number of the reprobate. Second, Luke sets before us in Sergius an example of a good and upright magistrate. For he burns with eagerness to learn the truth, and does not condemn with hasty judgment the ministers of a doctrine hitherto unheard of, but summons them to himself and grants them freedom to set forth their teaching. Our century's princes ought to imitate him, most of whom condemn the doctrine of truth before they have come to know it, and rage with cruel punishments against those whose faith and religion they utterly do not understand. But let them remember that those cannot be excused by ignorance who ought to do nothing out of ignorance, but to inquire diligently into all the causes.

units.la: His praemissis, huius certaminis congressum spectemus, in quo primas partes apostolis debere liquido patet. Quia enim bos ideo accersiuit Sergius Proconsul, ut ab illis verbum Dei disceret, illos mox omni mora abrupta tantam occasionem propagandi regni Christi, nequaquam neglexisse verisimile est. Hic vero confestim Magus quoq; prosilit, & Dei verbum praedicantibus resistit. Facile enim videbat, sibi posthac apud Proconsulem locum non fore, si in veritatis cognitione illuminaretur. Quanquam autem Lucas non exprimit, quomodo apostolis se opposuerit, quia tamen & pseudopropheta & Magus fuit, facile conijcitur, illum nihil eorum omisisse, quae ad opprimendam veritatem facere videbantur. Est, nobis diligenter inspiciendus antagonista hic, ut ex eo omnes pseudoprophetas agnoscere discamus. Et primò quidem nomen illud insolens observa, quo diuini aliquid sibi vendicat. Nam qui vero nomine Elymas dicebatur, Syriaca voce Bariesu, id est, Saluatoris filius dici vult. Unde colligimus, illis salutem polliceri ausum fuisse, qui ipsum sequerentur. Ex illorum ergo numero est, quos Christus venturos, & sui nominis maiestatem sibi ipsis vendicaturos esse praedixerat. dixerat. Matth.24. Illud vero omnibus pseudoprophetis proprium est, quod si non sibi ipsis, saltem doctrinae suae Dei nomen vsurpent, ut hoc praetextu incautis imponant. Sic Zedechias apud Achab de Syriaca victoria verba facturus, propheticum illud: Sic dicit dominus, praemittit. Idem in multis aliis videre est. Imo nemo unquam pseudopropheta fuit, qui non divini nominis praetextu sibi auctoritatem conciliare studuerit. Deinde illud quoq; ex communi pseudoprophetarum more facit, quod Proconsulis familiaritatem & amicitiam affectat, illiusq; lateri ceu indivulsus aliquis comes adhaeret. Solent enim in magnatum amicitias sese insinuare impostores, cum ut his in suas partes perattrahere reliqui illorum exemplo facilius trahantur, tum ut horum praesidio tuti sint. Quia enim veritatis patrocinio sese destitui norunt, carnale brachium quaerant oportet, quo defendantur. Sic Balaam olim, etiam si oraculo admonitus sit, Balaci tamen Moabitarum regis amicitiam demereri studet. Et Romanos Antichristos regum amicitiis & armis adiutos ad tantam potentiam ascendisse constat. Quid? quod hodie impostores & praestigiatores cucullati regum latera ita circunsistunt, ut illis insciis vix pedere liceat? Atqui haec fere causa est, quod qui tales sunt, doctrinam suam auditorum delicatis auribus accommodant, ne illos sibi infensos reddant, a quibus toti dependent. Finem vero & scopum hunc unum Elymas sibi propositum, ut Proconsulem a fide avertat, ne ijs credat, quae a Paulo dicebantur. Hunc finem Aegyptijs quoq; Magi propositum fuisse, Paulus tradit. 2. Tim. 3. Et ut verae doctrinae ministri in hoc omnes consentiunt, ut per fidem in Christum Deo lucrifiant homines: ita in hoc impostores omnes consentire certum est, ut fidem in Christum euertant, qua euersa, Dei regnum inter homines locum habere nequit. Sentit enim Satan fide vera vires suas maximè debilitari, cuius rei exempla passim apud euangelistas extant.
units.tr: With these things premised, let us look at the encounter of this contest, in which it is clear that the leading role ought to belong to the apostles. For since Sergius the proconsul had summoned them so that he might learn the word of God from them, it is hardly likely that they, breaking off every delay, neglected so great an opportunity of spreading the kingdom of Christ. But at once the Magus also leaps forward and resists those who preached the word of God. For he easily saw that, if the proconsul were enlightened in the knowledge of the truth, he would have no place with him from then on. Although Luke does not express how he opposed the apostles, nevertheless, since he was both a false prophet and a Magus, it is easily conjectured that he omitted nothing of those things which seemed to serve the suppression of the truth. This antagonist must be examined carefully by us, so that from him we may learn to recognise all false prophets. And first, observe that unusual name by which he claims something divine for himself. For he who was called by the name Elymas, in the Syriac word Bariesu, that is, wishes to be called the son of the Saviour. From this we gather that he dared to promise salvation to those who followed him. He is therefore of the number of those whom Christ had foretold would come and would claim for themselves the majesty of his name. Matthew 24. This, however, is peculiar to all false prophets: if not for themselves, at least for their teaching they usurp the name of God, so that under this pretext they may impose on the unwary. So Zedekiah, when he was about to speak to Ahab about the victory over Syria, prefaced his words with that prophetic formula: "Thus says the Lord." The same can be seen in many others. Indeed, there has never been a false prophet who did not strive to win authority for himself under the pretext of the divine name. Next, he also acts according to the common custom of false prophets in that he seeks the proconsul's familiarity and friendship, and clings to his side like an inseparable companion. For impostors are accustomed to insinuate themselves into the friendships of great men, partly so that by their example others may more easily be drawn over to their side, and partly so that they may be safe under their protection. For since they know that they have been deprived of the patronage of truth, they must seek a carnal arm by which they may be defended. So Balaam of old, although he had been warned by an oracle, nevertheless strove to win the friendship of Balak, king of the Moabites. And it is well established that the Roman Antichrists rose to such great power, aided by the friendships and arms of kings. What of the fact that today impostors and charlatans in hoods surround the sides of kings so closely that scarcely can anyone move a foot without their knowledge? And indeed, this is largely the reason why such men adapt their teaching to the delicate ears of their hearers, lest they make enemies of those on whom they wholly depend. But the one aim and purpose Elymas set before himself was to turn the proconsul away from the faith, so that he would not believe the things that were said by Paul. Paul relates that the magicians of Egypt also had this purpose. 2 Timothy 3. And just as the ministers of true doctrine all agree in this, that they win men to God through faith in Christ, so it is certain that all impostors agree in this, that they overturn faith in Christ; once it is overturned, the kingdom of God cannot have a place among men. For Satan perceives that his strength is chiefly weakened by true faith, and examples of this are found everywhere in the evangelists.

units.la: Sed Paulum videamus, & quomodo is impostorem nequissimum confutarit. Principio spiritu sancto repletum fuisse, id est, maiori & insolito spiritus motu efferbuisse, Lucas ait. Quod ideo actio-ni praemittit, ne quid carnis affectui tribuamus, cum grave & intolerabile verborum pondus audiemus. Interim admonemur, non caeco carnis affectu, sed spiritu sancto duce & consultore cum veritatis hostibus pugnandum esse: quem illi haud dubie hostem sentient, quantumuis carnali brachio optimè muniti videantur. Deinde intentis in Elymam oculis causam hanc agit: quod ingenui & intrepidi animi argumentum est. Et sane intrepidè & constanter Antichristianus resisti oportet, ne sese timeri existiment. Cur enim illos timeremus, cum maior sit, qui a nobis stat? 1. Ioan. 4. Cur item nostra pusillanimitate ferociores fierent, quos iam ante mentis sibi male conscia terrores exagitant? Tertiò suis illum coloribus egregiè depingit, & singulis verbis proprium quasi pondus adhibet. Primum, o plene omni dolo, inquit. Doli igitur mali & impostura accusat, qui ex Magia laudem & auctoritatem quaerebat. Secundò malitiam & animum ad quiduis perpetrandum audacissimum illi exprobrat. Quid enim malignius & audacius est, quàm sub divini nominis praetextu hominibus illudere, quae potissima Magorum & pseudoprophetarum laus est? Ita enim Deo quasi me dium vnguem offendunt, qui nominis sui prophanationem se non inultam dimissurum esse minatur. Tertiò filium diaboli vocat, ut eam impudentiam exagitet, qua se saluatoris filium dicere audebat. Diaboli vero filium esse, tum insolens animi superbia, tum pertinax malitiae studium abunde satis arguebat. Quartò, hostem omnis iustitiae esse dicit: & merito quidem, cum Christo aduersaretur, extra quem nulla iustitia inuenitur, qua Deo placere possit. Quintò, Non cessas (ait) peruertere vias Domini rectas. Quibus verbis duo maxima scelera comprehendit, incurabilem nimirum malitiam, & peruertendi verbi Dei studium. Simplex enim illud est & purum, simulq; planissimam salutis rationem nobis monstrat. Hominum vero malitia fit, ut ea perplexa & incerta videatur. Postremò grauem supplicij sententiam intonat: Et nunc ecce manus Domini super te, & eris caecus, non videns Solem usq; ad tempus. Vbi inter terrifica diuinarum minarum fulmina, spem salutis poenitentiam agenti & ad Dominum conuersio relinqui videmus. Ita enim iram suam Deus per verbum reuelare solet, ne per desperationem prorsus absorbeantur, quos ille saluos vult. Praecipuus vero huius loci vsus est, ut discamus quid hodie fidis ecclesiarum Christi ministris agendum sit, quando non unus Elymas regum & principum aures obsident, ut ijs a fide abalienatis, rude & ignobile vulgus pro sua libidine opprimant. Nec enim alios censere possumus Monachos & sacrificulos, qui nugas suas dolo malo sub divini nominis praetextu venditant, qui gigantea audacia potestatem sibi in caelis arrogant, qui Christi iustitiam & fidem iustificantem ex professo oppugnant, qui diuini verbi authoritatem impudenter eleuant, & idem illud humanis traditionibus corrumpunt, qui salutis rationem simplicissimam infinitis Labyrinthis votorum monasticorum, ordinum, regularum, meritorum, bullarum, indulgentiarum & casuum reseruatorum intricatissimam, adeoq; imperuestigabile reddunt: qui deniq; bis non contenti, principum animos insuper ad cades & sanguinis innoxij effusionem exti-mulant. Eos simili constantia & libertate argui oportet, vt ab illis sibi cauere discant, qui ipsorum theatrica maiestate hucusq; decepti sunt. Nec eos audiamus, qui in hac causa modestia & charitatis leges nobis praescribunt, quando plerosq; horum incurabiles esse constat, & in hoc vnum incumbere, vt semel arreptam tyrannidem per phas & nephas tueri possint.
units.tr: But let us look at Paul, and at how he refuted that most wicked impostor. First, Luke says that he was filled with the Holy Spirit, that is, that he boiled over with a greater and unusual movement of the Spirit. He puts this before the action so that we may not attribute anything to fleshly emotion, since we are about to hear words of heavy and intolerable weight. Meanwhile we are reminded that we must fight against the enemies of the truth not with a blind fleshly passion but with the Holy Spirit as our leader and counsellor; those enemies will undoubtedly feel him to be an enemy, however well they seem fortified with a carnal arm. Next, with his eyes fixed on Elymas, he brings the charge against him, which is a sign of a frank and fearless spirit. And indeed the Antichristian must be resisted boldly and steadily, so that they do not suppose they are feared. For why should we fear them, since he who is in us is greater than he who stands against us? (1 John 4.) Why should they grow fiercer through our timidity, when terrors of a guilty conscience already torment them? Thirdly, he depicts him splendidly in his true colours, and with each word he applies a certain weight of its own. First, "O full of all guile," he says. He accuses him, therefore, of wicked deceit and imposture, since he was seeking praise and authority from his magic. Secondly, he reproaches him for his malice and for a mind most bold for any kind of crime. For what is more malicious and more audacious than to mock men under the pretext of the divine name, which is the chief praise of magicians and false prophets? For they thus offend God, as it were, to the very quick, who threatens that he will not let the profaning of his name go unavenged. Thirdly, he calls him a son of the devil, so as to rebuke the impudence by which he dared to call himself a son of the Saviour. Indeed, being a son of the devil was amply proved both by his insolent arrogance of mind and by his stubborn zeal for wickedness. Fourthly, he says that he is an enemy of all righteousness; and rightly so, since he set himself against Christ, outside whom no righteousness is found by which one can please God. Fifthly, "You do not cease," he says, "to pervert the straight ways of the Lord." In these words he comprehends two very great crimes, namely an incurable malice and a zeal for perverting the Word of God. For that Word is simple and pure, and at the same time it shows us the very plainest way of salvation; but it comes about, through the malice of men, that it seems intricate and uncertain. Lastly, he thunders out a heavy sentence of punishment: "And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a time." Here, amid the terrifying flashes of divine threats, we see that hope of salvation is left to one who repents and is converted to the Lord. For God is wont thus to reveal his anger through the Word, so that those whom he wills to be saved are not utterly swallowed up by despair. But the chief use of this passage is that we may learn what the faithful ministers of the churches of Christ ought to do today, when it is not one Elymas alone who besets the ears of kings and princes, so that, with these alienated from the faith, they may oppress the rude and base crowd at their own pleasure. For we cannot judge otherwise of the monks and little priests, who peddle their trifles with wicked guile under the pretext of the divine name; who with giant audacity arrogate to themselves power in heaven; who expressly attack the righteousness of Christ and justifying faith; who shamelessly lessen the authority of the divine Word and corrupt the same Word with human traditions; who make the most simple way of salvation most intricate and well-nigh unsearchable, with the infinite labyrinths of monastic vows, orders, rules, merits, bulls, indulgences and reserved cases; and who finally, not content with these things, further goad the minds of princes to slaughter and the shedding of innocent blood. Such men must be refuted with the same constancy and freedom, so that those who have so far been deceived by their theatrical majesty may learn to beware of them. Nor should we listen to those who, in this cause, prescribe for us the rules of moderation and charity, since it is clear that most of these men are incurable, and that their one aim is to be able to defend by right or by wrong the tyranny once seized.

units.la: Restat certaminis huius finis & euentus, tristis quidem Elymae impostori, Sergio autem proconsuli laetissimus. Illi enim continuo irrogatur a Paulo denunciatum supplicium, & excaecatus quaerit qui eum manuduceret. Simile quid supra Ananiae & Sapphirae accidisse vidimus: vnde nos diuini verbi vim aguoscere conuenit. Maxime tamen hoc loco obseruandum est, quid impostores & pseudoprophetas maneat, qui vel quaestus vel honoris gratia Dei verbum oppugnare audent. Excaecantur illi plerunque, si non corpore, saltem animis, quos iusto iudicio in reprobum sensum tradit Dominus, vt nec agnitam veritatem ample&ti, nec palam deprehensos errores vitare possint. Praeterea Dei iudicio infames facti, carnis brachium amittunt, in quo potissimam spem collocarunt. Ita verò impletur, quod apud Zachariam cap. 11. scribitur: Va pastori idolo, qui gregem deserit. Gladius iminebit brachio eius & oculo eius dextero: brachium eius plane exarescet, & oculus eius dexter omnino hebescet. Nec desunt huius iudicij exempla hodie, at nobis oculi desunt, quibus illa obseruemus. Et nostri illi Elymae eò infeliciores sunt, quod excaecati adhuc tamen se videre putant, nec ducem quaerunt, imò à Deo oblatos cum stomacho reijciunt. Porrò vt infeliciter Elymae cessit pugna haec, ita magnus inde ad Proconsulem fructus redijt, quem hoc pacto vinculis tenebrarum liberauit Dominus. Is enim viso Dei iudicio, credidit, & doctrinam Christi admirari & magni facere coepit. Est hoc filiorum Dei proprium, quod Dei iudicia agnoscunt, & aliorum exemplis emendantur. Porrò mali homines & impostores proficiunt in peius. 2. Tim. 3. Caeterum in tota hac historia consolationis plenum est, quod veritatem nec aperta vi tyrannorum, nec subdolis diaboli artibus superari posse videmus. Pressa siquidem resurgit, & pugnando vires maiores colligit. Hanc ergo amplexi, constanter insistamus huius authori & vindici Iesu Christo Domino nostro: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: The end and outcome of this contest remains: sad indeed for the impostor Elymas, but most joyful for the proconsul Sergius. For at once the punishment threatened by Paul is inflicted on Elymas, and, blinded, he seeks someone to lead him by the hand. We saw something similar happen above to Ananias and Sapphira, and from this we ought to acknowledge the power of the divine Word. Yet in this passage it must chiefly be observed what awaits impostors and false prophets who dare to oppose the Word of God, whether for gain or for honour. They are for the most part blinded, if not in body, at least in mind; the Lord, by a just judgment, hands them over to a reprobate mind, so that they can neither avoid the truth once known nor the errors plainly detected. Moreover, having been made infamous by God's judgment, they lose the arm of the flesh, in which they placed their chief hope. Thus is fulfilled what is written in Zechariah, chapter 11: "Woe to the idol shepherd who forsakes the flock! The sword shall be upon his arm and upon his right eye: his arm shall utterly wither, and his right eye shall be wholly dimmed." Nor are there lacking examples of this judgment today, but we lack the eyes with which to observe them. And those Elymases of ours are the more unhappy because, though blinded, they still think they see, and they do not seek a guide, but indeed angrily reject the one offered them by God. Moreover, just as this contest turned out unhappily for Elymas, so great fruit came thence to the proconsul, whom the Lord in this way freed from the chains of darkness. For, having seen God's judgment, he believed, and began to admire the teaching of Christ and to hold it in high regard. It is a peculiarity of the sons of God that they acknowledge God's judgments and are amended by the examples of others; but wicked men and impostors go from bad to worse (2 Tim. 3). Otherwise, in this whole story there is much consolation, in that we see the truth can be overcome neither by the open violence of tyrants nor by the crafty arts of the devil. For when pressed it rises again, and by fighting it gathers greater strength. Let us therefore embrace it, and steadfastly persevere in it, in Jesus Christ our Lord, its author and defender, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LXXXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXXXVIII.

units.la: Cum autem à Papho soluissent qui cum Paulo erant, venerunt Pergen Pamphyliae. Iohannes autem digressus ab ipsis reuersus est Hierosolymam. Caeterum illi peragratis regionibus, à Perga venerunt Antiochiam Pisidiae: & ingressi synagogam die sabbatorum, sederunt. Post lectionem vero Legis & Prophetarum miserunt praesides synagogae ad eos, dicentes: Viri fratres, si quis est in vobis sermo exhortationis ad populum, dicite.
units.tr: When those who were with Paul had set sail from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and returned to Jerusalem. The others, travelling through the regions, came from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia, and on the sabbath day they entered the synagogue and sat down. After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, "Brethren, if there is any word of exhortation for the people, speak."

units.la: MVlta quidem & praeclara in Iesu Christi operibus diuinae ipsius potentia & maiestatis argumenta extant: inter illa vero cumprimis euidens & luculentum est, quod apostolorum ministerio intra paucos annos totum terrarum orbem subiugauit. Cum enim hos nullis carnalibus praeditos fidijs instructos, imò vilissimos omnium hominum fuisse constet, ijdem vero res tantas confecerint, diuinae virtutis opus in illis agnoscere oportet, qua factum est, vt noua totius orbis facies induceretur, & liberata veterum superstitionum erroribus gentes, religionem veram suscipèrent. Est huc praecipuum, quod in praesenti Pauli & Barnabae peregrinatione obseruemus. Duo enim isti ex spiritus sancti mandato emissi, vt euangelium promiscue gentibus praedicarent, felici cursu omnia perrumpunt, quae illis impedimento fore videbantur. Et primo quidem in Cyprum delati, opulentissimae insulae cultores, luxu simul & nefando Veneris culta perditos, Christi regno subiiciunt: nec modo modò ignobile vulgus in suas partes pertrahunt, sed Romanum Proconsulem Sergium, cuius authoritas vel sola resisteré potuisset, si humanum illud negotium fuisset, veri cognitione illustratum Christo lucrifaciunt, & Elymam Magum, selectum diaboli organum, caecitate horribili percussum, in triumpho ducunt: adeò ut uno conflictu simul humanas vires & diaboli artes superatas fuisse constet. Videamus autem, ut tam lata rerum initia felicem ulterius propagandi regni Christi occasionem apostolis praebuerint.
units.tr: There are many striking proofs of the divine power and majesty in the works of Jesus Christ, but among them this is especially clear and manifest: that within a few years, through the ministry of the apostles, he brought the whole world under his rule. For it is agreed that these men had no worldly advantages, but were in fact the most despised of all people. Since they nonetheless accomplished such great things, we must recognise in them a work of divine power, by which the face of the whole world was made new, and the nations, freed from the errors of ancient superstitions, embraced the true religion. The chief point we should notice in the present journey of Paul and Barnabas is this. The two of them, sent out at the command of the Holy Spirit to preach the gospel to the Gentiles without distinction, break through with a happy course every obstacle that seemed likely to stand in their way. First they were brought to Cyprus, where they subjected to the kingdom of Christ the inhabitants of that very wealthy island, who were ruined by luxury and by the wicked worship of Venus. They drew not only the common people to their side, but also won to Christ the Roman proconsul Sergius, who by his authority alone could have resisted them, had the matter been merely human; he was enlightened by the knowledge of the truth. And they led in triumph Elymas the magician, the chosen instrument of the devil, struck with a terrible blindness. So it is evident that in a single contest both human strength and the arts of the devil were overcome. Let us now see how such a promising beginning gave the apostles a happy opportunity to spread the kingdom of Christ further.

units.la: Cypro enim devicta, in Pamphyliam ex Papho traiecerunt, & Pergen eius regionis oppidum deuenerunt, non paruum itineris spacium per mare & terras emensi. Nec dubium m est, quin Pamphyliam quoque euangelij doctrina illustrarint, cum eo nomine peregrinationem iam suscepissent. Efl, hoc non vulgare apostolici zeli & inductrix exemplum, quod licet celeberrimam insulam Christo adduxissent, non tamen idcirco sibi quiescendum putauerunt, quasi suo officio iam probè defuncti essent, sed ad ulterira pergunt, eoq; plus se Christo debere exististimant, quo magis ille ipsorum ceptis benignus aspirat. Ita alibi Paulus, cum ab Arabia ad Illyricum usq; omnia longè lateq; euangelio Iesu Christi repleuisset, tam abest, ut ocium sibi polliceatur, ut potius ad Italiam & Hispaniam quoq; animum adiiciat. Rom.15. Quibus exemplis illorum ignauia arguitur, qui cum vix dum incaeperint, sibiipsis ferias indicunt, suosq; labores maximi aestimare solent, nec iustum aequumque putant, ut plus quiddam ab ipsis exigatur. At ad finem usq; perseuerare conuenit, ne ulla nos Christo seruiendi factas capiat, quoad illius gloriam per nos illustrari, & aliquos in salutis cognitionem perduci posse spes est.
units.tr: For Cyprus having been conquered, they crossed over from Paphos into Pamphylia and reached Perga, a town of that region, having travelled no small distance by sea and land. Nor is there any doubt that they also brought the teaching of the gospel to Pamphylia, since they had already undertaken the journey for that purpose. Here is a notable example, and one that stirs up apostolic zeal: although they had brought Christ to a most famous island, they did not think they should therefore rest, as if they had already discharged their duty well, but pressed on further, and considered that they owed all the more to Christ, the more kindly he favoured their undertakings. So elsewhere Paul, having filled everything far and wide with the gospel of Jesus Christ from Arabia as far as Illyricum, is so far from promising himself leisure that he rather turns his mind also to Italy and Spain. Rom. 15. By such examples the laziness of those is shown up who, scarcely having begun, declare holidays for themselves, and who are accustomed to think highly of their own labours, and do not judge it right and fair that anything more should be demanded of them. But it is fitting to persevere to the end, so that we never grow weary of serving Christ, as long as there is hope that his glory may be made known through us and some may be brought to the knowledge of salvation.

units.la: Caeterum sanctissimo studio occupatus, tristissimus casus accidit. Dum enim alios Christo lucrifacere conantur, comitis & Symmysta sui, quem ex multis sibi delegerant, iacturam faciunt. Fuit is Iohannes cognomento Marcus, Mariae illius filius, ad cuius domum Petrus carcere elapsus sese contulit, ut supra dictum est. Hic, ut infra cap.15. patebit, continuis laboribus & periculis assiduis fractus, illis relictis Hierosolymam redijt. Quo facto non modò opera sua defuit, quibus in sanctissimo officio indiuulse adesse debebat, verumetiam acerrimae contentionis, inter Paulum & Barnabam postea exortae, author fuit. Quia tamen Hierosolymam redijisse dicitur, vbi illi mater erat, verisimile est, ipsum ignauiae & pusillanimitati suae pietatem in matrem viduam praetexisse, ut ex eorum numero censeri possit, quorum typum in euangelio gerit is, qui à Christo vocatus, patrem prius sepelire voluit. Matth.8. Luc.9. Proponit autem eiusmodi exempla spiritus sanctus, non ut imitemur, sed ut intelligamus, semper defectores fore, & tristes casus frequenter oboriturös, qui felicem euangelij cursum remorentur. Nec enim ociatur satan, qui apostolos quoq; cribrare desyderauit, & licet illos à Christo prorsus diuellere non posset, effecit tamen, ut vinculis ipsius territi, omnes ab illo diffugerent. Sic Iohannis 6.cap.millia aliquot simul ab illo defecisse legimus. Et Paulus, qui modò Marcum deficere videt, postea Demadem quoq; praesens seculum amplexum, & se cum Caesari sistetur, ab omnibus amicis desertum fuisse conqueritur. 2. Tim.4. Neminem ergo quorundam leuitas offendat, qui hodie quoq; vbi haud poenitendos progressus in Christi causa fecerunt, mox deficiunt. Tales enim fore Christus & apostoli praedixerunt. Interim meminerint ipsi, se grauiter peccare. Nā Christi causam deserunt, quae abnegationis species est. Deinde infirmiores offendunt, & malignis euangelij fideiq; Christiana aestimatoribus calumniandi occasionem praebent, ut propter ipsos nomen Christi male audiat. Praeterea quosdam ignotos & exteros reliquis suspectos reddunt, quorum beneficentia subleuari debebant. Postremò dissidiorum authores sunt, dum in partium studia secum abripiunt eos, qui animos & vires in propagando Christi regno debebant coniungere: eoq; grauius nocent, quò sublimiori gradu dignitati constituti sunt.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while they were occupied with a most holy task, a very sad accident befell them. For while they were trying to win others to Christ, they suffered the loss of their companion and fellow-worker, whom they had chosen for themselves from among many. This was John, surnamed Mark, the son of that Mary to whose house Peter went after escaping from prison, as was said above. He, as will appear below in chapter 15, broken by continual labours and constant dangers, left them and returned to Jerusalem. By doing so he not only failed in his work, in which he ought to have been present without wavering in that most holy office, but he was also the author of the very sharp dispute that arose afterwards between Paul and Barnabas. Yet since he is said to have returned to Jerusalem, where his mother was, it is likely that he pretended his cowardice and fainthearted behaviour was devotion to his widowed mother, so that he could be counted among those whom the man called by Christ, who wished first to bury his father, represents in the Gospel (Matt. 8; Luke 9). The Holy Spirit sets forth examples of this kind not so that we should imitate them, but so that we should understand that there will always be deserters, and that sad accidents will often arise to delay the happy course of the gospel. For Satan is not idle; he also desired to sift the apostles, and although he could not wholly tear them from Christ, he nevertheless brought it about that, terrified by his chains, they all fled from him. So we read in John 6 that several thousand at once fell away from him. And Paul, who now sees Mark deserting, afterwards complains that Demas too embraced the present world, and that when he was to stand before Caesar he was deserted by all his friends (2 Tim. 4). Let no one therefore be offended by the fickleness of some who, even today, after making progress in Christ's cause that is not to be regretted, soon fall away. For Christ and the apostles foretold that such people would arise. Meanwhile let them remember that they sin grievously. For they desert Christ's cause, which is a kind of denial. Then they offend the weaker brethren, and give occasion for slander to those who maliciously judge the gospel and the Christian faith, so that the name of Christ is ill spoken of because of them. Moreover, they make certain strangers and outsiders suspect to the rest, whose kindness ought to have relieved them. Finally, they are the authors of divisions, while they drag into factional zeal those who ought to join their minds and strength in spreading Christ's kingdom; and they do the more harm the higher the rank of dignity to which they have been raised.

units.la: Sed ad apostolos reuersi, illorum exemplo discamus, quid nobis, si quid simile accidat, faciendum sit. Num enim illi subita Marci defectione intellecta, ipsi quoq; commissum sibi munus deserunt? Minimè gentium. Imò peragratis Pamphyliae regionibus, tandem etiam Tauro monte superato in Pisidiam transeunt, & Antiochiam (quae Caesarea quoq; dicta fuit olim teste Plinio) ingrediuntur: vbi maiori quàm vnquam aliàs feruore & studio euangelii praedicant, sicuti sequentia abunde docebunt. Admonemur exemplo hoc, minimè committendum esse, ut aliorum siue perfidia siue ignavia, nos ab officio renocari patiamur. Nec enim aliorum culpa nos excusare poterit, quorum lapsus
units.tr: But let us return to the apostles, and learn from their example what we should do if something similar happens to us. Did they, when the sudden desertion of Mark was known, themselves also give up the task committed to them? By no means. Rather, after crossing the regions of Pamphylia, and at last also crossing Mount Taurus, they pass into Pisidia and enter Antioch (which was also called Caesarea of old, as Pliny testifies). There they preach the gospel with greater zeal and earnestness than ever before, as the following passage will abundantly show. We are admonished by this example that we must by no means allow ourselves to be called back from our duty by the faithlessness or the cowardice of others. For the fault of others will not excuse us, whose lapse it becomes us rather to beware of than to imitate.

units.la: Pamphylia Euangelium illustratur. nos potius cauere, quàm imitari decet. Et quia Domini causa est, quam sustinemus, facile illi fuerit, hanc etiam per paucissimos & nullius coram mundo authoritatis homines afferere. Imò patiturū non raro, vt illi deficiant à quibus opem praestantissimā sperabamus, vt sic palàm fiat, in vno Deo non bis gloriandū esse. Accedit hū, quòd licet à mundo deseramur, soli tamen non sumus. Nam quod de seipso Christus pronunciauit, ad omnia illius membra extendi debet. Venit tempus (inquit) vt dispergamini vnusquisq; in sua, meq; solum relinquatis: & tamen non sum solus, quia pater mecum est. Iohan. 16. Quid quod idem ait? Non relinquā vos orphanos. Iohan. 14. Ecce ego vobiscum sum vsq; in consummationem seculi. Matth. 28. Quò etiam illud Dauidis pertinet: Vbi pater meus & mater mea deseruerunt me, Dominus colligit me. Psal. 27. Et horum quidem non modò verbi ministros, verumetiam principes & magistratus meminisse conuenit. Habent enim hi quoque suae vocationis authorem Deum, qui se in medio illorum versari testatur. Quare si in afferenda Dei gloria constantes fuerint, non est quòd mundi terroribus commoueantur, quando Deum tutorem & vindicem habituri sunt. Idem priuati quoq; cogitent, ne mundi facie commoueantur. Interit enim hæc, at Domini verbum, cui cùm salutis tum vocationis nostræ certitudo innititur, manet in æternum. Isa. 40.
units.tr: Pamphylia: the gospel is spread. And since it is the Lord's cause that we sustain, it would be easy for him to make it known through very few people, and men of no authority in the eyes of the world. Indeed, he will often allow those in whom we hoped for the most excellent help to fail, so that it may be made plain that we should glory in one God alone. In addition, although we are forsaken by the world, we are not alone. For what Christ declared about himself must be extended to all his members. "The time is coming," he says, "that you will be scattered, each to his own home, and will leave me alone; yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me" (John 16). What of the fact that he also says, "I will not leave you orphans" (John 14), and "Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age" (Matt. 28)? To this also belongs that saying of David: "When my father and mother have forsaken me, the Lord will take me up" (Ps. 27). And it is fitting to remember these not only as ministers of the Word, but also as princes and magistrates. For they too have God as the author of their calling, who testifies that he is present in their midst. Therefore, if they are steadfast in proclaiming the glory of God, there is no reason for them to be moved by the terrors of the world, since they will have God as their protector and avenger. Let private persons likewise consider that they should not be moved by the appearance of the world. For this appearance passes away, but the word of the Lord, on which the certainty both of our salvation and of our calling rests, remains for ever (Isa. 40).

units.la: IIII. Quid in Antiochia Pisidiæ fecerint apostoli.
units.tr: IIII. What the apostles did in Antioch of Pisidia.

units.la: Porrò videamus, quid Antiochiæ egerint apostoli. Die sabbatorum synagogam ingressi, consederunt. Scribit hoc Lucas, vt ostendat, illos docendi siue prædicandi euangelij occasionem quaesiisse. Diebus sabbatorum enim publicè convenire solebant Iudæi, vt in lege erudirentur & preces ad Deum funderent. Quæ causa fuit, quòd paulò ante apud Salaminem quoq; apostoli synagogas Iudaeorum ingressi fuisse dicti sunt. Nec dubium est, illos hoc ipsum etiam alibi fecisse, cum non alio loco commodiorem docendi occasionem sperare possent. Nec illos fefellit opinio. Finita enim solenni & consueta legis ac prophetarum lectione, Synagogæ præsides, illos non vulgares homines esse suspicati, ipsis quoq; ad populum dicendi copiam faciunt. Nam missio ad illos nuncio, dicunt: Viri fratres, si quis est in vobis sermo exhortationis ad populū, dicite. Et sic Paulus celeberrimā de Christo Iesu & vniuerso salutis nostræ mysterio concionem instituit, cuius initium eras (Deo volente (audiemus. In prae senti verò quaedam consyderanda veniunt, de quibus ordine dicendum est.
units.tr: Let us now see what the apostles did at Antioch. On the Sabbath day they entered the synagogue and sat down. Luke writes this to show that they sought an opportunity of teaching or preaching the gospel. For on the Sabbath days the Jews customarily gathered publicly to be instructed in the law and to pour out prayers to God. This is why it was said that shortly before, at Salamis, the apostles had also entered the synagogues of the Jews. There is no doubt that they did the same elsewhere too, since they could hope for no more suitable place to teach. Nor did their expectation deceive them. When the customary solemn reading of the law and the prophets was finished, the rulers of the synagogue, suspecting that these men were not ordinary people, gave them the opportunity to address the people. For they sent a messenger to them, saying: "Brethren, if there is any word of exhortation in you for the people, speak." And so Paul began a most famous sermon about Christ Jesus and the whole mystery of our salvation, which we shall hear tomorrow, God willing. For the present, however, some matters come up for consideration, and these must be discussed in order.

units.la: V. Veritas publicè docere debet.
units.tr: V. Truth ought to be taught publicly.

units.la: Primò non in œnopolijs inter ebrios comessatores, nec in angulis & obscuris syluis inter rude & imperitum vulgus salutis doctrinam spargunt apostoli: sed locum publicum ingressi, publicè euangelium docere cupiunt. Id verò iuxta Christi exemplum illos fecisse constat, qui & ipse synagogas frequenter ingressus fuisse, & publicè docuisse legitur. Et cum à Caiapha pontifice tanquam hereticus de doctrina & discipulis examinaretur, hoc vno argumento sese excusat, quòd in templo & synagogis publicè docuerit, nec totius populi iudicium de doctrina sua reformidet. Iohan. 18. Quā exemplo ijs arguendis seruiunt, qui noua dogmata clanculum apud imperitos disseminant, nec quicquam perinde vt lucem & ecclesiæ iudicium fugiunt & horrent. Id verò vnum abunde probat, ipsos impostores esse, cum veritas nihil perinde vt lucem expetat. Vbi tamen minimè eos damnamus, qui persecutionum terroribus circumsepti, occultius pietatis officia exercent, quod Hierosolymæ etiam à fidelibus in Mariæ domo & alibi facitatum fuisse audiuimus: modò parati sint ad reddendam rationem fidei suæ quibusuis hanc exigentibus, nec Anabaptistarum more, pertinaci silentio & subdola dissimulatione eos eludant, qui in illorum fidem & doctrinam inquirunt.
units.tr: First, the apostles do not spread the doctrine of salvation in wine-shops among drunken revellers, nor in corners and dark woods among a rude and unlearned crowd. Rather, they enter a public place and desire to teach the gospel publicly. It is clear that they did this in imitation of Christ, who is read to have frequently entered the synagogues and taught publicly. When he was examined by the high priest Caiaphas as a heretic about his doctrine and his disciples, he defended himself on this one ground: that he had taught openly in the temple and the synagogues, and he did not fear the judgment of the whole people concerning his teaching. John 18. Those who spread new doctrines secretly among the unlearned, and who flee and shun nothing so much as the light and the judgment of the Church, are rebuked by this example. This alone sufficiently proves that such men are impostors, since truth seeks nothing so much as the light. Yet we by no means condemn those who, hemmed in by the terrors of persecution, perform the duties of piety more quietly; we have heard that this was done even at Jerusalem by the faithful in Mary's house and elsewhere. Provided only that they are ready to give an account of their faith to any who demand it, and do not, in the manner of the Anabaptists, mock with stubborn silence and sly dissimulation those who inquire into their faith and doctrine.

units.la: VI. Sabbata religiosè obseruanda.
units.tr: VI. The Sabbaths are to be observed devoutly.

units.la: Deinde non superuacanea est temporis notatio, qua die sabbatorum synagogam ingressi fuisse dicuntur. Ea enim sabbati religionem studiosè ab illis obseruatam fuisse docet: quem diem in prima mundi origine diuinis cultibus consecratum, & per Mosem studiosissimè Israelitis commendatum esse constat. Quia enim diuersis occupationibus distrahimur, necesse fuit, vt tempus aliquod omnibus tam curis quàm negotijs liberum constitueretur, quo nos totos animo simul & corpore ijs impenderemus, quæ ad Dei cultum faciunt. Septimum ergo diem huic studio Deus destinauit, quem ideo suum dicere consueuit, vt sciremus nobis, quando vs agitur, ab omnibus alijs curis & studijs abstinendum esse. Tantam verò eius religionem esse voluit, vt capitali supplicio eius transgressores cohercendos esse statuerit. Num. 15. Et apud prophetas frequenter inter grauissima peccata, adeoq; inter Babylonicæ captiuitatis causas, hæc quoq; numeratur, quòd sabbata Dei prophanauerint. Quæ causa est, quòd & Dei filius, licet superstitiosam borum obseruationem non semel reprehenderit, ea tamen studiosè obseruarit, in quibus cultū suum deus consistere voluit. Nam illis diebus synagogas ingressus, caeribus cætibus sacris & publicis precibus interfuit, adhæc ipse docuit & alios docentes audiuit, simulq; beneficentiæ opera diligenter exercuit. Quorum memores apostoli, ipsi quoque præceptoris sui exemplum sibi imitandum esse putauerunt. At hodie eò res deuenit, ut inter Christianos homines optimi haberi possint, qui operibus manuarijs & victui seruientibus sabbata Dei violant, cum plerique illa nefandis sceleribus prophanent, nec unquam vel superbia & fastu, vel ebrietate, vel luxu & libidine plus peccetur, quàm illo die, qui totus Deo & diuinorum operum æternaq; quietis meditationi consecratus esse debebat. Et cum ista palàm fiant, adhuc tamen malorum nostri seculi causas inquirimus?
units.tr: Next, the note of time is not superfluous, namely that they are said to have entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day. This shows that they devoutly observed the sabbath religion, a day which, as is well known, was consecrated to divine worship at the very beginning of the world and was most earnestly commended to the Israelites through Moses. For since we are drawn in different directions by various occupations, it was necessary that some time be set apart, free from all cares and business, in which we might devote ourselves wholly, in mind and body, to the things that pertain to the worship of God. God therefore appointed the seventh day for this purpose, and he was accustomed to call it his own, so that we might know that when it is in progress we must abstain from all other cares and pursuits. Moreover, he willed its sanctity to be so great that he decreed its transgressors should be restrained by capital punishment. Num. 15. And among the prophets, this also is frequently counted among the gravest sins, and indeed among the causes of the Babylonian captivity, that they profaned the Sabbaths of God. This is why the Son of God, although he more than once rebuked the superstitious observance of these days, nevertheless observed devoutly those things in which God willed his worship to consist. For on those days he entered the synagogues, took part in the sacred and public assemblies and prayers, and besides taught and listened to others teaching, and at the same time diligently performed works of kindness. Mindful of these things, the apostles also thought that they should imitate the example of their master.
