For just as God kindly feeds us while he supplies food from the earth, so he has given us angels as guardians, who encamp around his worshippers and diligently defend them. But since this has already been said before, let these remarks suffice. Let us nevertheless observe the use of this teaching, which lies chiefly in this: that we should be grateful to God, and through all adversities struggle on, with unconquered hope and trust in divine help, to maintain our calling. Besides, this example commends to us the dignity of the gospel and of the evangelical ministry. For it is remarkable first that Paul is called to teach through an angel and by a divine oracle. So Peter was admonished by a heavenly vision to preach to Cornelius and the Gentiles; and the Spirit led Philip to become a teacher of salvation to the Ethiopian. It is therefore in vain that people despise the human ministry as some mean and ignoble thing, and seek angels as teachers, when angels send us to hear men. What more? Does Paul not teach that not even an angel is to be believed, if he should preach anything different from the apostolic doctrine? Gal. 1. Further, the words of the angel also commend the dignity of the ministry. For he says: "Having set out for Macedonia, help us." Yet it belongs to God alone to help both bodies and souls. But because the word of the gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, its ministers are not rashly said to bring help to men, indeed even to save them. And for this reason Obadiah, prophesying about the kingdom of Christ, called the apostles saviours. Therefore the rashness and impiety of those is here refuted who cry that tumults and the ruin of commonwealths arise from the gospel, when it is certain that men cannot but rush to destruction unless they are called back to the way of salvation by the preaching of Christ, the prophet saying: "The nation and kingdom that does not serve you will perish." Isa. 60.

units.la: Quid vero Paulus, vbi se diuinitus in Macedoniam, ad homines ignotos, adeoq; in aliam orbis partem, Europam scilicet, vocari audit? Num tergiuersatur & moras nectit, eo quod antea semel & iterum docere prohibitus esset? Minime gentium. Imo mox profectionem instituit, & diuina vocationi se totum accommodat, tandemq; recto & felici cursu ad Philippos, celeberrimam coloniam peruenit. Quo exemplo admonemur, absq; Dei quidem vocatione nihil temere instituendum, at vbi de illa certi sumus, mature faciendum esse quod dominus iubet. Adeo enim illæ procrastinatores auersatur, vt ne pietatis prætextum patienter ferat, si sub hoc vocationem nostram negligere velimus, quemadmodum illius exemplo docemur, qui ne patrem quidem sepelire permissus fuit, cum a Christo ad verbi ministerium vocaretur. Luc.9.cap. Atqui hac vicissim commodissima ratio est, res feliciter agendi, si in Dei vocationem respicientes, hanc bona fide & sedulo sectemur. Nam qui suis consilijs freti, ad vanitatem respiciunt (vt Dauides ait) non possunt non graviter impingere. Faxit Deus, vt huius memores, vocationem nostram singuli ornemus, vt officio nostro in terris defuncti, tandem in cælis viuamus cum Iesu Christo, saluatore nostro: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: But what does Paul do when he hears that he is called by God into Macedonia, to unknown people, and so into another part of the world, namely Europe? Does he shirk and delay, because he had already been forbidden to teach once and again? Not at all. Rather he soon sets out on the journey, accommodates himself wholly to the divine calling, and at last arrives by a straight and happy course at Philippi, a very famous colony. By this example we are warned that nothing should be undertaken rashly apart from God's calling, but once we are sure of that calling, we should promptly do what the Lord commands. For he shuns those procrastinators so much that he will not patiently endure even the pretext of piety, if under that pretext we want to neglect our calling, as we are taught by the example of the man who was not even allowed to bury his father when he was called by Christ to the ministry of the Word. Luke 9. Yet conversely, this is the most convenient way of doing things successfully: if, looking to God's calling, we follow it in good faith and diligently. For those who, relying on their own counsels, look to vanity (as David says) cannot help but stumble badly. May God grant that, mindful of this, each of us adorn our calling, so that, having discharged our duty on earth, we may at last live in heaven with Jesus Christ our Saviour, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CVIII.
units.tr: Homily 108.

units.la: Eramus autem in eadem vrbe diebus aliquot commorantes, & die sabbatorum egressi sumus ex vrbe iuxta flumen, vbi solebat esse precatio, & sedentes loquebamur mulieribus quæ conuenerant. Et quædam mulier, nomine Lydia, purpurarum venditrix, ciuitatis Thyatirorum colens Deum, audiuit: cuius dominus aperuit cor, vt intenderet his, quæ dicebantur à Paulo. Cum autem baptizata esset & domus eius, deprecata est, dicens: Si iudicastis me fidelem domino esse, introite in domum meam, & manete. Et adegit nos.
units.tr: We stayed in that city for some days, and on the Sabbath day we went out of the city, beside a river where prayer was customarily made, and we sat down and talked with the women who had gathered there. A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who worshipped God, was listening, and the Lord opened her heart to attend to what was said by Paul. When she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, saying: "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay." And she persuaded us.

units.la: Dum Paulus à Deo per angelum vocatus in Macedoniam transijt, vt illius gentis hominibus euangelium prædicaret. Quo exemplo partim euangelij dignitas asseritur, partim docetur, ex mera gratia nobis salute obtingere. Nam si Macedones spectemus, eadem illorum, quæ & aliarum gentium fuit conditio, quas Paulus alibi potestati tenebrarum subiectas, idololatras, immani peccatorum seruitute oppressas, & proinde à Deo alienas fuisse scribit. Accedit nunc, quod ne cogitantibus quidem de vera salutis ratione Deus Paulum doctorem transmittit. Sed quid in Philippis, prima Macedoniæ ciuitate egerit, videamus.
units.tr: Paul went over into Macedonia when he was called by God through an angel, so that he might preach the gospel to the people of that nation. From this example the dignity of the gospel is asserted in part, and in part it is taught that salvation comes to us from pure grace. For if we look at the Macedonians, their condition was the same as that of the other nations, whom Paul elsewhere describes as subject to the power of darkness, idolaters, oppressed by the monstrous slavery of sin, and therefore alienated from God. Moreover, God sends Paul as teacher even to those who were not thinking at all about the true way of salvation. But let us see what he did at Philippi, the first city of Macedonia.

units.la: Eramus (inquit Lucas) in eadem vrbe diebus aliquot commorantes. Moræ autem huius causa fuit (vt omnes circumstantiæ docent) quòd nulla sese offerret prædicandi occasio, quam apostoli vbiq; venabantur. Quare tandem hanc extra vrbem quærere cœperunt. Egressi enim ad flumen diebus sabbatorum, mulieribus, quæ illic ex more ad preces publicas conuenire solebant, euangelium prædicauere, EST verò hoc cumprimis memorabile exemplum, quo docemur, vt Deus suorum fidem & constantiam exercere soleat. Nam vt dictum est, per angelum vocatus erat apostolus, qui quasi conmunem patriæ totius causam ageret, opem postulauerat. Quare sperarat aliquis, Macedones aduenientem Paulum summa alacritate & publica lætitiæ significatione exceperuros, iamq; omnium mentes ad percipiendam euangelij lucem paratas esse. Sed adeò fallit hæc spes, vt in celeberrima & populosissima vrbe ne vnus quidem euangelio aures præbeat, nec per dies aliquot multum captata sese offerat prædicandi occasio. Extra vrbem verò solæ mulieres verbum audiunt, sed ita vt ex omnibus illis vna tantùmodo Lydia, eaq; peregrina, fide donetur. Quis ergo non lusoriam fuisse putaret Pauli vocationem, cuius nullus omnino effectus fore videbatur? Sed solet Deus in sua vocatione ambulantibus multa obijcere, quæ hanc impedire & remorari possint, vt suorum fidem probet, illos ad constantiam erudiat, & per aduersa quæuis eluctari doceat. Ita Moses ad liberandum populum missus multa sibi obijci sentit, quæ cum Dei voluntate siue decreto pugnare videbantur. Nam angelus domini ob neglectam in filio circuncisionem illi mortem machinatur, & non Pharaonem modò postulationi suæ iniquum, verumetiam Israelitas rebelles & murmuratores habet: iamq; Ægyptum egressus mare occurrit, sic vt ipsa rerum natura aduersus Mosen pugnare videretur. At omnia aduersa vincit fidei constantia & firmum diuina mandata exequendi propositum. Ita Danidi ad regni solium vocato manus Saul hostis insurgit, cuius tyrannide prius patrijs finibus pellitur, quàm ad regni fastigium perueniat. Et multa huius generis quotidie accidunt, quibus fides nostra tentari consueuit. At nostrum est constanti animo pergere, & Dei opem firma spe expectare, nec illum vel promissionibus suis vel nostris conatibus defuturum sentiemus.
units.tr: "We were," says Luke, "staying in that city for some days." The cause of this delay was (as all the circumstances show) that no opportunity for preaching presented itself, and the apostles were looking for one everywhere. So at last they began to seek it outside the city. For going out to the river on the Sabbath days, they preached the gospel to the women who were accustomed to gather there for public prayer. This is an especially memorable example, by which we are taught that God is wont to exercise the faith and constancy of his own people. For, as has been said, the apostle had been called through an angel, and he had asked for help as though pleading the common cause of his whole homeland. So someone might have hoped that the Macedonians would receive Paul on his arrival with the greatest eagerness and public signs of joy, and that the minds of all were now ready to receive the light of the gospel. But this hope so deceives that in that most famous and populous city not even one person lent an ear to the gospel, and after several days of eager waiting no opportunity for preaching offered itself. Outside the city, however, only women heard the word, and even among all of them only one, Lydia, and she a foreigner, was given faith. Who, then, would not have thought that Paul's calling was a joke, since it seemed to have no effect at all? But God is accustomed to throw many obstacles in the way of those who walk in his calling, which can hinder and delay it, so that he may test the faith of his own, train them to constancy, and teach them to struggle through any adversities whatever. So Moses, sent to free the people, finds many things thrown in his way which seemed to conflict with the will or decree of God. For the angel of the Lord plots his death because he had neglected the circumcision of his son, and not only does Pharaoh oppose his request, but he also has the Israelites rebellious and murmuring against him; and when he has left Egypt, the sea confronts him, so that nature itself seemed to fight against Moses. But the constancy of faith and the firm purpose of carrying out the divine commands overcome all adversities. So too, when David was called to the throne of the kingdom, Saul rose up as an enemy against him, and by Saul's tyranny he was driven from his native land before he reached the summit of the kingdom. Many things of this kind happen every day by which our faith is wont to be tested. But it is ours to press on with a steadfast mind and to await God's help with firm hope, and we shall feel that he will be wanting neither in his promises nor in our efforts.

units.la: Porrò memorabile conuersionis exemplum in Lydia proponitur, quod propter multiplicem doctrinam per singulas circumstantias Euangelista diligentissimè describit. Et quidem à persona descriptione exorsus mulierem fuisse ait, vt eius sexus admoneat, per quem peccatum in mundum introiuit. Conditione autem purpurarum venditrix fuit, & mercaturam exercuit, quæ fastui potius & superbiæ, quàm necessitati hominum inseruiebat: vt iam de auaritia, impostura, dolis & aliis vitijs, quibus fere istud hominum genus laborat, nihil dicamus. Adhæc peregrina erat, ex Thyatirinorum (quæ Lydiæ vrbs est) oriunda. Commemorantur hæc, vt discamus, Deum nullius ordinis aut conditionis homines negligere, sed ex omni ordine eos gratia & fauore suo completi, qui ad ipsum conuerti cupiunt. Docent idem infinita alia huius generis exempla. Nam Christus alibi cum meretricibus de salutis ratione disserit. Iohan. 4. Luc. 7. Alibi publicanis ad cœlorum regnum viam aperit. Matth. 9. Luc. 19. Idem nec pharisæorum ordinem fastidit, quando Nicodemum noctu in colloquium admittit, & eundem amicissimè instituit. Quid, quòd Centurionem, qui ipsius supplicio præerat fui cognitione illustrauit? Matth. 27. Vsus horum est, ne propter vitæ genus, quod aliquando secuti sumus, de Dei gratia desperemus, quando nemini non salutis ianuâ patere conflat, qui non sulcato illius amore ardet. Elucet præterea in hoc exemplo Dei consilium, qui filij sui regnum parum initijs prouehit. Lydiam enim eius ecclesiæ primitias esse vult, cuius fidem postea Paulus satis commendare nequit. Ita Christus ex piscatorum & publicanorum ordine primos discipulos elegit. Nec temere fieri putemus, quòd Christi regnum in terris, quoad externa speciem, humile, vile & contemptum est. Inde enim colligitur, illud non esse de hoc mundo, nec ea quæ mundi sunt in hoc quæri debere. Patet item ijs, qui Christi conforites esse cupiunt, non in carnis prudentia, nobilitate, splendore aut alijs eius generis rebus, sed in solo domino esse gloriandu, vt multis Paulus in priori ad Corinth. epist. Cap. 1. docuit. Habes hic quod ijs respondeas, qui euangelij doctrinâ & fidem eo nomine profitentur, quòd non nisi infimæ sortis homines & ignobile vulgus illam amplecti soleant: eodem nimirum argumento vtentes, quo Pharisæi olim & scribæ aduersus seruos suos, qui Christi doctrinam commendabant. mendabant, vti sunt. Ioan. 7. Quin potius ipsum Christum audiunt dicentem: Gratias ago tibi pater, quòd abscondëris haec à sapientibus & prudentibus, & reuelaris ea paruulis. Certè pater, sic fuit bona voluntas apud te. Matth. 11. Luc. 10.
units.tr: Moreover, a memorable example of conversion is set forth in Lydia, which the evangelist describes most carefully, with many teachings drawn from each circumstance. And indeed, beginning with a description of her person, he says she was a woman, so that he may remind us of her sex, through which sin entered the world. She was a seller of purple cloth by occupation, and she engaged in trade, which served the vanity and pride of men rather than their necessity; to say nothing now of the greed, deceit, trickery and other vices to which that class of men is almost always prone. Besides, she was a foreigner, a native of Thyatira (which is a city of Lydia). These things are recorded so that we may learn that God does not neglect people of any rank or condition, but from every rank he fills with his grace and favour those who desire to be turned to him. Countless other examples of this kind teach the same. For Christ elsewhere discourses with harlots about the way of salvation (John 4; Luke 7); elsewhere he opens the way to the kingdom of heaven for tax collectors (Matt. 9; Luke 19). Likewise he does not despise the order of the Pharisees, when he admits Nicodemus to conversation by night and instructs him most kindly. What of the fact that he enlightened the centurion who was in charge of his execution with the knowledge of himself (Matt. 27)? The use of these examples is that we should not despair of God's grace because of the manner of life we once followed, since it is clear that the door of salvation stands open to anyone who is not cold in his love for him. Moreover, in this example the counsel of God is evident, who advances the kingdom of his Son little by little at the start. For he wills that Lydia be the firstfruits of his church, whose faith Paul afterwards could not sufficiently commend. So Christ chose his first disciples from the order of fishermen and tax collectors. Nor should we think it happens by chance that Christ's kingdom on earth, as to outward appearance, is humble, base and despised. For from this it is gathered that it is not of this world, nor should the things of the world be sought in it. It is also plain to those who wish to be fellow-members of Christ that they must glory not in the wisdom of the flesh, nobility, splendour or other things of that kind, but in the Lord alone, as Paul taught at length in his first letter to the Corinthians, chapter 1. Here you have what to answer to those who profess the doctrine and faith of the gospel with the objection that only people of the lowest rank and the common crowd are wont to embrace it, arguing from the same reasoning by which the Pharisees and scribes once argued against their own servants who commended the teaching of Christ (John 7). Rather, let them hear Christ himself saying: "I thank you, Father, that you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight" (Matt. 11; Luke 10).

units.la: Caeteri[?] post descriptam Lydiae personam, modum & ordinem conuersionis ipsius commemorat. In quo primum locum habet, quòd religiosa & Dei timens fuisse dicitur: nimirum vt multi, alij inter gentes & Iudaeos, qui tamen veram religionis & salutis rationem ignorabant, eoque acrius veritati resistebant, quò maiori zelo suas superstitiones defendebant. Interim necesse hoc est in salutis causa, vt animi à Dei timore non alieni, sed ad veritatem amplectendam proclives, adeoque verae religionis appetentes sint. Nisi enim terra bona fuerit, verbi semen in illa germinare nequaquam poterit. Luc. 8. capite. Atqui non ita hoc accipiendum est, quasi ex nobis ipsis sit haec animorum promptitudo siue facilitas. Ex nobis ipsis enim ne ad cogitandum quidem idonei sumus, & cordis humani figmenta ab ineunte aetate prava esse, ipse Deus testis est. Dei ergo opus & donum est, si ad religionis & veritatis studium homines propensi sint, à quo alias ob ingenitam sibi corruptionem totis animis abhorrent. Deinde Paulum docentem audiuit Lydia. Eo igitur medio & organo vtitur, quo Deus fidem dare & excitare consueuit. Haec siquidem ex auditu est, auditus autem per verbum Dei. Rom. 10. Huic ergo eos studere necesse est, quicunque in salutis cognitione proficere volunt, nec audiendi sunt, qui nouas quasdam revelationes expectant. In scripturis enim nobis loquitur Deus, quae qui audire dedignantur, fere diabolo praeda sunt, qui praestigiosis & luxoriis reuelationibus miserè deceptos seducit. Postremò Dominus Lydiae cor aperuisse dicitur, vt iis animum intenderet, quae à Paulo dicebantur. Nisi enim id fiat, frustra verbum vel praedicatur vel auditur, de quo quia iam saepe dictum est, pluribus agere in praesenti minimè necessarium videtur. Quòd si quis interroget, cur non aliorum quoque corda aperuerit Deus, illi cum Paulo respondemus: Atqui ô homo, tu quis es, qui exaduerso respondes Deo? Quis prior dedit Deo, & reddetur ei? Arcana enim Dei consilia nos non curiosius scrutari, sed in illius immensam Dei bonitatem, iustitiam, veritatem & sapientiam admirari conuenit. Nostrum est, ex hoc loco verae conuersionis ordinem agnoscere, qui in tribus hisce potissimum consistit, vt animos religionis sensu imbutos habeamus, vt verbum audiamus, & vt Dei spiritu illuminemur.
units.tr: After describing Lydia's person, Luke records the manner and order of her conversion. In this, the first place belongs to the fact that she is said to have been religious and God-fearing: no doubt as were many others among the Gentiles and the Jews, who nonetheless were ignorant of the true way of religion and of salvation, and who resisted the truth all the more fiercely the more zealously they defended their superstitions. Meanwhile, it is necessary for salvation that minds should not be alien to the fear of God, but inclined to embrace the truth, and so desirous of the true religion. For unless the ground is good, the seed of the word cannot possibly sprout in it (Luke 8). Yet this must not be understood as if this readiness or docility of minds comes from ourselves. For we are not even fit to think of anything from ourselves, and God himself bears witness that the imaginations of the human heart are evil from childhood. It is therefore God's work and gift if men are inclined to the pursuit of religion and truth, from which otherwise, on account of the corruption innate in them, they turn away with their whole souls. Next, Lydia heard Paul teaching. She therefore uses that means and instrument by which God is wont to give and kindle faith. For faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of God (Rom. 10). Therefore all who wish to make progress in the knowledge of salvation must devote themselves to this, nor should those be listened to who look for some new revelations. For God speaks to us in the Scriptures, and those who disdain to hear them are for the most part prey to the devil, who seduces those whom he has miserably deceived with deceptive and wanton revelations. Lastly, it is said that the Lord opened Lydia's heart so that she attended to the things that were said by Paul. For unless this happens, the word is preached or heard in vain. Since this has often been said already, it seems in the present context by no means necessary to speak at more length. But if anyone asks why God did not also open the hearts of the others, we answer with Paul: "But, O man, who are you that answer back to God? Who has first given to God, that it should be repaid to him?" For it is fitting that we should not pry too curiously into the secret counsels of God, but marvel at his immense goodness, justice, truth and wisdom. It is ours to recognise from this passage the order of true conversion, which consists chiefly in these three things: that we have minds imbued with a sense of religion, that we hear the word, and that we are enlightened by the Spirit of God.

units.la: Restat vt verae fidei effectus consyderemus, qui in Lydia se exeruerunt. Primum ipsa baptiza-turi iuxta Christi praeceptum & morem ecclesiae traditum. Comprehendit hoc fidei confessionem, qua & priscina superstitioni valedicit, & Christo nomen dat, inter ecclesiae ipsius membra censeri volens. Simul vero exemplo hoc admonemur, sanctos sacramenta nequaquam contemnere, sed ijs religiose vti, tum quòd ea à Christo instituta esse intelligunt, tum quòd his salutis beneficium, cuius nobis author Christus est, obsignari gaudent. At non contenta suo baptismo Lydia, domum quoque suam & omnem familiam baptizari curat. Est enim hoc proprium fidelibus omnibus, quòd vna secum omnes homines salutis consortes fieri cupiunt, maximè vero eos, quos sibi diuinitus commissos esse norunt. Nec id priuato affectu faciunt, sed Dei praeceptum sequuntur, cuius haec perpetua voluntas est, vt nostros omnes illi consecremus. Ita Abraham non seipsum modò, sed omnes in sua familia mares ex Dei mandato circuncidit. Et in lege patribus familiàs mandatur, vt in Dei praeceptis suos erudire satagant. Vide Deut. 6. Psal. 78. Et quod illis mandatum fuit, hoc ipsum ad se quoque pertinere magistratus putent, & in hoc incumbant, vt sublatis superstitionibus vera religionis studium in populo floreat: quod sanctissimos reges, Dauidem, Asam, Iosaphat, Ezechiam, Iosiam & horum similes, diligenter fecisse legimus. Et sanè manifesta impietatis nota non caret, si quis ita in alios imperium obtinere velit, vt Deum suo iure, quo omnes homines sibi vendicat, spoliet. Postremò apostolos domum suam inuitat Lydia, & illis hospitium offert, idque serio. Si (inquit) iudicauistis me fidelem Domino esse, introite in domum meam, & manete. Quae verba obtestationis vim habent, adeo vt oblatum beneficium apostoli respuere non possent, nisi simul illam damnarent, & Christiano nomine indignam censerent. Quanquam principio domum illius subire ciuiliter renuant, tum ne (quod impostores solent) mulierculorum simplicitate abuti, & illarum fortunis insidiari viderentur, tum quòd nemi-nem granare vnquam Paulus voluerit, sicuti non semel testatur. 1. Corinth. 9. 2. Thess. 3. Caterum mutatione sua fidem charitate flagrantem & intrepida animi constantia munitam Lydia prodit. Charitatis enim est, quòd eos excipere & alere cupit, à quibus illa salutis doctrinam hauserat. Ae rursum fortis animi indicium est, quòd peregrina nouæ fidei & religionis doctores in domum suam recipit, id quod sine periculo fieri non posse, facile intelligebat. Sed illud fidei ingenium esse, vt nec fortunis nec corpori timeat, modò Christi gloria propagari possit. Inspiciant quaso in ... rius huius exemplum, qui hodie fidem iactitant, & mox videbunt, quàm procul à fidei ingenio absint. Oremus itaque Dominum, vt nostrum omnium corda aperire dignetur, vt vera fide instructi, Christum tota vita referamus, & cum eodem in cælis viuamus: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: It remains for us to consider the effects of true faith, which showed themselves in Lydia. First, she was ready to be baptized, in accordance with Christ's command and the custom handed down in the Church. This involved a confession of faith, by which she renounced her former superstition, gave her name to Christ, and wished to be counted among the members of the Church itself. At the same time, this example reminds us that the saints never despise the sacraments but use them devoutly, both because they understand that the sacraments were instituted by Christ and because they rejoice that through them the benefit of salvation, of which Christ is the author, is sealed to us. But Lydia was not content with her own baptism; she also saw to it that her household and her whole family were baptized. For it is characteristic of all believers that they wish all people to share with them in salvation, and especially those whom they know have been entrusted to them by God. Nor do they do this out of private feeling, but they follow God's command, whose constant will is that we should all be consecrated to him. So Abraham circumcised not only himself but, by God's command, all the males in his household. And in the law, heads of families were commanded to take care to instruct their own in the precepts of God. See Deut. 6, Psal. 78. And magistrates should think that what was commanded of those heads of families applies to them as well, and should devote themselves to this, that with superstitions removed, zeal for true religion may flourish among the people. We read that the most holy kings, David, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, Josiah and others like them, did this diligently. Indeed, it bears a clear mark of impiety if anyone wishes to hold such authority over others that he robs God of the right by which he claims all people for himself. Finally, Lydia invites the apostles to her house and offers them hospitality, and does so earnestly. "If," she says, "you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay." These words of entreaty carry such force that the apostles could not refuse the kindness offered without at the same time condemning it and judging her unworthy of the Christian name. Yet at first they refuse to enter her house in a civil manner, both so that they would not seem, as impostors usually do, to take advantage of the simplicity of silly women and to lay snares for their wealth, and because Paul never wished to be a burden to anyone, as he testifies more than once. See 1 Cor. 9, 2 Thess. 3. But by her change of heart Lydia shows her faith to be aflame with love and fortified by an unshaken constancy of spirit. For it is a sign of love that she desires to receive and feed those from whom she had drawn the teaching of salvation. And again, it is a sign of a brave spirit that she receives strangers, the teachers of the new faith and religion, into her house, though she easily understood that this could not be done without danger. Such is the nature of faith: that it fears neither loss of goods nor bodily harm, provided only that the glory of Christ can be spread abroad. Let them look, I beg, to the example of this … man, who today boast of faith, and they will soon see how far they are from the nature of faith. Let us therefore pray the Lord that he may deign to open the hearts of us all, so that, instructed in true faith, we may bear witness to Christ throughout our lives and live with him in heaven, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CIX.
units.tr: HOMILY 109.

units.la: Accidit autem euntibus nobis ad precationem, vt puella quædam habens spiritum Pythonis, occurreret nobis, quæ quæstum magnum præstabat dominis suis diuinando. Hæc subsecuta Paulum ac nos, clamabat dicens: Isti homines serui Dei excelsissimi sunt, qui annunciant nobis viam salutis. Hoc autem faciebat multis diebus. Paulus autem ægrè ferens, & conuersus spiritui dixit: Præcipio tibi in nomine Iesu Christi, vt exeas ab ea. Et exiit eadem hora.
units.tr: As we were going to prayer, it happened that a certain slave girl with a spirit of Python met us. She brought her masters a great profit by fortune-telling. She followed Paul and us, crying out: "These men are servants of the most high God, who proclaim to us the way of salvation." She did this for many days. But Paul, greatly troubled, turned and said to the spirit: "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her." And it came out that very hour.

units.la: VÀmuis Dei filius, Iesus Christus, mortis suæ merito diaboli regnum ita euerterit, vt nulla huic contra ipsum vires sint reliquæ: non cessat tamen is pro veteri suo ingenio Christi regnum oppugnare, & quemadmodum hic nihil eorum intermisit, quæ ad humani generis redemptionem faciebant, ita vicissim nihil intentatum relinquit satan, vt homines à Christo saluatore & salutis via abstrahat. Exemplum huius rei cumprimis euidens in præsenti historia proponitur. Postquam enim ad Philippenses Paulus venit, illius prædicatione ad fidem conuersa Lydia, purpurarum venditrix, præclaros fidei fructus edere cœpit. Nam gratitudinis officium apostolis exoluens, illos domum suam inuitat & hospitio excipit. Qua occasione fit, vt officio suo strenuè fungentes apostoli, quotidie alios quoq; discipulos lucrifaciant, sicq; ecclesia colligi incipiat, quemadmodum in fine capitis patebit. Id verò intolerabile putans satan, primis regni Christi initijs resistere tentat: & primò quidem dolo malo & insidiosis blanditijs rem aggreditur, mox verò (vbi primus conatus non succeßit) aperta vi apostolos oppugnat, & tandem vrbe eijcit. In præsenti tamen primum duntaxat congressum videbimus.
units.tr: Although the Son of God, Jesus Christ, by the merit of his death so overthrew the devil's kingdom that he has no power left against him, Satan does not cease, in his old nature, to attack Christ's kingdom. Just as Christ left nothing undone that pertained to the redemption of the human race, so in turn Satan leaves nothing untried to draw men away from Christ the Savior and from the way of salvation. The present history sets before us a very clear example of this. After Paul came to the Philippians, Lydia, a seller of purple cloth, was converted to the faith through his preaching and began to bear splendid fruits of faith. For she paid the apostles the duty of gratitude, inviting them to her house and receiving them as guests. As a result, the apostles, diligently performing their office, daily won over other disciples as well, and so a church began to be gathered, as will be shown at the end of the chapter. Satan, thinking this intolerable, tries to resist the first beginnings of Christ's kingdom. At first he attacks the matter with malicious cunning and insidious flattery; then, when the first attempt fails, he openly assails the apostles with force and at last expels them from the city. In the present passage, however, we shall see only the first encounter.

units.la: Orditur autem historiam Lucas ab eius persona descriptione, cuius opera in hoc certamine fuit vsus est. Fuit hæc puella, Pythonis spiritu afflata, quæ diuinando quæstum magnum faciebat dominis suis. Porrò Pythonis spiritum Apollinis numen esse gentiles credebant, cui ex Pythone serpente, ipsius sagittis confecto, nomen istud obuenisse, poetæ fabulantur. Apollinem verò vaticinijs præfuisse notius est, quàm vt multis demonstrari oporteat. Celebrantur enim vbiq; Delphi, Claros, Delos & infinita alia eius generis loca, in quibus sub Apollinis nomine satan olim oracula edidit. Idem priuatas quoq; personas afflare solebat, vt subito furore correpti, ambiguas voces ederent, quæ superstitiosi homines pro fide digni vaticinijs amplectebantur. Et eò tandem deuentum est, vt stulti homines nihil, nisi vatibus istis consulerent, sibi tentandum esse putarent, & ad illorum oracula in quauis necessitate concurrerent. Quare fieri non potuit, quin ex ea re ingens quæstus colligeretur, cum ea sit humani ingenij natura, vt nos nullius vel laboris vel sumptus pigeat, in ijs rebus, quæ curiositati nostræ aliqua ex parte satisfacere videntur. Et eius quidem generis organum apud Philippenses veritatis doctoribus fata opponit, vt illos vel cordatioribus suspectos, vel imperito & rudi vulgo inuisos reddat. Interim obseruandum venit, quibus armis regnum inter homines affectet satan: mendacijs nimirum, & curiosis siue fatidicis artibus, quibus prophetiæ spiritum imitatur, vt ea occasione à Dei verbo homines abstrahat, quod nobis vnica debebat esse in rebus agendis regula. Harū artium professores in Ægypto Magi fuerunt, quos Mosi restitisse historia sacra docet. Exod. 7. 8. &c. Inter hos Balaam quoq; censeri meretur, quàmuis veritatis studium egregiè simulet. Tales fuerunt inter Chananæos multi & varij vates, quos excindere lex diuina iubet. Ad quem ordinem referri debent augures,
units.tr: Luke begins the history by describing the person whose work the devil used in this contest. This girl was inspired by the spirit of Python and by her fortune-telling brought her masters a great profit. The poets tell that the Gentiles believed the spirit of Python to be the divinity of Apollo, to whom that name came from the serpent Python, slain by his arrows. That Apollo presided over prophecies is too well known to need proof from many sources. Delphi, Claros, Delos and countless other places of this kind are celebrated everywhere, where in times past Satan gave oracles under the name of Apollo. He was also accustomed to inspire private persons, so that, seized by sudden frenzy, they uttered ambiguous words, which superstitious people embraced as prophecies worthy of belief. At last things came to such a pass that foolish men thought they must consult nothing but these seers, and in every need they ran to their oracles. It could not but happen that great profit was gathered from this, since it is the nature of the human mind that we do not mind any labor or expense in those matters which seem in some way to satisfy our curiosity. Among the Philippians, Satan set this kind of instrument against the teachers of the truth, to make them suspect to the more sensible and hateful to the unskilled and crude crowd. Meanwhile, we must observe with what weapons Satan aims at his kingdom among men: namely lies and curious or prophetic arts, by which he imitates the spirit of prophecy, so that on that pretext he may draw men away from the Word of God, which ought to be our one rule in conducting affairs. The practitioners of these arts in Egypt were the magicians, whom sacred history teaches resisted Moses (Exod. 7, 8, etc.). Among these Balaam also deserves to be counted, although he cleverly feigns zeal for the truth. Many and various seers of this kind were among the Canaanites, whom the divine law orders to be destroyed. To this class belong the augurs,

units.la: Puella Pythonica, diaboli organum. augures, aruspices, somniorum interpretes, genethliaci, astrologi, necromantæ, geomantæ, hydromantæ & infiniti alij, quorum consilia & dictata apud reges quoq; & magistratus in regnorum & rerumpub. administratione summam authoritatem habuerunt. Et sane si rem probè expendamus, vix alia in re regni sui vires potentius satan exercuit, quàm oraculorum vanitate, qua totum terrarum orbem seculi aliquot dementauit. Et hodie vates quosdam frequenter excitat, qui vel futurorum cognitionem sibi ipsis vendicant, vel incantationum præstigijs morbos pellere & alia quædam humanus viribus impossibilia conficere tentant. At quærat aliquis, cur hæc fieri olim Deus permiserit, & hodie permittat? Sed in promptu causa est. Quia enim gentes olim Dei revelationibus non contentæ, humani ingenij acumine diuinæ maiestatis mysteria inuestigare conatæ sunt, meruit illarũ audacia, vt in reprobum sensum traditæ, diabolicis dolis & impostuṙis miserè seducerentur. Vide Rom.1. Idem nouissimo tempore euenturum esse Paulus monuit, quando Antichristo in eos duntaxat ius fore dicit, qui veritatem disinitus oblatam ampletti noluerint. 2. Thess.2. Quod si Philippenses inspicias, dignos fuisse deprehendes, quos diaboli furijs agitata puella seduceret. Tanta enim in hanc illorum fuit liberalitas, vt haud vulgarem inde quæstũ haberent puellæ domini. At ijdem apostolos Christi ita negligunt, vt hospitio illi caruissent, nisi Lydia, quæ & ipsa peregrina erat, illos in domum suam recepisset. Eadem nostri seculi ingratitudo est & peruersitas. Nolunt enim veritatis lucem amplecti homines, & qui in mutas imagines, in impostores sacrificulos, in exorcistas & incantatores, in diuinos & hariolos, ingentes sumptus faciunt, ijs nimium videtur, quicquid in veritatis doctrinam insumitur. Digni ergo sunt, qui satanæ præda fiant, cuius dolo tu fortunas suas diripi, tum corpora quoq; diuexari sentiant. Discamus itaq; Dei legem audire, quæ ab omnibus huius generis impostoribus cauendum esse docet, & vnius verbi Dei studium præcipit. Vide Deut.18. Leuit.20. Isa.8. Hoc qui facere negligunt, Saulis exemplo discant, quid ipsos sperare oporteat. Vide 1.Sam.28.
units.tr: The Pythonic girl, an instrument of the devil. augurs, haruspices, interpreters of dreams, casters of horoscopes, astrologers, necromancers, geomancers, hydromancers, and countless others, whose counsels and dictates have held the highest authority even with kings and magistrates in the government of kingdoms and commonwealths. And indeed, if we weigh the matter rightly, Satan has hardly exercised the power of his kingdom more effectively in any other matter than through the vanity of oracles, by which he deluded the whole world for some centuries. And even today he frequently raises up certain seers who either claim for themselves knowledge of future things, or attempt by the tricks of incantations to drive out diseases and to accomplish other things impossible for human powers. But someone may ask: why did God permit these things to happen in times past, and why does he permit them today? The cause is at hand. For since the nations of old, not content with God's revelations, tried to investigate the mysteries of the divine majesty by the keenness of human intellect, their audacity deserved to be given over to a reprobate mind and miserably seduced by diabolical deceits and impostures. See Rom. 1. Paul warned that the same thing would happen in the last times, when he says that Antichrist will have power only over those who were unwilling to embrace the truth offered to them from heaven (2 Thess. 2). Indeed, if you look at the Philippians, you will find that they deserved to be deceived by the girl agitated by the devil's frenzy. For they were so generous to her that her masters gained no small profit from her. Yet these same people so neglected the apostles of Christ that they would have gone without lodging, had not Lydia, herself also a foreigner, received them into her house. This same ingratitude and perversity exists in our own age. For men are unwilling to embrace the light of truth, and those who spend huge sums on dumb images, on impostor priests, on exorcists and enchanters, on diviners and soothsayers, think that whatever is spent on the teaching of the truth is too much. Therefore they deserve to become the prey of Satan, by whose deceit they feel their fortunes plundered and then their bodies also tormented. Let us learn, then, to hear the law of God, which teaches us to beware of all impostors of this kind and enjoins the study of the one Word of God alone. See Deut. 18, Lev. 20, Isa. 8. Let those who neglect this learn from the example of Saul what they ought to expect (see 1 Sam. 28).

units.la: Sed postulat tempus, vt quid per puellam hanc egerit satan, videamus. Hæc apostolos, ex more ad precationem euntes, subsecuta, illis acclamabat, dicens: Isti homines serui Dei excelsissimi sunt, qui annunciant nobis viam salutis. Quid (inquis) audio? Hæc ne diaboli, apostolos oppugnatūs, vox est? Maximè. Atqui maiori elogio illos ornare non poterat, quando illos Dei seruos & salutis præconès esse fatetur. Cæterum non tam verba, quàm mentem & institutum diaboli, cuius suggestione hæc dicuntur, inspicere conuenit. Ita enim deprehendes, illum Christo tunc maximè insidiari, quando illius causam tueri videtur. Et in præsenti apostolorum doctrinæ testimonium fert, vt illa apud cordatos omnes (maximè si qui ex Iudæis erant) suspectam reddat. Nouit enim satan, se apud omnes homines mendacem haberi. Eo igitur nomine apostolos Dei seruos & salutis nuncios esse clamat, vt omnibus cordatis suspecti fiant. Deinde hoc etiam quærit, vt si qui apostolis credant, ipsius simul responsis fidem habeant, quibus apostolorum doctrinam commendari audiuerint. At fidem Christi consistere impossibile est, vbi aliquid diabolo tribuitur, cuius destruendi causa Christus in mundum venit. Sub Christi igitur prætextu subrepere conatur, vt paulatim à Christo rursum abstrahat, si qui huic credere incipiant. Adhæc ambitione & inani gloriæ cupiditate apostolorum animos titillare voluit, vt hac incensi, Dei gloriam negligant. Vides ergo quantũ veneni sub honorificæ istius & sanctæ acclamationis prætextu lateat? Hoc ipso propositio illum Christo etiam blanditiũ fuisse, & testimonium tulisse, legimus. Mar.1. Luc.4. Obseruemus autè hoc loco ingenium satanæ, qui veritatis odium mirificè dissimulare, & in lucis angelum se transformare nouit. Suspecta ergo nobis sint quæcunq; ab illo proueniunt. Nec etiam ipsius organis credamus, quantùmuis graviter simul & magnificè sanctos Dei cultores commendent, & sacra verba plenis buccis resonent. Seruit itaq; ijs refutandis locus hic, qui nos papatui abfq; iusta causa tam iniquos esse dicunt, cum in hoc Christi nomen prædicetur, sanctorum laudes celebrentur, scripturæ sacræ lectiones in quotidiano vsu sint, nec quicquam absque diuini nominis inuocatione instituatur. Sed ignorant isti homines, Antichristi sedem in ipsa ecclesia esse debere, nec illud Christi expendunt: Non omnis, qui dicit mihi, Domine Domine, &c. Matth.7. Quòd si rem penitius inspiciamus, sub religionis & ecclesiæ Christianæ prætextu & veniendo Christi nomine, illos non aliud quærere patebit, quàm vt humanis traditionibus fidem faciendo, suam tyrannidem stabiliant. Confutantur præterea hoc loco, qui exorcistis & incantatoribus, siue diuinaculis, patrocinantur, quòd ab illis tremenda Dei nomina inuocari, & grauissimas scri-
units.tr: But the time demands that we see what Satan accomplished through this girl. She followed the apostles as they went, as was their custom, to prayer, and cried out to them: "These men are servants of the most high God, who proclaim to us the way of salvation." "What," you say, "do I hear? Is this the voice of the devil attacking the apostles?" Most certainly. Yet he could not have praised them with a greater commendation, since he confesses that they are servants of God and heralds of salvation. But it is more fitting to look not so much at the words as at the mind and purpose of the devil, by whose prompting they are spoken. For you will find that he is then most of all laying snares for Christ, when he seems to defend his cause. And in the present case he bears testimony to the apostles' teaching in order to make it suspect to all the sensible people (especially those who were Jews). For Satan knows that he is regarded as a liar by all men. Therefore he calls the apostles servants of God and messengers of salvation, so that they may become suspect to all the wise. Next, he also seeks this: that if any should believe the apostles, they might at the same time give credence to his own answers, by which they would hear the teaching of the apostles being commended. But faith in Christ cannot stand where something is attributed to the devil, whose destruction is the reason Christ came into the world. Under the pretext of Christ, therefore, he tries to creep in, so that he may gradually draw away from Christ again those who begin to believe him. Besides, he wished to stir the minds of the apostles with ambition and the desire for empty glory, so that, inflamed by this, they would neglect the glory of God. Do you see, then, how much poison lies hidden under the pretext of this honorable and holy acclamation? We read that by this very same means the devil also flattered Christ and gave testimony to him (Mark 1; Luke 4). Let us observe in this place the nature of Satan, who knows how wonderfully to disguise his hatred of the truth and to transform himself into an angel of light. Therefore whatever comes from him should be suspect to us. Nor should we trust his instruments, however gravely and magnificently they commend the holy worshippers of God and resound sacred words with full cheeks. This passage serves to refute those who say that we Papists are unjustly so hostile, since in their case the name of Christ is preached, the praises of the saints are celebrated, the readings of Holy Scripture are in daily use, and nothing is undertaken without invoking the name of God. But these men do not understand that the seat of Antichrist must be in the church itself, nor do they weigh that saying of Christ: "Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, etc." (Matt. 7). But if we look more deeply into the matter, it will be plain that under the pretext of religion and of the Christian church, and coming in the name of Christ, they seek nothing else than to establish their tyranny by making human traditions credible. Moreover, in this place are refuted those who defend exorcists and enchanters, or fortune-tellers, because they hear the awful names of God invoked by them and the most solemn sentences of Scripture muttered.

units.la: Satan veritati fert testimonium. ptura sententias demurmurari audiunt. Atqui id mirum non est, quando aduersus Christum Dominum scripturas allegare diabolus ausus fuit. Imò eò grauius ab illis peccatur, quòd impietati sua Dei nomen praetexant, cuius abusum & prophanationem ille impunitam abire non finit.
units.tr: Satan bears witness to the truth. They hear the sentences of Scripture muttered by these people. Yet this is no wonder, since the devil himself dared to allege Scripture against Christ the Lord. Indeed, they sin all the more gravely in that they cloak their impiety with the name of God, whose abuse and profanation he does not allow to go unpunished.

units.la: Porrò quid de omnibus istis sentiendum sit, Pauli exemplum praefens docet. Is enim puellam ipsis vera acclamantem fert quidem ad tempus, nimirum spiritus suggestionem expectans, ne quid caeco & praecipiti affectu peccaret: tandem verò sancta indignatione & zelo inflammatus, clamantem increpat, & spiritum malignum Christi nomine eijcit. Quod exemplum quàmuis omnium institutioni seruiat, in primis tamen verbi ministros officij sui admonet, quibus veritatis studium itacommendatum esse debet, ut nihil ferant quod huic aliqua ex parte derogare queat, etiamsi cum ipsorum laude & gloria coniunctum sit. Nam (ut supra monuimus) solet blanditijs eos aggredi sa-tan, quos alioqui inuitos esse nouit. Quae causa est, quòd Christus malignos spiritus loqui vetuit, nec illorum testimonijs voluit commendari. Quare vehementer errant, qui cum ijs colluduntquos à veritate alienissimos esse constat. Occultant illi interdum virus suum, sed eò grauius nocent, quò magis blandiuntur. Christiani hominis est neminem amicum habere, quem Christi inimicum & Christiana doctrinae impatientem esse nouerit. Caeterum cumprimis memorabile est, quòd Christum lesum diabolo opponit Paulus, & quòd is cedere cogitur, ut primum Christi nomen enunciari audiuit. Est hoc irrefragabile potentiae Christi argumentum. Nemo enim potest domum potentis alicuius ingredi, & illius vasa diripere, nisi prius illum deuictum constrinxerit. At Christus Iesus in mundum veniens, huius principem diabolum ita deuicit, ut is audito duntaxat Christi nomine, possessionem suam relinquere, & Christo in hominibus locum dare coactus fuerit. Longè maiorem ergo Christi quàm diaboli potentiam esse, fateamur oportet. Et hinc nos in tentationibus consolationem petere conuenit, ne illum timeamus, cuius adeò nulla est aduersus Christum, cui nos per fidem insiti sumus, potentia. Rursum admonemur hoc loco nihil prorsus Christo cum diabolo commune esse, cum ne testimonium quidem, quantumuis honorificum, ab illo accipere dignetur. Quae enim inter hos communio esse poterit, cum iuxta primam promissionem ideo in mundum Christus venerit, ut diaboli caput conterat, & illius opera destruat? Gene. 3. 1. Iohan. 3. Hoc ipsum verò officij quoq; Christianos admonet, ne quid ipsi cum diabolo commune habeant. Nec enim par est, ut cum diabolo colludant aliqua in re, quicunq; Christo semel nomen dederunt. Fugiant ergo fatidicas artes, quas satanae calliditas & improba hominum curiositas excogitauit. Fugiant incantationum praestigia, quibus ille vel in morbis vel in alijs afflictionibus auxilium pollicetur. Fugiant falsos & prophanos cultus, superstitionem, idololatriam, & quaecunq; à Deo abstrahunt. Exosam habeant peccati tyrannidem, quae libertas à Christo nobis parta euertitur. Vigileut deniq; & resistant diabolo constantes in fide, & recedet ab ipsis: unde fiet: ut illius imperio excusso, vitam Deo probatam ducere, & olim in coelis vina re ac regnare possint cum Iesu Christo, Domino & saluatore nostro: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Paul's example here shows what ought to be thought of all these people. For he indeed tolerates the girl, who was crying out what was true about them, for a while, no doubt waiting for the prompting of the Spirit, lest he sin through a blind and headlong emotion. At last, however, inflamed with holy indignation and zeal, he rebukes her as she cries out and casts out the evil spirit in the name of Christ. Although this example serves the instruction of all, it reminds in particular the ministers of the Word of their office, to whom a zeal for the truth ought to be so entrusted that they bring forward nothing that could in any way detract from it, even if it is joined with their own praise and glory. For (as we have warned above) Satan is wont to approach with flattery those whom he knows to be otherwise unwilling. This is why Christ forbade evil spirits to speak and would not have his cause commended by their testimony. Therefore those greatly err who play with such people, whom it is plain are very far removed from the truth. They sometimes conceal their poison, but they harm all the more grievously the more they flatter. It is the mark of a Christian man to have no friend whom he knows to be an enemy of Christ and impatient of Christian teaching. But especially worth noting is that Paul sets Jesus Christ against the devil, and that the devil is compelled to give way as soon as he hears the name of Christ pronounced. This is an unanswerable argument for the power of Christ. For no one can enter the house of a powerful man and plunder his goods unless he has first bound and overcome him. But Christ Jesus, coming into the world, so overcame the prince of this world, the devil, that at the mere hearing of the name of Christ he was compelled to leave his possession and give place to Christ in men. We must therefore confess that the power of Christ is far greater than that of the devil. And from this we ought to seek consolation in temptations, that we need not fear him against whom Christ, into whom we have been grafted by faith, has no power at all. Again, we are reminded here that Christ has absolutely nothing in common with the devil, since he does not deign to accept from him even a testimony, however honourable. For what fellowship could there be between them, since according to the first promise Christ came into the world so that he might crush the head of the devil and destroy his works? Gen. 3. 1 John 3. This same thing also admonishes Christians of their duty, that they should have nothing in common with the devil. For it is not fitting that those who have once given their name to Christ should play with the devil in any matter. Let them therefore flee the prophetic arts that the cunning of Satan and the wicked curiosity of men have devised. Let them flee the trickery of incantations, by which he promises help in diseases or other afflictions. Let them flee false and profane worship, superstition, idolatry, and whatever draws them away from God. Let them hold the tyranny of sin in abhorrence, which overthrows the liberty won for us by Christ. Finally, let them be watchful and steadfast in faith and resist the devil, and he will withdraw from them; whence it will come about that, once his dominion has been shaken off, they may lead a life approved by God and one day reign with Jesus Christ, our Lord and Saviour, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CX.
units.tr: HOMILY CX.

units.la: Videntes autem Domini eius, quòd abiisset spes quaestus sui, apprehensum Paulum & Silam traxerunt in forum ad principes, & offerentes eos magistratibus, dixerunt: Isti homines conturbant ciuitatem nostram, cum sint Iudaei: & annunciant institute, quae non licet nobis suscipere, neq; seruare, cum simus Romani. Et concurrit turba aduersus eos: & magistratus scissis vestibus eorum, iusserunt virgis caedi. Cumq; multas plagas eis imposuissent, coniecerunt eos in carcerem, praecipientes custodi carceris, ut diligenter custodiret eos. Qui cum tale praeceptum accepisset, coniecit eos in carcerem interiorem, & pedes eorum strinxit ligno.
units.tr: When her masters saw that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the forum before the rulers. Presenting them to the magistrates, they said: "These men are throwing our city into confusion. They are Jews, and they announce customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or observe, since we are Romans." The crowd rose up against them, and the magistrates tore off their garments and ordered them to be beaten with rods. After laying many blows on them, they threw them into prison and commanded the jailer to guard them carefully. Receiving such an order, he put them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.

units.la: Quemadmodum Dei filio Iesu Christo, in terris agenti & euangelium praedicanti, diabolus partim blanditijs & dolis, partim verò aperta vi se oppositurita ijs de armis aduersus apostolos solos Christi idem illi pugnauit olim, & hodie etiam pugnat. Est id in præsenti historia videre. Nam Paulo apud Philippenses prædicanti puellam Pythonis spiritu asflatam obijcit, per quam illi præclarum defert veritatis testimonium, vt hac ratione euangelij doctrinam cordatis quibusuis suspe-stam reddat, & sibi apud Christianæ fidei professores locum aliquem reliquum faciat. Sed facilè animaduertit dolum Paulus apostolus, & Christi nomine adiuratum spiritum è puella discedere co-git, simul suo exemplo docens nec ipsi Christo nec Christi cultoribus quicquam cum diabolo commu-ne esse debere, cum ideo in mundum hunc Christus venerit, vt diaboli opera dissoluat. At non propte-rea stationem suam diabolus deserit: quin potius vbi se blanditijs nihil efficere videt, in furorem con-uersus, per puellas dominos apertas cum Paulo inimicitias exercet, eos{que} rem deducit, vt primò qui-dem virgus casi apostoli in publicos carceres abripiantur, mox autem vrbe eijciantur. Est{que} singulari consyderatione dignus locus hic, vt qui communis hostis nostri dolos & conatus omnes, ceu in specu-lo inspiciendos, nobis proponit.
units.tr: Just as the devil, the enemy of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, while he lived on earth and preached the gospel, opposed him partly with flatteries and deceits and partly with open violence, so he has fought against the apostles with the same weapons, and he still fights today. This can be seen in the present story. For when Paul was preaching at Philippi, he set before him a slave girl possessed by a Python spirit, through whom the devil bore a remarkable testimony to the truth, so that by this means he might make the teaching of the gospel suspect to any thoughtful people and secure for himself some place among the professors of the Christian faith. But the apostle Paul easily detected the trick, and commanded the spirit, adjured in the name of Christ, to depart from the girl. At the same time he taught by his example that neither Christ himself nor the worshippers of Christ should have anything in common with the devil, since Christ came into this world for the very purpose of destroying the works of the devil. Yet the devil does not therefore abandon his post. Rather, when he sees that he accomplishes nothing by flattery, he turns to rage, and through the girl's masters he carries on enmity against Paul, and brings the matter to the point where first the apostles are dragged to the public prison, stripped of their clothes and beaten with rods, and soon afterwards are cast out of the city. This place deserves special consideration, since it sets before us, as in a mirror, all the tricks and attempts of our common enemy, which we ought to examine.

units.la: Ante omnia vero cansam indicat Lucas, quæ puella huius dominos aduersus apostolos extimu-lauit. Viderunt (inquit) eiecto Pythonis spiritu, spem quæstus sui intercidisse. Auaritia ergo præ-cipua huius mali causa fuit, quæ non oculos modo perstrinxit, vt veritatem videre non possent, ve- rumetiam illos ita exacerbauit, vt illam hostiliter persequerentur. Est{que} hoc memorabile exemplū, quo docemur quàm magna quamq{ue} noxia auaritiæ pestis sit. Paulus illam omnium malorum radi-cem vocat. 1. Tim. 6. Et auaro nihil sceleratius esse, alibi scriptura docet. Ecclesiastici 10. Extant præterea passim exempla, quæ per auaritiam iura corrumpi, bonos mores vitiari, virginum & ma-tronarum pudicitiam expugnari, amicitias dissolui, deniq{ue} respub. florentissimas euerti probant. At nuspiam euidentius, quàm in religionis causa, huius mali vis cernitur. Auaritia enim animum bo-minū à Deo reuocans, idololatras reddit eos, qui in vno Deo spem & fiduciam omnem repositam ba-bere debebant. Nam vbi thesaurus noster est, ibi quoq{ue} est cor nostrum. Matth. 6. Auari verò thesau-rus in opibus & pecuniarum aceruis est. Iisdem ergo animum quoq{ue} auari addictū esse oportet. Vnde constat religionem omnino nullam esse posse, vbicunq{ue} auaritia imperium obtinet. Quæ causa est, quòd hanc Paulus idololatriam nominare non dubitauit. Coloss. 3. Ephef. 5. Quòd si verò religionis nomen auari iactant, illam quoq{ue} sibi quæstum faciunt, eoq{ue} turpius peccant, quo sanctiori cupiditatis suæ pretextu utuntur. Ita Iudæorum sacerdotum auaritia factum est, vt templum domini emporiū sieret, & sub longæ precationis prætextu domus viduarum & pupillorum devorarentur. Et aposto-lus nouissimorum temporum sectatoribus hoc maximè tribuit, quòd abnegato domino, qui ipsos rede-mit, ex illius membris quæstum captaturi sint. 2. Pet. 2. Quod oraculū, si ad nostri seculi mores trans-feras, Petrum rem acu tetigisse fateberis, quando iam seculis aliquot in Papatu omnia sacra vena-lia fuerunt. Imò huic vni causæ tot hominum traditiones, tot monachorum ordines, tot ceremoniarū Chaos, exequias, & quæcunq{ue} alia huius generis sunt, debemus. Sed accedit omnibus istis longè gra-uissimum, quòd eadem auaritia Veritatis impatientes, adeoq{ue} hostes Veritatis homines reddit. Nam vt multa alia ferre possint auari, quæstum tamen suum minui ferre non possunt, imò toti furunt, vt primùm huius materiam subtraxerint. Inde ergo impiæ aduersus veritatem consultationes, prodditio-nes, turbæ & omnis generis persecutiones exoriri solent. Exempla quibus hoc probetur, passim sune obuia. Auaritia excæcatus Caiaphas, Christum occidendum esse decernit. Iohan. 11. Eundem auaritia extimulatus Iudas prodidit. Iohan. 12. Et Pythonicæ puellæ domini non aliam ob causam apostolos sublatos volunt, quàm quòd horum doctrina quæstui ipsorum officeret. Possunt ferre ad Christum conuersam esse Lydiam, in huius domo diuersari apostolos, eosdē ad flumen congregatis cœtibus præ-dicare, & nouos quotidie Christo discipulos adducere. Sed quæstum suum euerti, ferre non possunt. Si-mile quid paulò post in Demetrio apud Ephesios videbimus. At quid veteribus exemplis commemo-randum immoramur, quando nostro seculo sola auaritia veritatis cursum maximè impedit? Quæstus cupiditate excæcati antistites, reformationem omnem fugiūt. Eadem principes Antichristo deuincie & nobiles viros, cum ecclesiasticis opibus multos generis sui nobilitatem & splendorem tueri posse videant, qui alioqui ad ignobile vulgus & mechanicas artes relegandi essent. Hæc ipsa causa mer-catores, publicanos, milites, deniq{ue} omnis loci & ordinis homines euangelio iniquos reddit, eò quòd hoc admisso ditescendi studium, quo hodie pleriq{ue} occupantur, subsistere non posse videnti. Quid verò de euangelicis dicemus? Nonne etiam isti ad hunc scopulum maxime impingunt, dum sub euangelij prætextu opes & honores vanantur? Qua spes si ipsos fallat, manifesti veritatis hostes fiunt, eodem nimirum animo prediti, cuius exemplum supra in Simone Mago vidimus. Fugiamus ergo immanissimam pestem, & nostra forte contenti, nihil antiquius ducamus euangelica veritatis cognitione, quae sola æterna salutis confortes reddere possÉ.
units.tr: First of all, Luke indicates the cause that stirred up the girl's masters against the apostles. They saw, he says, that with the Python spirit driven out, the hope of their gain had perished. Greed, then, was the chief cause of this evil. It not only dazzled their eyes so that they could not see the truth, but also so inflamed them that they hostilely pursued it. This is a memorable example, by which we are taught how great and how harmful a plague of greed is. Paul calls it the root of all evils (1 Tim. 6). And Scripture elsewhere teaches that nothing is more wicked than a covetous man (Ecclesiasticus 10). Moreover, there are everywhere examples which prove that by greed laws are corrupted, good morals are spoiled, the chastity of virgins and matrons is violated, friendships are dissolved, and finally the most flourishing commonwealths are overthrown. But nowhere is the force of this evil seen more clearly than in matters of religion. For greed draws the minds of men away from God and makes idolaters of those who ought to have placed all their hope and trust in the one God. For where your treasure is, there your heart is also (Matt. 6). But the treasure of the covetous lies in riches and heaps of money, so the mind of the covetous must also be devoted to these things. Hence it is evident that there can be no religion at all wherever greed holds sway. This is why Paul did not hesitate to call it idolatry (Col. 3; Eph. 5). But if greedy men boast of the name of religion, they make even that a source of profit, and they sin all the more shamefully the more holy the pretext of their desire they use. Thus, through the greed of the Jewish priests, the temple of the Lord became a marketplace, and under the pretext of long prayers the houses of widows and orphans were devoured. And the apostle assigns this above all to the followers of the last times, that, having denied the Lord who redeemed them, they will seek profit from his members (2 Pet. 2). If you apply this oracle to the manners of our own age, you will confess that Peter hit the mark exactly, since for several centuries under the Papacy all sacred things have been for sale. Indeed, to this one cause we owe so many human traditions, so many orders of monks, such a chaos of ceremonies, funeral rites, and whatever else is of this kind. But, far more serious than all these things, the same greed makes men impatient of the truth and therefore enemies of the truth. For although the greedy can bear many other things, they cannot bear to see their gain diminished; rather, they rage utterly to remove the very material of it. From this arise impious plots against the truth, betrayals, disturbances, and every kind of persecution. Examples proving this lie everywhere in view. Caiaphas, blinded by greed, decreed that Christ must be put to death (John 11). Judas, spurred on by greed, betrayed him (John 12). And the masters of the Python girl wanted the apostles removed for no other reason than that their teaching was harmful to their profit. They could bear that Lydia had been converted to Christ, that the apostles lodged in her house, that they preached to assemblies gathered by the river, and that they brought new disciples to Christ every day. But they cannot bear that their gain is overthrown. A similar thing we will see a little later in Demetrius at Ephesus. But why do we linger on ancient examples, when in our own age greed alone chiefly hinders the course of the truth? Prelates blinded by the desire for gain flee from every reformation. Princes bind themselves to the Antichrist, and noblemen, seeing that with church resources they can maintain the nobility and splendour of their families, who otherwise would be relegated to the common crowd and the mechanical arts. This same cause makes merchants, tax collectors, soldiers, and finally men of every place and rank hostile to the gospel, because they see that if the gospel is admitted, the eagerness to get rich, by which most people are now occupied, cannot stand. And what shall we say of those who profess the gospel? Do not even they strike hard against this rock, while under the pretext of the gospel they pursue riches and honours? If their hope deceives them, they become open enemies of the truth, endowed without doubt with the same mind whose example we saw above in Simon Magus. Let us therefore flee this most savage plague, and, content with what we have, let us regard nothing as more important than knowledge of the gospel truth, which alone can make us partakers of eternal salvation.

units.la: Cæterum ad Pythonissæ dominos reuersi, quid aduersus apostolos egerint, videamus. Primo Paulum & Silam, quasi totius negotij duces, comprehendunt: comprehensos in forum trahunt ad ciuitatis proceres: inde eos τοῖς στρατηγοῖς, id est, militum præfectis (qui à Romanis præsidij loco impositi fuisse videntur) offerunt. Accusationem vero instituunt amarulentam simul & artificiosam. Isti homines (inquiunt) conturbant ciuitatem nostram, cum sint Iudæi: & annunciant instityтa, quæ non licet nobis suscipere neque seruare, cum simus Romani. Duo igitur atrocissima crimina obijciunt, seditiosam ciuitatis conturbationem, & seducendi populi studium. Posterius autem per Romanas leges amplificant, quibus noui cultus prohibebantur, nec cuiquam Deum aliquem novum colere licebat, priusquam illum Senatus pro Deo habere censuisset, quod ipsum vetustissimum ecclesiæ scriptor Tertullianus adnotauit. Adhæc vtrunque crimen personarum circunstantijs exaggerant. Se enim Romanos esse gloriantur, & proinde dignos qui defendantur, vt ipsis tutò secundum leges Romanas viuere liceat: apostolos autem odiose Iudæos nominant, eò quòd Iudæorum nomen omnibus exosum & inuisum esset, adeò vt Claudio regnante omnes Roma & Italia decedere coacti fuerint. Et sanè indignum videri poterat, homines Iudæos, tantum non publica infamia notatos, Romanis ciuibus, qui tamen orbis totius domini habebantur, iura legesque præscribere: tantæque authoritatis fuit ista accusatio, vt totus populus aduersus apostolos, tanquam ad commune incendium restinguendum, concurreret. Obseruabis autem hoc loco, quæ hostium veritatis artes sint. Priuati commodi & quæstus cupiditate hos inflammatos fuisse audiuimus. At quiatur-pe fuisset, propter paucos totam ciuitatem conturbari, miro artificio ex priuata causa publicam fa-ciunt, perinde agentes, ac si publicæ salutis studio causam hanc agendam suscepserint. Ita Caiaphas rhetoricari audimus, quando contra Christum consultantibus scribis, ait: Expedit nobis, vt unus homo moriatur pro populo, & non tota gens pereat. Et hodie nihil tam vulgare est, quàm quòd publicæ salutis studium priuatis suis affectibus prætexunt, qui veritatis doctrinam explosam vellent. Habent autem artificium hoc à capite suo, diabolo, quem à primo rerum exordio hoc ipso callidissimè vsum fuisse legimus. Nonne enim primos parentes ad transgressionem sollicitaturus, ita causam suam proponit, vt nihil sibi ipsi quærere, sed pro horum salute solicitus videri possit? Idem cum Christo disputationem instituens, videri vult hoc quærere, vt Christus miraculose suam diuinitatem munido patefaciat, nec diutius suspensam teneat totius mundi expectationem. Huc enim faciunt, quæ de lapidibus in panes conuertendis, & de præcipitio è pinna templi suggerit. Occurrunt passim huius generis exempla, quorum hic præcipuus vsus est, ne subdolus tum ipsius diaboli tum membrorum ipsius artibus nos circumueniri & falli patiamur. Admonet præterea locus hic, quorum criminum ferè in mundo Veritas accusari soleat. Nimirum quòd respub. turbet, & nouis falsisque religionibus imperitum & rudem vulgus seducat. Hinc est quòd huius doctores fiue ministri pro seditionis & seductoribus vel impostoribus habentur. Audiunt hoc à Pharaone tyranno fidelissimi Dei serui, Moses & Aaron. His enim populi libertatem flagitantibus ille respondet: Tu Moses & Aaron, cur abstrahitis populum ab operibus suis? Hoc ipsum multo amarulentius Eliæ prophetæ impius Achab objicit, dicens: Annon tu es ille, qui conturbas Israelem? Gravius adhuc est, quòd Amos propheta apud Ieroboamum regem Amasias sacerdos accusat his verbis: Amos coniurationem fecit contra te in medio domus Israelis, nec poterit terra sermones eius omnes ferre. Quid quòd Ieremiam proditionis & defectionis ad hostes Assyrios impij Sedechiæ regis aulici accusant? & eundem vnicum publicarum calamitatum & ipsius excidij authorem esse clamant? Atqui mira hæc non sunt, quando hæcipsa accusationis contra Christum instituta capita fuerunt. Pilato enim dicut sacerdotes: Hunc deprehendimus euertentem gentem, ac vetantem tributa dare Cæsari, dicentem se Christum regem esse. Item: Si hunc absolueris, non es amicus Cæsaris: Quicunque se regem facit, contradicit Cæsari. Grauia sunt hæc, & enormem mundi improbitatem & impudentiam arguunt. Tolerabilia tamen videri possunt, si cum ijs, quæ nostro seculo fiunt conferantur. Dixerunt hæc olim, qui ex professo prophetarum & apostolorum hostes erant, quiá Christum salvatorem ignorabant. At hodie, qui Christiani esse & haberi volunt, qui ecclesiæ Christi supremam administrationem sibi vendicant, qui denique se ecclesiæ nutritios, pastores & tutores esse profitentur, Christi & evangelij ministros persequi solent, & eam doctrinam novam, seditiosam & seductoriá esse dicunt, quæ iuxta veteris, & novi Testamenti scripturas in uno Iesu Christo omnem salutis rationem monstrat, quæ sacramentorum legitimum usum docet, quæ innocentiá & vitæ puritatem tradit, quæ charitatis officia instituit, quæ inimicos diligere iubet, quæ magistratibus sua iura suasque leges liberas permittit, quæ Cæsari quæ Cæsaris sunt, & Deo quæ Dei sunt exolvere iubet, quæ publicæ pacis studium unicè commendat, & quantum in nobis est, nos cum omnibus hominibus pacè tueri præcipit. Quis igitur nō exclamet, O mores, o tempora? Agnoscamus ergo mundi cæcitatem, nec unius æstus æstimemus calumnias, quibus salutarem evangelij doctrinam suspectam reddere & infamare studet.
units.tr: Let us now return to the masters of the soothsaying girl and see what they did against the apostles. First they seize Paul and Silas, as the leaders of the whole business: once seized, they drag them into the forum before the chief men of the city, and from there hand them over to the τοῖς στρατηγοῖς [tois stratēgois], that is, to the prefects of the soldiers (who seem to have been placed there by the Romans as a garrison). Their accusation is both bitter and crafty. "These men," they say, "are throwing our city into confusion, though they are Jews; and they announce customs which it is not lawful for us to adopt or observe, since we are Romans." So they bring two most atrocious charges: the seditious disturbance of the city, and the aim of seducing the people. They then magnify the second charge by appeal to Roman law, under which new forms of worship were forbidden, and no one was allowed to worship any new god until the Senate had judged him to be a god; the most ancient writer of the Church, Tertullian, has noted this very point. In addition they inflate each charge by the circumstances of the persons. They boast that they are Romans, and therefore deserve to be defended, so that they may live safely under Roman law; but they name the apostles spitefully as Jews, because the name of Jews was hateful and odious to everyone, so much so that under the emperor Claudius all Jews were compelled to leave Rome and Italy. And indeed it might well seem unworthy that Jews, marked with almost public infamy, should prescribe laws and rights to Roman citizens, who were regarded as lords of the whole world; and this accusation carried such authority that the whole people ran against the apostles, as if to put out a common fire. Here you should observe what the arts of the enemies of truth are. We have heard that these men were inflamed by desire for private gain. But because it would have been shameful to throw the whole city into confusion for the sake of a few, they cleverly turn a private cause into a public one, acting as if they had taken up this cause out of concern for the public safety. So we hear Caiaphas speaking rhetorically when the scribes were consulting against Christ: "It is expedient for us that one man die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish." And today nothing is so common as for men who wish the doctrine of truth driven out to pretend a concern for public safety while pursuing their own private passions. They have this trick from their head, the devil, whom we read to have used it most cunningly from the very beginning of things. For when he was about to entice our first parents to transgression, did he not so set forth his cause that he could seem to seek nothing for himself but to be anxious for their welfare? Likewise, when he disputed with Christ, he wished to seem to seek only that Christ should miraculously reveal his divinity by a sign and not keep the expectation of the whole world in suspense any longer. To this belong the suggestions about turning stones into bread and about throwing himself down from the pinnacle of the temple. Examples of this kind occur everywhere, and the chief use of this place is that we should not allow ourselves to be circumvented and deceived by the crafty arts of the devil himself and of his members. This passage also reminds us of the charges with which truth is commonly accused in the world: namely, that it disturbs the commonwealth and leads the unlearned and ignorant crowd astray with new and false religions. Hence it is that the teachers, or ministers, of this truth are regarded as seditious, as seducers or as impostors. The most faithful servants of God, Moses and Aaron, heard this from the tyrant Pharaoh. For when they demanded the liberty of the people, he answered: "Moses and Aaron, why do you draw the people away from their works?" The impious Ahab objected the same thing to the prophet Elijah, far more bitterly, saying: "Is it you who troubles Israel?" Still more serious is the accusation which the priest Amaziah brought against the prophet Amos before King Jeroboam, in these words: "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel, and the land will not be able to bear all his words." What of the courtiers of the impious King Zedekiah, who accused Jeremiah of treason and of defection to the Assyrian enemies, and cried out that he alone was the author of the public calamities and of the ruin itself? Yet these things are not strange, since these very heads of accusation were drawn up against Christ. For the priests say to Pilate: "We found this man subverting the nation and forbidding tribute to be given to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ the king." Likewise: "If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend; whoever makes himself king speaks against Caesar." These things are grave, and they prove the monstrous wickedness and shamelessness of the world. They may seem tolerable, however, if they are compared with what happens in our own age. Those who once said these things were openly enemies of the prophets and apostles, because they did not know Christ the Saviour. But today those who wish to be and to be called Christians, who claim for themselves the supreme administration of the Church of Christ, who finally profess themselves the nurturers, pastors and guardians of the Church, are accustomed to persecute the ministers of Christ and of the gospel, and they say that doctrine new, seditious and seductive which, according to the Scriptures of the Old and New Testament, shows every way of salvation in the one Jesus Christ; which teaches the lawful use of the sacraments; which delivers innocence and purity of life; which establishes the duties of charity; which bids us love our enemies; which allows magistrates their own rights and their own free laws; which bids us render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the things that are God's; which uniquely commends the pursuit of public peace, and, so far as in us lies, commands us to keep peace with all men. Who then would not exclaim: "O manners! O times!"? Let us therefore acknowledge the blindness of the world, and let us not be surprised by the slander with which it strives to render the wholesome doctrine of the gospel suspect and infamous.

units.la: Restat, ut Philippensis magistratus iudicium de præsenti causa consyderemus. Quid vero iudicium dico, cum absque omni iudicio, immani furore in apostolos debacchati sint? Mox enim ipsi illorum vestes dilacerant, quasi scelerum ministri desint. Deinde insontes, indicta causa, virgis cædere iubent. Et postquam multis plagis misere mulctati sunt, demum in carcerem coniiciunt, simulque mandant, ut singulari cura custodiantur, quasi pro aliis facinorosis maiori supplicio digni sint. Quæ causa fuit, ut in interiorem carcerem coniectis pedes cippo astringerentur. Quid vero indignius, quid iniquius abijs, qui magistratu funguntur, fieri poterat? Peccat, qui reo sese excusandi copiam denegat. At ipsi insuper virgis cædunt homines peregrinos, & casos demum custodiæ tradunt, ut ipsorum causam postea cognoscant. Furoris huius causa fuit, quòd calumniis sibi bile commoveri passi sunt.
