From this we may conjecture that there was also disputation among them, and that Paul answered their arguments. For it is not likely that those who were still wholly ignorant of Christ could have listened to Paul with such patience as not to interrupt him at some point with their objections. Meanwhile the ardent zeal both of Paul and of his hearers is expressed, of which we had a similar example above in chapter twenty. Here the sloth of our own age is rebuked, from which some ministers of the Word and hearers are also accustomed to suffer, who think that all the effort spent on holy sermons is excessive. But that famine of the Word will one day arise, of which we read in the prophet, etc. (Amos 8).

units.la: Quinto concionis tam seriae tamen, diligentius effectus describitur. Alij enim credunt, alij minus. Imo grauis inter illos disceptatio exoritur. Videmus hic, quàm nam in mundo hoc euangelij fors sit. Quia enim Christus in signum positus est, cui contradicitur, fieri nequit, vt vnanimi consensu euangelium ipsius homines recipiant. Neminem ergo credentium paucitas & disceptationum verberima leges bodie offendant, quando olim paucissimos credidisse audimus, cùm ipse Dei filius, & apostoli illius praedicarent. Hoc ipsum ministros quoq; consoletur, quando se praedicando parum aut nihil proficere vident. Tunc enim illud Christi in animum reuocent: Si sermonem meum seruauerint, & verum seruabunt; &c. Iohan. 15.
units.tr: Fifth, the effect of such a serious sermon is described, though rather more carefully. For some believe, others less so. Indeed a serious dispute arises among them. We see here what the lot of the gospel is in this world. For since Christ has been set as a sign which is spoken against, it cannot happen that men receive his gospel with unanimous consent. Therefore let neither the small number of believers nor the most violent disputes trouble anyone today, since we hear that very few believed long ago, when the Son of God himself and his apostles were preaching. This same fact should also console the ministers, when they see that they make little or no progress in preaching. For then let them recall to mind that saying of Christ: If they have kept my word, they will keep yours also, etc. (John 15).

units.la: Caterum Paulus illorum contumaciam feueriter admodum arguit, & horrendum Dei iudicium illis denunciat. Ita enim cum illis agendum esse, apud quos blanda & salutari euangelij praedicatione nihil proficitur, Christus suo exemplo docet, qui non raro atroces minas & horrendum illud Vae pharisaeorum & scribarum auribus intonat. Paulus autem, ne quid carnis affectui dare videatur, propheticum oraculum ex Isa. 6. cap. allegat, vt ostendat non nouam esse contumaciam illam, qua euangelio relu&antur. Tales olim quoque ipsorum patres fuisse, & tales ipsos fore reuelato Christi regno Deum olim praedixisse. Ita vero infirmis in fine medetur, quos contradicentium multitudo & authoritas offendere poterat. Et simul hos quoque perterrefacit, quando poenam illis iam olim à Deo constitutam esse docet. Est autem memorabilis omnino hic Isaiae locus, quo non alius frequentius in novo Testamento citatur. Meminerunt enim huius euangelistae omnes, nimirum Matthaeus 13. Marc. 4. Luc. 8. & Iohan. 12. cap. Et Paulus eundem ad Romanos cap. 10. repetit. Quare non superuacaneâ nobis videri debet illius consyderatio. Tria enim completitur, ad nos quoq; non parum pertinentia:
units.tr: Moreover, Paul rebukes their obstinacy very severely and announces to them God's dreadful judgment. Christ teaches by his own example that this is how one must deal with those among whom nothing is gained by the gentle and healthful preaching of the gospel. He often thunders dire threats and that dreadful "Woe" against the ears of the Pharisees and scribes. Paul, however, so that he may not seem to yield to fleshly feeling, quotes a prophetic oracle from Isaiah chapter 6, to show that the obstinacy by which they resist the gospel is not something new. Their own fathers were like this of old, and God had foretold long ago that they would be like this too when the kingdom of Christ was revealed. In this way he heals the weak at the end, those whom the multitude and authority of the opponents could offend. At the same time he also terrifies these people, when he teaches that the punishment has already been appointed for them by God long ago. This passage of Isaiah is altogether memorable, and no other is cited more often in the New Testament. All the evangelists recall it, namely Matthew 13, Mark 4, Luke 8, and John chapter 12. And Paul repeats the same passage in Romans chapter 10. Therefore its consideration ought not to seem superfluous to us. For three things are contained in it, which pertain no little to us as well:

units.la: Primò Iudaeorum peccatum describitur, quòd nimirum scientes & volentes caecutiant, & agnitam veritatis lucem auernentur: ijs similes, qui cum oculis & auribus integris vtantur, se tamen caecos & surdos esse simulant. Et tales quidem illos fuisse, euangelica historia non vno in loco docet. Vtinam verò soli illi tales olim fuissent, & non bodie etiam passim horum similes inuenirentur; qui cum conscientiae testimonio conuincantur, adhuc tamen se fidei mysterium capere non posse simulant. Interim verbi Dei perspicuitas, hic eluceat, quae tanta est, vt illa hominum oculos & aures potenter feriat. Nec enim obscurum esse potest Verbum, quod nobis lucernae instar Deus proponit. Psalmo 119. Obscuritas ergo omnis ex hominibus, adeoque crassa & voluntaria est, vt sequentia docent.
units.tr: First, the sin of the Jews is described: that they knowingly and willingly blind themselves, and turn away from the light of truth they have recognised. They are like those who, though they use their eyes and ears whole, pretend to be blind and deaf. Evangelical history teaches in more than one place that they were indeed such people. Would that only they had been such of old, and that people like them were not found everywhere today as well, who, though they are convicted by the testimony of conscience, still pretend that they cannot grasp the mystery of faith. Meanwhile the clarity of God's Word shines forth here, and it is so great that it strikes powerfully the eyes and ears of men. For the Word, which God sets before us like a lamp, cannot be obscure. Psalm 119. All obscurity therefore comes from men, and is so gross and wilful, as the following words show.

units.la: Secundo enim causam huius mali propheta describit, Cor videlicet incrassatum. Ita vero dicitur animus, quem affectus prauì induraverunt, ita vt nullis vel monitionibus vel adhortationibus flecti possit. Explicatur hoc omne à Christo per nuptiarum & inuitatorum parabolam. In qua alij vxorem duxerunt, alij boues, alij villas emerunt, & isti rebus occupati nuptias adire detrectant.
units.tr: Second, the prophet describes the cause of this evil, namely a heart made gross. A soul is so called when wicked affections have hardened it, so that it cannot be bent by any warnings or exhortations. Christ explains all this by the parable of the wedding and the invited guests. In it, some took wives, others oxen, others bought farms, and these, occupied with their possessions, refuse to come to the wedding.

units.la: Paulus à mane vsq; ad vesperam docet.
units.tr: Paul teaches from morning until evening.

units.la: Concionis Pauline effectus.
units.tr: The effect of Paul's sermon.

units.la: Paulus Iudaeorum contumaciam arguit.
units.tr: Paul rebukes the obstinacy of the Jews.

units.la: Isa. VI.
units.tr: Isaiah 6.

units.la: I. Iudaeorum incredulitas voluntaria.
units.tr: I. The Jews' unbelief is wilful.

units.la: II. Incredulitatis causa.
units.tr: II. The cause of unbelief.

units.la: Intelliguntur autem illi homines, qui carni & terrae addicti, caelestia spontè fastidiunt & negligunt. Quales Iudaeorum proceres fuisse constat, qui maiorem sui honoris & quaestus, quàm Christi & regni coelorum rationem habuerunt. Et hodie vix alia contempti euangelij causa indicari potest, quàm quòd vel opibus congerendis vel carnis voluptatibus ita passim studetur, ut Christo potius carere velint homines, quàm haec sua studia deserere. Ita verò inexcusabiles esse constat omnes eos, qui in sua incredulitate pereunt. Venit enim lux in mundum, sed homines magis dilexerunt tenebras, &c. Ioan.3.cap. Et Paulus tempus fore praedicit, quando veritatis doctrinam homines non ferant, sed cateruatim sibi ipsis doctores falsos coacerent, qui suis affectibus conuenientia loquantur. Id verò iam saeculis aliquot iuxta literam quoque impletum fuisse constat, & hodie ita impletur, ut non paucos inuenire liceat, qui euangelio quidem veram de fide & religione doctrinam tradi confitentur, Papisticam tamen religionem praeferendam esse dicunt, eò quòd & carni magis arrideat, & mundo acceptior sit. Ut interim de illis nihil dicamus, qui publicè, & magnis quidem clamoribus, se meliora & saniora docentes nec audire nec ferre velle, testantur.
units.tr: Those men are meant who, given over to the flesh and the earth, willingly scorn and neglect heavenly things. It is clear that the leaders of the Jews were such, who valued the regard for their own honour and gain more than the cause of Christ and the kingdom of heaven. And today scarcely any other cause of contempt for the gospel can be pointed out, than that people everywhere so eagerly pursue either the piling up of wealth or the pleasures of the flesh that they would rather be without Christ than give up these pursuits. It is clear that all who perish in their unbelief are thus inexcusable. For "the light has come into the world, but men loved darkness rather than light," etc. John 3 chapter. And Paul foretells that a time will come when men will not endure the teaching of the truth, but will heap up for themselves false teachers by the crowd, who will say things agreeable to their affections. This has indeed been fulfilled literally for several centuries, and it is fulfilled today in such a way that one may find not a few who confess that the gospel does indeed teach the true doctrine concerning faith and religion, yet say that the Papist religion is to be preferred, because it both pleases the flesh more and is more acceptable to the world. To pass over for now those who publicly, and with great outcries, testify that they will neither hear nor endure those who teach better and saner things.

units.la: Ceterum ijsdem poenam, quam merentur, propheta denuntiat, quae multiplex simul & horribilis est. Primò enim ipsi non conuertuntur, ut fanari possint. Omnis ergo salutis spes ipsis denegatur. Quia enim non alia vsquam inuenitur salutis ratio, quàm ut ad Deum conuersi, cum illo in gratiam redeamus, fieri non potest, quin à salute in vniuersum excidant, quotquot Dei verbum, quo ad conuersionem hanc salutarem inuitantur, & quo eiusdem vera ratio traditur, maligne fastidiunt. Quare in peccatis suis pereant necesse est, sicuti Christus Iudaeorum sacerdotibus minatur. Ioan.8. Deinde salutare illud Dei ad alios transfertur. Id verò frequenter Iudaeis interminatur Deus, ut illorum duram confidentiam molliret. Quia enim semel à Deo adoptati & illius peculium facti erant, impossibile fore putabant, ut à sua dignitate exciderent: imò Dei regnum collapsurum sibi ipsis persuaserant, si ipsi à Deo repudiarentur. Paulus ergo vaniffimam esse docet hanc illorum fiduciam: eò quòd Deo facile fit, regnum suum omnibus suis partibus integrum, ad gentes transferre. Nec id ex semetipso pronunciat, sed ad Dei oracula respicit, quibus hoc euenturum esse, olim praedictum fuerat. Huc enim pertinent, quae Deuteron.32. leguntur: Ipsi me prouocauerunt ad indignationem in eo, qui non est Deus, ad iracundiam me irritarunt vanitatibus suis: & ego ipsos quoque prouocabo in eo, qui non est populus, in gente stulta irritabo eos, &c. Vide etiam quae in eandem sententiam apud Hosea dicuntur. Sed & Christus diserte ait: Transferetur à vobis regnum Dei, & dabitur genti facienti fructus eius. Matth.21. Id verò qua ratione factum sit, totus libri huius contextus abundè docuit, & Paulus ad Romanos Cap.10. & 11. fusius declarat. At ne quis in hoc gradu Dei iudicium subsistere existimet, insuper obseruandum est, horribile vrbis simul & totius gentis excidium secutum fuisse, sicuti Christus minatus erat, ut primum euangelij doctrina ab illis ad gentes translata fuit. Sunt autem haec diligenti & iugi obseruatione dignissima, ut ex ijs colligamus, quid nobis sperandum sit, si Iudaeos imitati, Deo ingrati simus, & euangelij doctrinae improbè reluctemur. Constat enim sibi ipsi Deus in iudicijs suis, & gentem similia facientem simili iudicio punire consueuit. Ieremiae quinto cap. Nec est, quòd nobis repulsis euangelium & Christi regnum collapsurum putemus, qua perfuasione Iudaeos seductos fuisse, modò diximus. Potest enim Deus ex lapidibus Abrahami filios facere, & non paucae coniecturae sunt, quae iuxta Lactantij sententiam, Imperium in Orientem breui reuersurum, & Occidentem denuò seruiturum portendunt. Quod si fiat, Christi regnum inter Turcas & fortasse Iudaeos quoque magnis incrementis exurgere vi-debimus. De quo Paulus ad Romanos capite vndecimo quaedam non omnino obscurè vaticinari videtur.
units.tr: Moreover, the prophet announces to these same people the punishment they deserve, which is at once manifold and dreadful. For first, they are not converted, so that they might be healed. Therefore all hope of salvation is denied them. For since no other way of salvation is found anywhere than that we, turned to God, return into grace with him, it cannot but be that all who maliciously scorn the Word of God, by which they are invited to this saving conversion and by which the true way to it is taught, fall away from salvation altogether. Therefore they must perish in their sins, just as Christ threatens the priests of the Jews. John 8. Next, that saving grace of God is transferred to others. God often threatened this to the Jews, so as to soften their hard confidence. For since they had once been adopted by God and made his peculiar people, they thought it impossible that they would fall from their dignity; indeed they had persuaded themselves that the kingdom of God would collapse if they themselves were rejected by God. Paul therefore teaches that this confidence of theirs is most vain, because it is easy for God to transfer his kingdom, whole in all its parts, to the nations. Nor does he pronounce this on his own authority, but looks to the oracles of God, by which it had been foretold long ago that this would happen. For to this pertain the words in Deuteronomy 32: "They provoked me to jealousy with what is not God; they angered me with their vanities; and I will provoke them with what is not a people; I will anger them with a foolish nation," etc. See also what is said to the same effect in Hosea. And Christ plainly says: "The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruit." Matthew 21. How this came about the whole context of this book has amply taught, and Paul in Romans chapters 10 and 11 explains it more fully. But lest anyone think that God's judgment stopped at this stage, it must further be observed that a horrible destruction of the city and of the whole nation followed, just as Christ had threatened, once the teaching of the gospel was transferred from them to the nations. These things are most worthy of diligent and constant observation, so that from them we may gather what we ourselves ought to expect, if we imitate the Jews, are ungrateful to God, and wickedly resist the doctrine of the gospel. For God is consistent in his judgments, and he is accustomed to punish a nation doing similar things with a similar judgment. Jeremiah chapter 5. Nor is there cause for us to think that, if we are rejected, the gospel and the kingdom of Christ will collapse, which persuasion, as we just said, led the Jews astray. For God can raise up sons of Abraham from stones, and there are not a few conjectures which, according to the opinion of Lactantius, portend that the empire will soon return to the East, and the West will serve again. If this happens, we shall see the kingdom of Christ rise with great increase among the Turks and perhaps among the Jews as well. Concerning this, Paul in Romans chapter eleven seems to prophesy certain things not altogether obscurely.

units.la: Sed ad Pauli auditores redeamus, quos Lucas exiuisse scribit magna inter illos orta contentione, dum alij veritatis doctrinae reluctari pergunt, alij verò eidem patrocinari student. Et hic quidem illud Christi impletur, qui se gladium & separationem immittere dicit, qua fiat, ut qui antea coniunctissimi erant, acerrimis contentionibus inter se committantur. Nemo tamen hoc euangelij culpa fieri existimet: quando hunc illius finem esse constat, ut omnes nos in Christo vniat & coniungat. Impiorum ergo siue reproborum improbitate omne illud contingit. Quorum proprium est, ut quò propius & fortius Dei verbo vrgentur, eò magis insaniant, sicuti Caini, Pharaonis, Achabi, Zedechia & aliorum exempla testantur. At quia ijsdem pij cedere non possunt, qui Dei gloriam sibi contra quosuis defendendam esse nouerunt, inde contentionum ignis in immensum exardescit. Sed quoad præsentem locum, facile patet non omnino nihil apud illos profecisse Paulum, quando non defuerunt, qui sese palàm impijs opponerent. Nec enim vnquam frustra aut in cassum prædicatur Dei verbum, cum illud per se frugiferum sit, & vbiq; locorum suos Christus habeat, qui vocem ipsius agnoscunt & sequuntur. Interim officij nostri admonemur, vt qui pij & fideles censeri volumus, veritatis causam constanter aduersus quosuis defendamus. Ardentes enim & zelo flagrantes cultores Dei requirit, non tepidos & ignauos, qui quamuis ad impietatē conniuere, & quæuis impiorum scommata patientibus animis & auribus ferre possint. Quales hodie multos passim inuenire licet, qui etiam hoc nomine sibijpsis primam sapientiæ & modestiæ laudem vendicant. Sed reuera stupidi sunt & omni pietatis sensu vacui, qui blasphemijs non exacerbantur: stulti item, qui mundi amicitiam, tanti faciunt, vt Christo pietatis officium denegent. Quin ergo ad salutarem illam pugnam & disceptationem nos præparamus, quæ pijs omnibus in hoc mundo sustinenda est. Nec est, quòd mundi potentia terreamur, quando ei nos militare scimus, qui contradicentes aliquando ferreo sceptro comminuet: qui est Dei filius, dominus & saluator noster, Iesus Christus, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: But let us return to Paul's hearers, from whom Luke writes that he departed, a great contention having arisen among them, while some continued to resist the doctrine of the truth, and others strove to defend it. And here that saying of Christ is fulfilled, who says that he brings a sword and division, so that those who were most closely joined before are set against one another in the bitterest disputes. Yet let no one think that this comes from the fault of the gospel, since it is plain that its end is to unite and join us all in Christ. All this therefore happens through the wickedness of the impious or reprobate. It is characteristic of them that the closer and more forcibly they are pressed by the Word of God, the more they rage, as the examples of Cain, Pharaoh, Ahab, Zedekiah and others bear witness. But because the godly cannot give way to those who know that the glory of God must be defended against anyone whatever, the fire of contention blazes up without measure. Yet as far as the present place is concerned, it is easy to see that Paul did not achieve nothing among them, since there were those who openly set themselves against the impious. For the Word of God is never preached in vain or to no purpose, since it is fruitful in itself, and Christ has his own in every place, who recognise his voice and follow it. Meanwhile we are reminded of our duty: that we who wish to be counted godly and faithful should constantly defend the cause of the truth against anyone whatever. For he seeks fervent worshippers of God, burning with zeal, not lukewarm and lazy ones, who, though they may connive at impiety, and bear with patient minds and ears whatever scoffs of the impious they hear. Many such people may be found everywhere today, who even on this account claim for themselves the highest praise of wisdom and moderation. But in truth they are stupid and empty of all sense of piety, who are not stirred to anger by blasphemies; foolish too are those who value the friendship of the world so highly that they deny Christ the duty of piety. Why not, then, prepare ourselves for that saving struggle and contest, which all the godly must endure in this world? Nor should we be terrified by the power of the world, since we know that we serve him who will one day crush those who oppose him with an iron sceptre: he who is the Son of God, our Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXXV.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXXV.

units.la: Mansit autem Paulus biennio toto in suo conducto, & suscipiebat omnes qui ingrediebantur ad ipsum, prædicans regnum dei, ac docens quæ sunt de domino Iesu cum omni fiducia, nemine prohibente.
units.tr: Paul remained for two whole years in his own rented house, and welcomed all who came to him, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus with all confidence, no one forbidding him.

units.la: Dominus & saluator noster Iesus Christus frequenter discipulos suos hoc argumento consolatur, quòd illos nequaquam relinquere velit orphanos, sed illis præsens adesse vsq; ad consummationem seculi. Quarum promissionum veritas tum vbique alias, tum maxime in aduersis elucet. Tum enim ita suis Christus adest, vt illos non modò potenter & fideliter tueatur, verumetiam omnia ea, quæ ipsis tristia & aduersa videri poterant, ad illorum salutem & gloriam suam dirigat. Qua in re nobis multorum testimoniorum instar esse potest Pauli captiuitas. Quæ initiò quidem euangelij cursum omnino impeditura videbatur, sed ita illam moderatur dominus, vt per hanc euangelij doctrina magis propagata quàm impedita fit. Ea enim occasione factum est, vt & Romani Præsides & milites euangelium audirent, tandemq; illius prædicatio Romam, imò ipsum Prætorium & Cæsaris aulam repleret. At quia de his ante dictum est, alia quæ nobis in historia hac consyderanda relinquant, breuiter percurremus.
units.tr: Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ often comforts his disciples with this argument: that he will by no means leave them orphans, but will be present with them until the end of the age. The truth of these promises shines out everywhere, but most of all in adversity. For then Christ is so present to his own that he not only powerfully and faithfully protects them, but also directs all those things which might seem sad and adverse to them toward their salvation and his own glory. In this matter Paul's imprisonment can serve us as the equivalent of many testimonies. At first it seemed likely to hinder the course of the gospel altogether, but the Lord so governed it that through it the teaching of the gospel was spread more widely than it was hindered. For on that occasion it came about that both the Roman governors and the soldiers heard the gospel, and at last its preaching filled Rome, indeed the Praetorium itself and the court of Caesar. But since this has been said before, we will briefly run through the other things which this history leaves for us to consider.

units.la: Primò tempus captiuitatis Pauli exprimit euangelista, & illum toto biennio in suo illo hospitio, quod suis impensis conduxerat, mansisse ait, nimirum milite illo stipatus, cuius antea mentio facta est. Atqui prius quoq; sub Felice totum biennium in vinculis egit. Et verisimile est aliquos menses elapsos fuisse intra Felicis è prouincia discessum & Pauli profectionem, qua Romam peruenit. Adhæc nauigationi quoque & tempori in Melita exacto menses ad minimum quatuor tribuendi erunt. In quintum ergo annum vsque Pauli captiuitas extenditur. In qua hoc vnum commodi habuit, quòd non in carcerem detrusus fuit, sed in libera custodia egit, vt prædicandi occasionem haberet. Hic verò obseruanda est sanctorum sors, quam in hoc mundo sustinent, dum soli fere pro sceleratissimis habentur, quos aut libertate aut vita frui nefas fit. Quàm multos enim interea temporis nefarios & sceleribus infames sub Nerone, tyranno libidinosissimo, impunè grassatos fuisse putabimus? At solus Paulus, ceu publica quædam mundi totius pestis, in vinculis asseruatur. Eandem fortem olim prophetæ, & post hos Iohannes Baptista, tandemq; ipse Dei filius sustinuerunt, quem cum latronibus ductum & Barraba latrone nocentiorem habitum fuisse constat. Quorum omnium vsus est, ne similibus hodie offendamur. Nec enim par est, vt discipulorum & seruorum sors præstantior & melior sit, quàm præceptoris & domini fuerit. Adhæc cum Christo etiam regnaturos in cœlis sciimus eos, qui in hoc seculo afflictionū ipsius consortes fiunt. Vide 2. Timoth. 2. Simul verò immensa
units.tr: First, the evangelist states the time of Paul's captivity, and says that he remained for the whole two years in that lodging which he had rented at his own expense, guarded no doubt by that soldier mentioned before. Yet previously too he had spent the whole two years under Felix in chains. And it is likely that some months elapsed between Felix's departure from the province and Paul's voyage, by which he reached Rome. Besides, at least four months must be allowed for the sailing and for the time spent on Malta. So Paul's captivity extends into the fifth year. In this one advantage was his, that he was not thrust into a prison but lived in free custody, so that he had an opportunity to preach. Here, however, we should observe the lot the saints bear in this world, since they are almost alone regarded as the most wicked, when it is wrong for them to enjoy either liberty or life. For how many wicked men, infamous for their crimes, shall we suppose went about unpunished meanwhile under Nero, that most lustful tyrant? Yet Paul alone, as though a public plague of the whole world, is kept in chains. The prophets bore the same lot long ago, and after them John the Baptist, and finally the Son of God himself, who is known to have been led off with robbers and judged more guilty than the robber Barabbas. The purpose of all these examples is that we may not be offended by similar things today. For it is not fitting that the lot of the disciples and servants should be better and more excellent than that of their teacher and Lord. Besides, we know that those who become sharers of his afflictions in this age will also reign with Christ in heaven. See 2 Timothy 2. At the same time the immense

units.la: Paulus toto biennio cāptiuitas. Dei bonitas apparet, qui Paulum tanto tempore in libera custodia seruarit, himirum propter electos suos, quibus ea occasione euangelium suu reuelare voluit. Id enim cum aliorum fidelium, tum ipsius Pauli spem longe superauit, quando jub Neronis imperio, libidine & inaudita crudelitate infami, tale quid nemo sperare potuit. Hinc ergo consolatione petant quotquot in Dei vocatione ambulant. Quoad enim Deo vsui erimus, & ita nostrae salutis ratio postulabit, Deus nos inter hostes truculentis simos facile tuebitur, qui & Noah inter diluuij omnia inundantes fluctus, & Ionam in immani Balenae aluo delitescentem seruare potuit. Idem vero, vbi sic tempus postularit, omnibus malis exemptos in aeternum filij sui regnum transferet.
units.tr: Paul's captivity for the whole two years. The goodness of God appears, who kept Paul for so long a time in free custody, namely for the sake of his elect, to whom he wished to reveal his gospel on that occasion. For this went far beyond the hope both of the other faithful and of Paul himself, when under the reign of Nero, infamous for lust and unheard-of cruelty, no one could hope for such a thing. Therefore let all who walk in their calling of God take comfort from this. For as long as we shall be useful to God, and as the reckoning of our salvation requires, God will easily protect us among the most savage enemies, just as he was able to preserve Noah amid the waves flooding over the whole deluge, and Jonah hidden in the vast belly of the whale. Likewise, when the time demands it, he will bring his own, freed from all evils, into the eternal kingdom of his Son.

units.la: Porro quid hoc biennij tempore Paulus fecerit videamus. Suscipiebat (inquit) omnes, qui ingrediebantur ad ipsum, praedicans regnum Dei, ac decens quae sunt de domino Iesu cum omni fiducia, nemine prohibente. Idem ergo in vinculis fecit, quod antea solutus & liber fecerat, eo quod se non minus quam antea Christi Iesu apostolum & seruum esse intelligeret. Nec tamen docuit modo, verum etiam epistolis scriptis & hinc inde missis ecclesias tum instituit tum consolatus est: adeo vt si nostra tempora spectes, plus utilitatis & comodi ad nos ex Pauli vinculis redijsse fatebimur, quam ex eius cum dictis tum factis, quando liberè orbem terrarum peruagatus est. Illis enim debemus praeclaras illas & spiritu dictante scriptas epistolas ad Ephesios, Philippenses, Colossenses, Hebreos, Philemonem & alteram ad Timotheum, quas ceu pretiosissima clenodia in hunc vsq; diem Ecclesia custodiunt. Atqui multa Paulum abstterrere poterat, quo minus vel scriberet vel doceret. Huius enim doctrinae causa in vincula coniectus fuerat. Solus etiam erat, qui in causa hac Romae laborabat. Primo item congressu Iudaeos sui similes id est, contumaces & renitentes expertus erat. Adhaec aliquam animi parum quieti speciem referre videbatur indefessum illud ad exteros scribendi studium. Nec multum a seditionis crimine aberat, in ea fide & religione homines & instituere & confirmare, quam iam antea publico Senatus decreto damnatam fuisse, alibi diximus. Praeterea periculum erat, ne illi tandem libertas hac arctioribus vinculis constrictio & in carcerem aliquem detrusio eriperetur. Nec adeo stupidum fuisse putabimus, vt ista videre & cogitare non potuerit. Sed non potest istis rationibus ab officio dimoueri, qui se vitam ipsam Christo debere nouerat. Est hoc memorabile omnino exemplum, quo quid Deo debeamus admonemur, si quando ab illo nos inter media pericula iuuari & protegi sentimus. Tunc enim nullis vel praeteritis vel praesentibus aut etiam futuris periculis terreri, sed potius maiori zelo inflammari debemus, vt Dei gloriam fortius afferendo illi dignam gratiam rependamus. Inepta ergo est & peruersa plane carnalis prudentia ratio, quà hodie plerique secuti, nobis propter hostes & undique imminentia pericula silendum esse existimant. Quasi vero in hostium arbitrio situm sit, euangelij cursum impedire aut promouere. Quin eo fortius nos Dei causam agere conuenit, quando illius fidem & potentiâ inter media pericula luculenter omnino experimur. Caeterum quoad Pauli doctrinam, tria Lucas dicit, quae minime a nobis praeteriri debent. Primum est, quid praedicarit. Nimirum regnum Dei, de quo non semel antea dictum est.
units.tr: Furthermore, let us see what Paul did during this period of two years. "He welcomed," it says, "all who came to him, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus with all confidence, no one forbidding him." He therefore did in chains what he had done before when he was free and at liberty, because he understood that he was no less than before an apostle and servant of Jesus Christ. Yet he not only taught, but also by letters written and sent here and there he both founded and comforted the churches. So much so that if you look at our own times, we will confess that more profit and advantage has come to us from Paul's chains than from his words and deeds when he wandered the world freely. For we owe to those chains those splendid epistles, written under the inspiration of the Spirit, to the Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Hebrews, Philemon, and the other to Timothy, which the Church has guarded to this day like the most precious jewels. Yet many things could have deterred Paul from either writing or teaching. He had been cast into chains on account of this very teaching. He was also the only one who was labouring at Rome in this cause. At his first meeting he had found the Jews to be like themselves, that is, stubborn and resistant. Besides, that tireless zeal for writing to outsiders seemed to show some lack of peace of mind. Nor was he far from the crime of sedition in instructing and confirming men in that faith and religion which had already been condemned by a public decree of the Senate, as we have said elsewhere. Moreover there was a danger that this liberty might at last be taken from him, by being bound with tighter chains and thrust into some prison. Nor shall we suppose he was so dull that he could not see and consider these things. But he who knew that he owed his very life to Christ could not be turned from his duty by such reasons. This is a truly memorable example, by which we are admonished what we owe to God, if at any time we feel that we are helped and protected by him in the midst of dangers. For then we ought not to be frightened by any dangers, past, present, or even future, but rather to be inflamed with greater zeal, so as to repay God the thanks worthy of him by bearing witness to his glory more boldly. Therefore that foolish and plainly perverse fleshly prudence is wrong, which many today follow, and think that we must keep silent on account of enemies and the dangers hanging over us on every side. As if it lay in the power of enemies to hinder or advance the course of the gospel! Indeed we ought all the more to act for the cause of God, since we experience his faithfulness and power clearly enough amid the midst of dangers. But as for Paul's teaching, Luke mentions three things which must by no means be passed over by us. The first is what he preached: namely the kingdom of God, of which mention has been made more than once before.

units.la: Hic vero per expositionem additur: Docens ea, quae sunt de domino Iesu. Vnde colligimus tum demum praedicari regnum dei, quando Christus praedicatur. Nec enim alia ad illud perueniendi via est, quàm quae in Christo Iesu vnanimi totius scripturae consensu monstratur. Vnus enim ille est, qui diaboli regnum & illius opera destruxit. Vnus ille inter Deum & nos mediator est. 1. Tim. 2. Vnus ille deleto, quod aduersus nos erat, peccati chirographo, patrem nobis placauit. Colos. 2. Matth. 3. & 17. Non temere ergo clamat: Nemo venit ad patrem nisi per me, &c. Iohan. 14. Quae sola omnibus aliis religionibus arguendis sufficiunt, quibus extra Christum Dei regnum aut salutis ratio monstratur. Secundo, quomodo praedicarit Paulus indicatur. Cum omni fiducia. Id est, liberè & ingenuè, sic vt in homine minum gratiam nihil vel simulauerit vel dissimulauerit. Nec enim illum euangelij Iesu Christi puduit, vt alibi testatur, nec mundi & principis huius tyrannidem timuit, qui iam longo & diuturno vsu cum illa luctari didicerat. Et sane eiusmodi ministros Christus requirit, qui ingenuè illius negotium agant, nec aliquid vel mundo vel carnis sapientiae tribuant, quae sub plausibili modestiae praetextu ignauam veritatis dissimulationem & verae fidei abnegationem introducit. Tertio successus quoq; notatur, quo inter praedicandum Paulus vsus est. Quem felicissimum fuisse, vno hoc argumento abunde patet, quòd nemo fuit qui docentem prohiberet. Id vero inter omnia, quae in Paulo Deus edidit,
units.tr: Here, moreover, the explanation is added: "teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus." From this we gather that the kingdom of God is then preached when Christ is preached. For there is no other way of attaining to it than that which is shown in Christ Jesus, by the unanimous consent of the whole of Scripture. For he alone is the one who destroyed the kingdom of the devil and his works. He alone is the one mediator between God and us. 1 Timothy 2. He alone, having blotted out the handwriting of sin that was against us, reconciled the Father to us. Colossians 2; Matthew 3 and 17. Not without reason, therefore, he cries out: "No one comes to the Father except through me," etc. John 14. These alone are sufficient for refuting all other religions, which show a way of salvation or a kingdom of God apart from Christ. Second, how Paul preached is indicated: "with all confidence." That is, freely and openly, so that he neither pretended nor concealed anything in order to win human favour. For he was not ashamed of the gospel of Jesus Christ, as he testifies elsewhere, nor did he fear the tyranny of this world and its prince, having learned by long and continued practice to wrestle with it. And indeed Christ requires ministers of this kind, who carry out his business openly, and attribute nothing to the wisdom of the world or of the flesh, which under the plausible pretext of modesty introduces the cowardly dissembling of the truth and the denial of true faith. Third, the success is also noted with which Paul preached. That it was most happy is abundantly clear from this one argument, that there was no one who forbade him while he taught. Indeed, of all the things which God displayed in Paul,

units.la: 2. Paulus ingenuè praedicat.
units.tr: 2. Paul preaches openly.

units.la: 3. Pauli successus. edidit, miracula, mihi omnium maximum esse videtur. Hactenus enim quocunque terrarum venit, illico hostes reperit, qui vel occultis insidijs vel etiam aperta vi & seditionibus illi negotium facerent, & docere volentem impedirent, tandemque urbibus eijcerent. At ubi Romam captivus ducitur, & illic ex vinculis docet, ubi Nero, prodigium hominis, imperabat, ubi & Christiana & Iudaicae ligioinuisa & exosa habebatur, ubi vel inani deorum superstitione vel Epicuraeo omnis religionis contemptu omnes dementati erant, ubi deniq; regni sui sedem primariam diabolus tenere videbatur, toto biennio libere & nemine prohibente Christum praedicat. Cuius rei non aliam causam afferre possumus, quàm quod Deus potenti manu omnium animos frenare voluit, ut licet non omnes evangelij doctrinae cederent, illam tamen oppugnare non auderent. Ita vero in urbe rerum domina per Christi crucifixi praedicationem apostolus captivus triumphat, multo plures sub Christi obedientiam trahens, quam vllus Imperatorum olim subiugauerit. Simile quid olim accidisse legimus, quando in Babylonem captivus abductus Daniel, veram religionem constanter simul & feliciter asserit, & quantumuis reluctantibus regni proceribus, primo quidem Nabuchodonosorem, deinde vero Darium quoq; aliqua veri Dei cognitione illustrat, ijsq; author est, ut illius cultum & gloriam publicis editis per omnes regni sui terminos longe lateq; propagent. Quo & illud referri meretur, quòd Romanis Imperatoribus incredibili immanitate contra Christi nomen & ecclesiam grassanti-bus, tamen in eorundem aulis, adeoq; inter summos proceres inuenti sint non raro, qui & Christianis egregie fauerent, & religioni verae palàm patrocinarentur: quorum aliqui postea sublatis Christi hostibus in summum imperij fastigium euecti sunt, ut in Iouiniani & Valentiniani Impp. rebus gestis esse videre. Ita ubi minimè sperss potentiam suam Christus exerit, nec illi difficile est hominum voluntates frenare, qui insano mari limitem constituit, ad quem fluctus suos tumentes deponat. Iob 38. Ierem. 5. Huius ergo praesens auxilium sperent, quicunq; in illo fortes sunt, nec vnquam spe sua fallentur.
units.tr: 3. Paul's success. This seems to me the greatest of all the miracles God performed in Paul. Wherever he came in the world, he at once met enemies who, by secret plots or even open force and riots, tried to stop him from carrying on his work and from teaching, and in the end drove him out of the cities. But when he was led to Rome as a prisoner, and there taught from his chains, while Nero, a monster of a man, was emperor, where both the Christian and the Jewish religion were hated and detested, where everyone had been driven mad either by empty superstition about the gods or by Epicurean contempt for all religion, and where the devil seemed to hold the chief seat of his kingdom, he preached Christ freely for two whole years, and no one stopped him. We can give no other cause for this than that God, with a mighty hand, restrained the minds of all men, so that, although not all yielded to the teaching of the gospel, they did not dare to oppose it. Thus the apostle, a prisoner, triumphed in the city that ruled the world, by preaching Christ crucified, and brought many more men under the obedience of Christ than any emperor had ever subjugated. We read that something similar once happened when Daniel, led away captive to Babylon, steadfastly and successfully affirmed the true religion, and, though the nobles of the kingdom resisted, first enlightened Nebuchadnezzar and then Darius too with some knowledge of the true God, and advised them to spread his worship and glory far and wide throughout all the borders of their kingdom by public edicts. To this may also be added that, although the Roman emperors raged against the name of Christ and the Church with incredible savagery, yet in their courts, and even among the highest nobles, there were not infrequently found men who showed great favour to Christians and openly defended the true religion. Some of these, after the enemies of Christ had been removed, were raised to the highest rank of the empire, as we see in the deeds of the emperors Jovian and Valentinian. Thus, when Christ displays his power where we least expect it, it is not hard for him to restrain the wills of men, he who set a boundary to the raging sea, beyond which it must lay down its swelling waves. Job 38; Jer. 5. Therefore let those who are strong in him hope for his present help, and they will never be disappointed in their hope.

units.la: Quid autem euoluto biennij tempore Paulus egerit, Lucas non commemorat, hic nimirum ex spiritus sancti suggestione historiam suam finiens, qui ecclesiam pluribus scriptis & nimia librorum mole grauari noluit, sed ea duntaxat tradidit quae ad fidei & vitae institutionem sufficiunt. Attamen ex ipsius Pauli epistolis coniectura aliquot colligi possunt, quibus quid postea fecerit, docetur. Nam se causam coram Caesare dixisse, & Dei beneficio liberatum fuisse, cum se iam immolandum putaret, in posteriori ad Timoth. 4. diserte testatur. Ad Philippen. vero scribens, inter alia inquit: Timotheum spero me missurum ad vos, mox vbi videro mea negotia. Confido autem in domino, quòd & ipse breui venturus sim. Phil. 2. Et Philemoni Colossensi scribit: Simul etiam praepara mihi hospitium. Spero enim, quòd auxilio precum vestrarum donabor vobis. Rursum ad Hebraeos cap. 13. ait: Orate pro nobis, & magis quidem vt hoc faciatis oro, quo celerius restituar vobis. Sciatis fratrem vestrum Timotheum solutum esse: cum quo (si celerius venerit) visam vos. Interim priusquam Romam captivus duceretur, illi Hispanias adire animus fuit, quemadmodum epistola ad Roman. cap. 15. testatur. Ex quibus no omnino praeter causam nonnulli colligunt, illum vinculis solutum per Graeciam & Asiam minorem in Syriam redijsse, & salutatis Orientalibus ecclesijs, per Italiam & Gallias in Hispaniam vsq; contendisse. Ita vero iuxta horum sententiam annis fere decem, postquam dimissus fuit, euangelium praedicauit, tandem vltimo Neronis anno Romam retractus, & capite truncatus, martyrij coronam recepit, cum annis continuis triginta septem Christum maximae orbis parti praedicasset. At quia in his minimè consistit salutis ratio, cum nemine pertinacius contendere velim. Nec mihi de religione & fide Christiana multum mereri videntur, qui in ijs inuestigandis laborant, quae sacrae literae silentio praeterire voluerunt. Ita enim & hae negligentius tractantur, & superstitiosis occasio datur, ut circa incerta & inutilia occupati, apostolorum doctrinam negligant, & fabulis dementati circa fidem quoq; & salutis rationem grauiter impingant. Et sane vt olim Mosis sepulchrum Deus latere voluit, & de prophetarum martyrijs pauca in veteri Testamento spiritus sanctus memoriae prodidit: ita in praesenti quoque opere Lucas duorum tantummodo exitum, Stephani nimirum & Iacobi apostoli, descripsit, de reliquis hoc dixisse contentus, quòd per omnis generis aduersa Christum constantissimè praedicarint & confessi sint: ita nimirum doctrinae apostolicae studium nobis commendare volens, quod apostolorum imitatores simul & eorundem consortes in ca-
units.tr: But what Paul did during the course of those two years Luke does not record. Doubtless, under the prompting of the Holy Spirit, he ends his history here; the Spirit did not wish the Church to be burdened with many writings and a great mass of books, but handed down only those things that suffice for the instruction of faith and life. Nevertheless, from Paul's own letters some things can be gathered by conjecture, which teach what he did afterwards. For in his second letter to Timothy, chapter 4, he clearly testifies that he had pleaded his cause before Caesar and had been delivered by God's kindness, when he thought he was already about to be sacrificed. Writing to the Philippians, he says among other things: "I hope to send Timothy to you soon, as soon as I see how my affairs stand. And I trust in the Lord that I myself shall come shortly" (Phil. 2). And he writes to Philemon of Colossae: "At the same time prepare a lodging for me, for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you." Again, in Hebrews chapter 13 he says: "Pray for us, and I urge you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you the sooner. Know that our brother Timothy has been set free, and if he comes soon, I shall see you with him." Meanwhile, before he was led to Rome as a prisoner, he had a desire to visit Spain, as the letter to the Romans, chapter 15, bears witness. From these passages some, not without reason, gather that, released from his chains, he went through Greece and Asia Minor back to Syria, and after greeting the churches of the East, pressed on through Italy and Gaul to Spain. According to their opinion, then, he preached the gospel for about ten years after he was released, and at last, in the final year of Nero, was brought back to Rome and beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom, after he had preached Christ to the greatest part of the world for thirty-seven continuous years. But since the way of salvation does not consist in these things at all, I would not wish to contend stubbornly with anyone about them. Nor do those seem to me to deserve well of the Christian religion and faith who labour to investigate matters that Holy Scripture chose to pass over in silence. For in this way both Scripture itself is handled too carelessly, and superstitious people are given occasion, busied with uncertain and useless matters, to neglect the teaching of the apostles, and, driven mad by fables, to stumble badly over faith too and the way of salvation. And indeed, just as God wished the tomb of Moses to be hidden, and the Holy Spirit in the Old Testament handed down only a few things about the martyrdoms of the prophets to memory, so in the present work Luke has described the deaths of only two men, namely Stephen and the apostle James, being content to say of the rest only that they preached Christ and confessed him most steadfastly amid adversity of every kind. Thus he wished to commend to us the zeal for apostolic teaching, so that we might be imitators of the apostles and at the same time their companions in the heavenly inheritance of the fatherland.

units.la: Quid euoluto biennio factum. lestis patriæ hæreditate facere consueuit. Quare in præsenti quoq; ardens illud & indefessum Pauli studium in Christi gloria propaganda cumprimis obseruandum simul & imitandum erit. Nec est, quòd eiusdem exitu offendamur. Ita enim Christus suos cultores sibi in hoc seculo conformes reddit, vt eosdem cœlestis suæ gloriæ & regni olim consortes habeat.
units.tr: What was done after the two years. Therefore, in the present case too, that burning and tireless zeal of Paul for spreading the glory of Christ must above all be observed and imitated. Nor should we be offended by his end. For Christ makes his worshippers conformed to himself in this world, so that he may have them as companions of his heavenly glory and kingdom in time to come.

units.la: HACTENVS verò librum hunc pro gratia nobis concessa exposuimus. Vidimus in eo veteris ecclesiæ formam, fidem atq; doctrinam, quæ nobis etiam hodie retinenda erit, siquidem Christi ecclesia censeri volumus. Nec enim eos audire conuenit, qui multa ad religionem & salutis rationem necessariò requiri clamant, quibus primitiua illa Ecclesia caruerit. Quorum num temeritatem siue impudentiam magis admireris, nescio. Ita enim & apostolos vel negligentiæ vel perfidiæ accusant, & ijsdem præferre non verentur, quorum exemplum omnibus ijs imitandum spiritus sanctus proposuit, quicunq; ecclesiæ Christi membra fieri, & salutem in ipso consequi volunt. Quis verò illos, qui totis viginti octo annis in fide & religione ab apostolis tradita perseuerarunt, aliquibus caruisse putet, sine quibus salus obtineri non possit? Quòd si verò illi sine ijs, quæ postea audaculi quidam et superstitiosi introduxerunt, saluati sunt, quis nobis illorum vestigia sectantibus salutem negare audeat? Nemo opinor, nisi quis Manichæorum furoribus agitatus totum hunc librum falsi accusare velit. Vidimus quoq; ecclesiæ in hoc mundo conditionem, quæ indesinentibus aduersis vexatur, dum illi & aperti hostes & falsi fratres negotium faciunt. Vidimus indignam ministrorum Christi sortem, & quàm malam gratiam illis mundus referat. Simul verò potentem Christi Iesu manum vidimus, qua ecclesiam suam inter medios persecutionum fluctus fideliter tuetur, & per suorum crucem de mundo hoc & illius principe gloriosissimè triumphat. His ergo ad fidei nostræ institutionem & confirmationem sedulò vtamur, vt iuxta apostolorum & veteris ecclesiæ exemplum in fide fortes, & omnibus periculis superiores factì, destinatam nobis ab æterno cœlestis regni hæreditatem adire possimus cum Christo Iesu, Rege & Sacerdote nostro: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: So far we have expounded this book, as the grace given to us allows. In it we have seen the form, faith and teaching of the early Church, which must be kept by us even today, if we wish to be counted as the Church of Christ. For we should not listen to those who cry out that many things are necessarily required for religion and the way of salvation, things which that primitive Church lacked. I do not know whether to admire more the rashness or the shamelessness of such people. For they accuse the apostles of negligence or treachery, and do not hesitate to prefer themselves to them, though the Holy Spirit has set the apostles before all who wish to become members of the Church of Christ and to obtain salvation in him as an example to imitate. Who would think that those who persevered for the full twenty-eight years in the faith and religion handed down by the apostles lacked things without which salvation cannot be obtained? But if those men were saved without the things that some bold and superstitious people introduced later, who would dare to deny salvation to us, if we follow their footsteps? No one, I think, except someone driven by the frenzy of the Manichaeans who would wish to accuse this whole book of falsehood. We have also seen the condition of the Church in this world, which is harassed by unceasing adversities, while both open enemies and false brothers make trouble for it. We have seen the unworthy lot of the ministers of Christ, and how wretched the thanks the world gives them. At the same time we have seen the mighty hand of Jesus Christ, by which he faithfully protects his Church amid the waves of persecution, and through the cross of his people triumphs gloriously over this world and its prince. Let us therefore use these things diligently for the instruction and confirmation of our faith, so that, following the example of the apostles and of the early Church, strong in faith and superior to all dangers, we may come to the kingdom of heaven, the inheritance destined for us from eternity, with Jesus Christ, our King and Priest, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: DIVI HIERONYMI DE Actis Apostolorum iudicium.
units.tr: Saint Jerome's judgment on the Acts of the Apostles.

units.la: Actus Apostolorum nudam quidem videntur sonare historiam, & nascentis Ecclesiae infantiam texere: sed sinouerimus scriptorem eorum Lucam esse medicum, cuius laus est in euangelio, animaduertemus pariter, omnia verba illius, animae languentis esse medicinam.
units.tr: The Acts of the Apostles may seem to sound like a bare history and to weave the infancy of the newborn Church; but if we recall that its writer Luke was a physician, whose praise is in the Gospel, we shall likewise notice that all his words are a medicine for a languishing soul.
